## Mutant spike result — `severity.py`

Ran mutmut on the severity/threshold-banding module (pure logic, the ADR-0005/0016 tier derivation):

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Mutants generated | **32** |
| Killed | **31** |
| Survived | **1** |
| Real coverage gaps | **0** |

The lone survivor (#201, line 41) is an **equivalent mutant**: mutmut flipped the *type annotation* `dict[str, Any] | None` → `dict[str, Any] & None`. Annotations aren't evaluated at runtime here, so behavior is identical — no test can kill it by construction. So the test suite kills **100% of behavioral mutants** on this module, including all the boundary-sensitive ones (`>=`→`>`, threshold ordering, the `no_thresholds`/`metric_value is None` short-circuit, the NaN/inf finite guard). Solid — no follow-up needed on the tests themselves.

**One tooling snag worth flagging:** mutmut 2.5.0's `mutmut results` / `mutmut show` crash on Python 3.13 (ADR 0017) — its pony-ORM decompiler hits `IndexError` on 3.13 bytecode. The `run` itself works (it just shells out to pytest); only the *reporting* is broken. I worked around it by querying mutmut's SQLite cache (`.mutmut-cache`) directly. The [CONTRIBUTING rule 4a](CONTRIBUTING.md#L18) command flow assumes `mutmut results` works, so that's stale on 3.13.

## Frontend equivalent — yes: Stryker Mutator

mutmut's JS/TS analog is **[Stryker Mutator](https://stryker-mutator.io/)**. It's **not set up** in this repo. Given the stack (Vitest 4), it'd be:
- `@stryker-mutator/core` + `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` (dev deps), a `stryker.conf.json`, and — like mutmut — **manual/periodic, never CI** (it's slow), kept off the `pnpm audit` gate the same way `requirements-mutation.txt` is kept off `pip-audit`.

Good first targets (pure logic with existing tests, same "covered-but-unasserted" risk profile): [suiteTarget.ts](frontend/src/components/suites/suiteTarget.ts) (`suiteTarget.test.ts`), [checkForm.ts](frontend/src/components/checks/checkForm.ts), `expectationCatalog.ts`, `resultsFormat.ts`.

3. **Extend the backend spike** to another pure module (e.g. `run_target.py`) while mutmut's installed.

So the documented [CONTRIBUTING rule 4a](../blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) flow (`mutmut run … && mutmut results`) is half-broken: you can run a spike but can't read the survivors via the normal command.\n\n## Impact\n\nLow / tooling only — mutation testing is a manual, periodic spike (never CI), so this never blocks a merge. But anyone following rule 4a on 3.13 hits a wall reading results.\n\n## Workaround (in use)\n\n`mutmut run` populates a SQLite cache at `.mutmut-cache`. Query survivors directly instead of `mutmut results`:\n\n```python\nimport sqlite3\nc = sqlite3.connect(\".mutmut-cache\")\nq = '''select s.filename, l.line_number, l.line, m.status\n       from Mutant m join Line l on m.line=l.id join SourceFile s on l.sourcefile=s.id\n       where m.status != \"killed\" order by s.filename, l.line_number'''\nfor fn, ln, src, st in c.execute(q):\n    print(f\"{fn}:{ln} [{st}] {src.strip()}\")\n```\n\n(`mutmut apply <id>` to materialize a survivor on disk for inspection still works — it doesn't go through the decompiler.)\n\n## Options\n\n1. **Bump mutmut** to a 3.x line (3.x dropped pony for a different storage/reporting backend) and re-validate the rule-4a flow on 3.13. The CLI/flags changed between 2.x and 3.x, so rule 4a's command would need updating too.\n2. Keep 2.5.0 and **document the SQLite-cache query** in CONTRIBUTING rule 4a as the 3.13 way to read results (cheap; done as a first pass alongside this issue).\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- [ ] CONTRIBUTING rule 4a reflects a working \"read the survivors\" step on Python 3.13\n- [ ] (if opt 1) `requirements-mutation.txt` bumped + the rule-4a command line updated to the new mutmut CLI\n\nFound during a periodic mutmut spike on `backend/app/services/severity.py` (32 mutants, 31 killed, 1 equivalent annotation mutant — clean).\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",
```json
  "description": "File mutmut-on-3.13 tooling issue"
}
```

```
1	import type { ConnectionType } from '../../api/connections';
2	import type { RunTarget } from '../../api/suites';
3	
4	/**
5	 * A suite's run target (#215) is datasource-shaped: SQL warehouses identify a
6	 * `table` (+ optional `schema`), Unity Catalog adds a required `catalog`, and
7	 * flat-file stores (ADLS / S3) identify a `path` (+ optional `file_format`).
8	 * `targetKind` collapses the six datasource types to the three input shapes the
9	 * editor renders; orchestration types never reach here (they can't back a suite).
10	 */
11	export type TargetKind = 'sql' | 'uc' | 'flatfile';
12	
13	export function targetKind(type: ConnectionType): TargetKind | null {
14	  switch (type) {
15	    case 'snowflake':
16	      return 'sql';
17	    case 'unity_catalog':
18	      return 'uc';
19	    case 'adls_gen2':
20	    case 's3':
21	      return 'flatfile';
22	    default:
23	      return null; // adf / airflow — not a datasource
24	  }
25	}
26	
27	/** The raw target inputs the drawer collects (all optional strings). */
28	export interface TargetFormValues {
29	  target_table?: string;
30	  target_schema?: string;
31	  target_catalog?: string;
32	  target_path?: string;
33	  target_format?: 'csv' | 'parquet';
34	}
35	
36	/** Narrow an untyped stored `file_format` to the supported set, else `undefined`
37	 *  — the suite target is an untyped JSONB bag, so a stray value (e.g. `json`)
38	 *  must not prefill the Select with an option that doesn't exist. */
39	export function asFileFormat(value: string | undefined): 'csv' | 'parquet' | undefined {
40	  return value === 'csv' || value === 'parquet' ? value : undefined;
41	}
42	
43	export interface AssembledTarget {
44	  /** The target to send: `null` = leave targetless (no field was filled). */
45	  target: RunTarget | null;
46	  /** Set when the section was started but a required field is missing. */
47	  error?: { field: keyof TargetFormValues; message: string };
48	}
49	
50	const trimmed = (v?: string): string | undefined => {
51	  const t = v?.trim();
52	  return t ? t : undefined;
53	};
54	
55	/**
56	 * Turn the raw inputs into a `RunTarget` for the connection's datasource, mirroring
57	 * the backend `run_target.resolve_target` rules so a saved target is always
58	 * runnable. All-blank → `null` (a valid targetless suite). Partially filled but
59	 * missing the datasource's required field → an `error` naming that field, so the
60	 * UI flags it inline rather than letting the backend 422 on save.
61	 */
62	export function assembleTarget(kind: TargetKind, v: TargetFormValues): AssembledTarget {
63	  if (kind === 'flatfile') {
64	    const path = trimmed(v.target_path);
65	    if (!path && !v.target_format) return { target: null };
66	    if (!path) {
67	      return {
68	        target: null,
69	        error: { field: 'target_path', message: 'Path is required to run this suite.' },
70	      };
71	    }
72	    return { target: { path, ...(v.target_format ? { file_format: v.target_format } : {}) } };
73	  }
74	
75	  if (kind === 'sql') {
76	    const table = trimmed(v.target_table);
77	    const schema = trimmed(v.target_schema);
78	    if (!table && !schema) return { target: null };
79	    if (!table) {
80	      return {
81	        target: null,
82	        error: { field: 'target_table', message: 'Table is required to run this suite.' },
83	      };
84	    }
85	    return { target: { table, ...(schema ? { schema } : {}) } };
86	  }
87	
88	  // Unity Catalog: catalog + table required, schema optional.
89	  const catalog = trimmed(v.target_catalog);
90	  const table = trimmed(v.target_table);
91	  const schema = trimmed(v.target_schema);
92	  if (!catalog && !table && !schema) return { target: null };
93	  if (!catalog) {
94	    return {
95	      target: null,
96	      error: { field: 'target_catalog', message: 'Catalog is required to run this suite.' },
97	    };
98	  }
99	  if (!table) {
100	    return {
101	      target: null,
102	      error: { field: 'target_table', message: 'Table is required to run this suite.' },
103	    };
104	  }
105	  return { target: { catalog, table, ...(schema ? { schema } : {}) } };
106	}
107
```

> AGENT

Classic pnpm strict-isolation issue — Stryker dynamically imports `typescript` (an undeclared dep), which pnpm's non-hoisted dlx layout won't resolve. Forcing a hoisted (flat, npm-style) linker for the dlx env should fix it:

> TOOL

tool_use Bash
id: toolu_015Uo1NUcdDKrvHqjujxjALX
```json
{
  "command": "npm_config_node_linker=hoisted pnpm dlx --package @stryker-mutator/core@9.6.1 --package @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner@9.6.1 --package typescript@6.0.3 stryker run 2>&1 | grep -vE '^\\s+at |node:internal|ERR_MODULE' | tail -45",
  "description": "Run Stryker with hoisted node-linker"
}
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/mutation/run.sh",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Frontend mutation spike (Stryker) — manual / periodic, NOT CI.\n#\n# Mirrors the backend mutmut spike (CONTRIBUTING.md rule 4a): a hostile pass over\n# a pure module to find covered-but-unasserted logic. Stryker + its vitest runner\n# are deliberately NOT in frontend/package.json, so they stay off the `pnpm audit`\n# merge gate (the backend keeps mutmut off `pip-audit` the same way via a\n# standalone requirements-mutation.txt). This script installs them ad-hoc, runs\n# Stryker from the project root (Stryker sandboxes the cwd, so it must run there),\n# and restores the manifest on exit — even if Stryker fails — so the mutation deps\n# never land in the committed package.json / lockfile.\n#\n# Usage (from anywhere):\n#   frontend/mutation/run.sh                         # mutate the configured target\n#   frontend/mutation/run.sh --mutate 'src/components/checks/checkForm.ts'\n# Pin lives here so spikes are reproducible:\nSTRYKER_VERSION=9.6.1\n\nset -euo pipefail\ncd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\"   # -> frontend/ (Stryker must run from the project root)\n\n# Refuse to run with a dirty manifest — the EXIT trap restores it via `git\n# checkout`, which would clobber any unrelated staged/working changes to it.\nif ! git diff --quiet -- package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ||\n   ! git diff --cached --quiet -- package.json pnpm-lock.yaml; then\n  echo \"✗ package.json / pnpm-lock.yaml have uncommitted changes — commit or stash them first\" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\n\n# Restore the manifest no matter how Stryker exits (keeps the spike deps uncommitted).\ntrap 'git checkout -- package.json pnpm-lock.yaml 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT\n\n# typescript is already a project dep; Stryker resolves it from node_modules.\n# Explicit plugin name in stryker.conf.json — pnpm's strict layout defeats the\n# default \"@stryker-mutator/*\" glob plugin discovery.\npnpm add -D \"@stryker-mutator/core@${STRYKER_VERSION}\" \\\n            \"@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner@${STRYKER_VERSION}\"\n\npnpm exec stryker run \"$@\"\n"
}
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/mutation/README.md",
  "content": "# Frontend mutation testing (Stryker)\n\nThe frontend analogue of the backend mutmut spike ([CONTRIBUTING rule 4a](../../CONTRIBUTING.md)).\n**Manual / periodic, never CI** — mutation testing is too slow to gate merges, and\nits big tool tree shouldn't sit on the `pnpm audit` surface. So, like the backend's\nstandalone `requirements-mutation.txt`, **Stryker is not a dependency in\n`frontend/package.json`** — [`run.sh`](./run.sh) installs it ad-hoc (pinned) and\nrestores the manifest on exit.\n\n## Run a spike\n\n```bash\nfrontend/mutation/run.sh                                  # mutate the configured target\nfrontend/mutation/run.sh --mutate 'src/components/checks/checkForm.ts'\n```\n\nConfig lives in [`../stryker.conf.json`](../stryker.conf.json); the version pin is in\n`run.sh`. The default `mutate` target is `suiteTarget.ts` — point it at whatever pure\nmodule you're hardening (the conversion/resolver utils are the best targets:\n`suiteTarget.ts`, `checkForm.ts`, `expectationCatalog.ts`, `resultsFormat.ts`).\n\n## Reading the result\n\nStryker prints a `[Survived]` block per mutant the tests failed to kill, plus a\nmutation-score table. Triage each survivor:\n\n- **Real gap** — a behavioural mutation (flipped condition, dropped branch, changed\n  return) that no test caught. Add/strengthen a test. This is the point of the spike.\n- **Equivalent mutant** — a change with no observable effect (e.g. mutating a value\n  that's re-narrowed downstream, or an unreachable branch). Not a gap; leave it.\n- **Low-value** — e.g. an error-`message` string mutated to `\"\"`. Pin it only if the\n  copy is contractual; asserting exact UI strings is usually brittle.\n\nA score < 100% is fine — chase the *real* gaps, not the number.\n\n## Gotchas (Node ≥ 20, pnpm v11)\n\n- Stryker must run from `frontend/` — it sandboxes the cwd, so a separate manifest\n  dir can't host it. `run.sh` cd's there for you.\n- `stryker.conf.json` sets `plugins: [\"@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner\"]` explicitly;\n  pnpm's strict `node_modules` layout defeats Stryker's default `@stryker-mutator/*`\n  plugin-discovery glob.\n- `pnpm dlx` is unreliable here (its isolated store can't resolve Stryker's dynamic\n  `typescript` import), which is why `run.sh` does a real install + revert instead.\n"
}
```

| Cluster | Survivors | Verdict |

| **`asFileFormat()` entirely** (lines 39–40) | 10 | **Real gap** — no direct test. The whole body can be emptied / both `=== 'csv'`/`=== 'parquet'` flipped and tests still pass. It's the JSONB-narrowing guard that stops a stray stored `file_format` prefilling the Select — worth a focused test. |

| **Error `message` strings → `""`** (lines 69, 96, 102) | 3 | **Low-value** — tests assert the error `field` but not the copy. Pinning exact UI strings is brittle; I'd leave these. |

## Harness notes
- Stryker kept **out of `package.json`** → off the `pnpm audit` gate; `frontend/mutation/run.sh` installs it pinned, runs from the project root, and **restores the manifest on exit** (guards against a dirty manifest first). - `pnpm dlx` proved unreliable on Node 26 / pnpm v11 (can't resolve Stryker's dynamic `typescript`/plugin imports), hence the install-and-revert approach; documented in the README.

```
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import type { ConnectionType } from '../../src/api/connections';
import { assembleTarget, targetKind } from '../../src/components/suites/suiteTarget';

describe('targetKind', () => {
  it('maps each datasource type to its input shape; orchestration → null', () => {
    const cases: [ConnectionType, ReturnType<typeof targetKind>][] = [
      ['snowflake', 'sql'],
      ['unity_catalog', 'uc'],
      ['adls_gen2', 'flatfile'],
      ['s3', 'flatfile'],
      ['adf', null],
      ['airflow', null],
    ];
    for (const [type, kind] of cases) expect(targetKind(type)).toBe(kind);
  });
});

describe('assembleTarget', () => {
  it('returns a null target when nothing is filled (valid targetless suite)', () => {
    expect(assembleTarget('sql', {}).target).toBeNull();
    expect(assembleTarget('uc', {}).target).toBeNull();
    expect(assembleTarget('flatfile', {}).target).toBeNull();
  });

  it('builds a SQL target, omitting an empty schema', () => {
    expect(assembleTarget('sql', { target_table: 'ANALYTICS.ORDERS' }).target).toEqual({
      table: 'ANALYTICS.ORDERS',
    });
    expect(
      assembleTarget('sql', { target_table: 'ORDERS', target_schema: 'PUBLIC' }).target,
    ).toEqual({ table: 'ORDERS', schema: 'PUBLIC' });
  });

  it('flags a SQL section started without the required table', () => {
    const { target, error } = assembleTarget('sql', { target_schema: 'PUBLIC' });
    expect(target).toBeNull();
    expect(error?.field).toBe('target_table');
  });

  it('builds a flat-file target with optional format', () => {
    expect(assembleTarget('flatfile', { target_path: 'c/data.csv' }).target).toEqual({
      path: 'c/data.csv',
    });
    expect(
      assembleTarget('flatfile', { target_path: 'c/d.parquet', target_format: 'parquet' }).target,
    ).toEqual({ path: 'c/d.parquet', file_format: 'parquet' });
  });

  it('flags a flat-file section started (format only) without a path', () => {
    const { target, error } = assembleTarget('flatfile', { target_format: 'csv' });
    expect(target).toBeNull();
    expect(error?.field).toBe('target_path');
  });

  it('builds a Unity Catalog target requiring catalog + table', () => {
    expect(
      assembleTarget('uc', {
        target_catalog: 'main',
        target_schema: 'default',
        target_table: 'orders',
      }).target,
    ).toEqual({ catalog: 'main', table: 'orders', schema: 'default' });
  });

  it('flags a UC section missing catalog, then table', () => {
    expect(assembleTarget('uc', { target_table: 'orders' }).error?.field).toBe('target_catalog');
    expect(assembleTarget('uc', { target_catalog: 'main' }).error?.field).toBe('target_table');
  });

  it('trims whitespace and treats blank-only input as absent', () => {
    expect(assembleTarget('sql', { target_table: '  ORDERS  ' }).target).toEqual({
      table: 'ORDERS',
    });
    expect(assembleTarget('sql', { target_table: '   ' }).target).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

```
=== ADR 0012 head ===
# ADR 0012 — Monitor-kind seam (`check.kind` discriminator + numeric metric storage)

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-05-30
- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771

## Context

Every v1 check is a Great Expectations expectation (ADR 0003): a value-level
assertion on column/table data. But most real data-quality incidents are **not**
value-level — they are **freshness** (a table stopped loading) and **volume** (a
load delivered 10% of its usual rows). These are *monitors over a measured
scalar*, not expectations over row values. The post-v1 roadmap (Theme A) makes
this the leap from "a GX runner" to "a DQ platform": freshness, volume,
schema-drift, and anomaly auto-monitors.

v1 will **not** build those monitors. But the v1 check/result schema is written
in the Week-3 migration, and that migration is a **one-shot** for schema seams
(CLAUDE.md §10) — once results are written, changing the shape is a
backward-compatible two-step deploy (W5+ discipline). If v1 ships a schema that
assumes "a check is always a GX expectation, a result is always binary + a JSONB
`observed_value`," then every auto-monitor in v1.x forces a check/result schema
rewrite that ripples into the suite, check, run, and result layers.

Two specific gaps:

1. **No discriminator on `checks`.** The run path hardwires "expectation → GX."
   A freshness monitor has no expectation_type; it has an interval and a
   timestamp column. Without a `kind`, there's nowhere to branch on *what kind of
   monitor this is* (a question orthogonal to *which datasource* — that's the
   `CheckRunner` / `ConnectionAdapter` seam).
2. **Metrics only live in JSONB `observed_value`.** A freshness monitor measures
   "hours since last load = 26.5"; a volume monitor measures "row count =
   1,203,847." These are scalars you must `AVG()` / `STDDEV()` for Week-6 trend
   charts and v1.1 anomaly baselines. **You cannot aggregate a value buried in a
   JSONB blob in SQL** — the dashboard would have to pull every row and reduce in
   Python.

This decision must land **before the Week-3 threshold migration** so both
columns ride that single migration.
```

> AGENT

Before writing code, I hit a genuine fork that the exploration reframes — and it's worth your call because it revises a CLAUDE.md assumption and sets the security posture for running user SQL.

**What I found:**
- The Monaco SQL editor was flagged "backend-blocked: need a custom-SQL check kind." But GX Core ships `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` (takes a raw SQL query; any rows it returns = failures), and it **already rides the existing path** — `kind='expectation'`, `expectation_type='unexpected_rows_expectation'`, query in `config`. The runner maps `expectation_type`→`gxe.<Class>(**config)` generically, and check CRUD treats `expectation_type`/`config` as free-form. So a custom-SQL check would persist and run **today** with zero schema/runner changes.
- Real backend work is therefore **not** a new kind — it's **guardrails**: read-only/SQL-shape validation, gating to SQL-queryable datasources only (Snowflake + Unity Catalog; flat files aren't SQL-queryable), thresholds, and a catalog entry so the picker offers "Custom SQL."
- This is security-sensitive (arbitrary SQL on warehouses) → warrants an ADR either way.

The pivotal decision:

```
This Expectation will fail validation if the query returns one or more rows. The WHERE clause defines the fail criteria.

    UnexpectedRowsExpectations facilitate the execution of SQL or Spark-SQL queries     as the core logic for an Expectation. UnexpectedRowsExpectations must implement     a `_validate(...)` method containing logic for determining whether data returned     by the executed query is successfully validated. One is written by default, but     can be overridden.

    A successful validation is one where the unexpected_rows_query returns no rows.

    UnexpectedRowsExpectation is a     [Batch Expectation](https://docs.greatexpectations.io/docs/guides/expectations/creating_custom_expectations/how_to_create_custom_batch_expectations).

    BatchExpectations are one of the most common types of Expectation.
    They are evaluated for an entire Batch, and answer a semantic question about the Batch itself.
```

I have what I need to design this. Here's the plan — per your choice, **PR 1 leads with ADR 0019**, then a phased build. Looking for your approval before I start coding.

## Design (decided): custom-SQL = `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` under `kind='expectation'`
- A custom-SQL check persists as `expectation_type='unexpected_rows_expectation'`, `config={"unexpected_rows_query": "<SQL>"}`. **Fails if the query returns ≥1 row** (success = 0 rows); `{batch}` is GX's placeholder for the run target's table.
- The model, check CRUD, run/result/severity path, and `gx_runner` (`expectation_type → gxe.<Class>(**config)`) **already support this** — no schema migration, no new `kind`. This is what the exploration changed vs. the old "need a new kind" note.

## ADR 0019 (the first artifact) will record
- The decision + why (reuses GX + the entire run path; a distinct `kind` would duplicate it).
- **Security posture** — the load-bearing part: user SQL runs with the connection's credentials, so (1) app-layer validation: single statement, read-only (`SELECT`/`WITH` only; reject DML/DDL and `;`-chaining), (2) defense-in-depth: document that custom-SQL connections should use a least-privilege read-only role, (3) gate to **SQL-queryable datasources only** (Snowflake, Unity Catalog) — flat files (ADLS/S3) are DataFrame assets, not SQL.
- v1 semantics: **binary pass/fail** (thresholds deferred — UnexpectedRowsExpectation yields a row count, not an unexpected-%, so banding on count is a follow-up).

## Phased build (backend → frontend, per the dependency)

**PR 1 — backend (ADR + guardrails + validation)**
1. `docs/adr/0019-custom-sql-check-kind.md` + index updates (CLAUDE.md table, docs/progress.md).
2. A `custom_sql` validation module: when `expectation_type=='unexpected_rows_expectation'`, require a non-empty `unexpected_rows_query`, enforce single-statement + read-only (reject `INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/DROP/ALTER/CREATE/GRANT/…` and multiple statements), wired into `check_service.create/update` + suite-import.
3. Datasource gating: reject custom-SQL in a suite whose connection isn't SQL-queryable (resolve via the suite's connection type).
4. **De-risk the integration first**: run one `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` through `gx_runner` against the dev Postgres to confirm the outcome maps to pass/fail + `sample_failures` correctly (this is the one real unknown).
5. Tests: adversarial SQL battery (injection/DML/multi-statement/empty), datasource-gating, the GX round-trip.

**PR 2 — backend dry-run** (small): make the dry-run path run a custom-SQL check so the editor can "preview" before save.

**PR 3 — frontend (Monaco)**: a "Custom SQL" category in `expectationCatalog.ts` + a Monaco SQL field type rendered in `CheckNew`/`CheckDrawer`, client-side mirror of the read-only/empty validation, results wired through the existing surface. Tests (+ a Stryker spike on the new pure validation logic, now that the harness exists).

## Two things I'll decide in PR 1 unless you object
- **Keep `expectation_type` free-form** (today's behavior) vs. add a server allowlist. I'll keep it free-form for now (the SQL guardrail is the real control) and note an allowlist as optional later hardening.
- **Thresholds**: ship binary pass/fail; defer count-banding.

Approve this and I'll start PR 1 (ADR first, then the backend guardrails). Anything you want changed — e.g. fold dry-run into PR 1, or require the allowlist now?

```
1	"""Shared Great Expectations machinery for the datasource `CheckRunner`s.
2	
3	The GX-version-specific translation — snake_case `expectation_type` → GX class,
4	and GX `ExpectationSuiteValidationResult` → our GX-agnostic `SuiteOutcome` DTOs —
5	is identical across datasources. It lives here so every runner (Snowflake table,
6	flat-file DataFrame, Unity Catalog later) reuses one implementation and the GX v1
7	API is pinned in a single place (CLAUDE.md §5 — GX has drifted across releases).
8	
9	Each runner only differs in how it builds the GX *batch* (a Snowflake table
10	asset vs an in-memory pandas asset); once it has a `batch_definition` it calls
11	`run_expectations`, which registers the suite + validation definition and maps
12	the result. Tests exercise these pure parts with constructed GX results and a
13	canned DataFrame — no live datasource required.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from typing import Any
19	
20	import great_expectations as gx
21	import great_expectations.expectations as gxe
22	
23	from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckOutcome, CheckSpec, SuiteOutcome
24	
25	# GX result keys that describe failing rows — copied into CheckOutcome.sample_failures.
26	# These may contain real data, so they only ever reach logs via the redactor.
27	_SAMPLE_KEYS = ("partial_unexpected_list", "unexpected_count", "unexpected_percent")
28	
29	# GX injects internal bookkeeping keys into expectation_config.kwargs at run time
30	# (e.g. batch_id); strip them so expected_value persists only the check's own
31	# parameters.
32	_GX_INTERNAL_KWARGS = frozenset({"batch_id"})
33	
34	
35	class UnknownExpectationError(ValueError):
36	    """Raised when a check's expectation_type has no matching GX expectation."""
37	
38	
39	def _expectation_class_name(expectation_type: str) -> str:
40	    """snake_case GX type → PascalCase class name.
41	
42	    ``expect_column_values_to_not_be_null`` → ``ExpectColumnValuesToNotBeNull``.
43	    """
44	    return "".join(part.title() for part in expectation_type.split("_"))
45	
46	
47	def _to_gx_expectation(spec: CheckSpec) -> Any:
48	    class_name = _expectation_class_name(spec.expectation_type)
49	    expectation_cls = getattr(gxe, class_name, None)
50	    if expectation_cls is None:
51	        raise UnknownExpectationError(
52	            f"Unknown expectation_type {spec.expectation_type!r} (no gx class {class_name!r})"
53	        )
54	    return expectation_cls(**spec.kwargs)
55	
56	
57	def _extract_sample_failures(result: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
58	    sample = {key: result[key] for key in _SAMPLE_KEYS if key in result}
59	    return sample or None
60	
61	
62	def _expected_value(kwargs: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
63	    cleaned = {key: value for key, value in dict(kwargs).items() if key not in _GX_INTERNAL_KWARGS}
64	    return cleaned or None
65	
66	
67	def to_suite_outcome(gx_result: Any) -> SuiteOutcome:
68	    """Map a GX ExpectationSuiteValidationResult onto our GX-agnostic DTO.
69	
70	    Kept GX-translation-only (no datasource specifics) so it is unit-testable
71	    with a constructed GX result, no live datasource required.
72	    """
73	    outcomes: list[CheckOutcome] = []
74	    for check_result in gx_result.results:
75	        config = check_result.expectation_config
76	        detail: dict[str, Any] = check_result.result or {}
77	        observed = (
78	            {"observed_value": detail["observed_value"]} if "observed_value" in detail else None
79	        )
80	        outcomes.append(
81	            CheckOutcome(
82	                expectation_type=config.type,
83	                success=bool(check_result.success),
84	                observed_value=observed,
85	                expected_value=_expected_value(config.kwargs) if config.kwargs else None,
86	                sample_failures=_extract_sample_failures(detail),
87	            )
88	        )
89	    return SuiteOutcome(success=bool(gx_result.success), checks=outcomes)
90	
91	
92	def run_expectations(
93	    context: Any,
94	    *,
95	    batch_definition: Any,
96	    checks: list[CheckSpec],
97	    name: str,
98	    batch_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
99	) -> SuiteOutcome:
100	    """Register the suite + validation definition for `batch_definition` and run.
101	
102	    The shared tail of every runner: GX 1.x requires the suite and validation
103	    definition to be registered on the (ephemeral, per-run) context before
104	    ``run()``. `batch_parameters` carries the in-memory DataFrame for a pandas
105	    asset; it stays `None` for an asset that resolves its own batch (a SQL table),
106	    matching a bare ``run()``.
107	    """
108	    suite = context.suites.add(
109	        gx.ExpectationSuite(
110	            name=name,
111	            expectations=[_to_gx_expectation(check) for check in checks],
112	        )
113	    )
114	    validation_definition = context.validation_definitions.add(
115	        gx.ValidationDefinition(name=f"vd-{name}", data=batch_definition, suite=suite)
116	    )
117	    result = validation_definition.run(batch_parameters=batch_parameters, result_format="COMPLETE")
118	    return to_suite_outcome(result)
119	
```

```
6	- **Related:** ADR [0005](0005-severity-tier-weights.md) / [0016](0016-severity-derivation-semantics.md) (severity), [0012](0012-monitor-kind-seam.md) (`metric_value`/`duration_ms` seam), [0011](0011-extensibility-seams-for-deferred-integrations.md) (`ResultPublisher` redaction seam)
7	
8	## Context
9	
10	DataQ now persists DQ run outcomes — `runs` + `results` (severity tier, `metric_value`, `observed/expected`, `sample_failures`) and orchestration `pipeline_runs`. Users need to **see** them: which suites ran, pass/fail/severity, per-check detail, trends, and the orchestration monitoring feed. Two shapes were on the table:
11	
12	1. **In-app React page** backed by the DataQ REST API (`runs.py` read endpoints shipped in PR-C0b — `GET /runs`, `GET /runs/{id}`, `GET /pipeline_runs`).
13	2. **Grafana** (or any BI tool) pointed straight at PostgreSQL.
14	
15	Grafana is attractive — free panels, alerting, ad-hoc SQL — and the `metric_value`/`duration_ms` columns were deliberately built SQL-aggregatable (ADR 0012) partly with dashboards in mind. But pointing a dashboard at the database **bypasses two boundaries that only exist in the application layer**:
16	
17	- **Per-suite sharing (authz).** Suite visibility is "owner or `shares` row" (`suite_authz`). A raw DB connection has no concept of the requesting user, so a Grafana viewer sees **every** suite's results regardless of who they're shared with. The whole sharing model — the v1 access story — evaporates.
18	- **PII redaction.** `results.sample_failures` holds raw failing rows, which can contain sensitive data (CLAUDE.md: redaction is the logger's job; `gx_runner` treats sample keys as redactor-only). A direct DB read serves them unredacted. The API layer is where row-level redaction / opt-in policy can live (the same trust-boundary concern ADR 0011 flags for `ResultPublisher`).
19	
20	## Decision
21	
22	**The primary results surface is an in-app React page (`/results`) backed by the DataQ API.** It is the only surface that enforces suite-level sharing and can apply PII redaction, so it is the one users get.
23	
24	**Grafana is deferred to an optional, post-v1 *ops* add-on** — a read-only operational dashboard for an operator/admin persona (fleet health, run volumes, latency), provisioned with its own read-only reporting DB role and explicit grants, **never** the per-user product surface and never a substitute for the authz/redaction the API owns. It is additive: nothing in v1 depends on it, and it can be added later without schema change (the aggregatable columns are already there).
25	
26	Concretely for v1 (PR-C1): a runs table (suite, status, timing, duration) with status filtering, a run-detail view with per-check results (severity tag, `metric_value`, observed/expected), and a `pipeline_runs` monitoring tab — all through `runs.py`, all suite-scoped. `sample_failures` stays **withheld** from the API until row-level redaction lands (tracked separately); the page shows the redaction-safe summary fields first.
27	
28	## Consequences
29	
30	**Positive**
31	- Suite-level sharing holds on the results surface — a user sees results only for suites they own or are shared on, identical to suites/checks.
32	- PII redaction has a home (the API boundary); raw sample rows never leave the trust boundary unredacted.
33	- Domain-native UX (Connections / Suites / Checks / **Results**) consistent with the rest of the app; deep-linkable, auth-gated, same error envelope.
34	- The SQL-aggregatable `metric_value`/`duration_ms` seam still pays off — for both the in-app trend charts (Week 6) and a future Grafana ops board.
35	
36	**Negative / watch**
37	- We build + maintain the results UI rather than getting Grafana's panels for free. Accepted: the authz/PII cost of the DB-direct shortcut is not payable in v1.
38	- Rich ad-hoc exploration (arbitrary SQL, custom panels) isn't available in-app v1; that's exactly the gap the optional ops Grafana add-on fills later for the operator persona.
39	- Exposing redacted `sample_failures` on the drill-down is a follow-up (needs the row-level redaction policy first).
40	
41	## Validation
42	
43	PR-C0b's `runs.py` enforces the gate (suite-scoped list + `require_permission(view)` on detail; `pipeline_runs` auth-only) with DB-backed tests proving cross-suite isolation. PR-C1 builds the page on top; the seeded demo runs/results/pipeline-runs exercise it end-to-end (browser E2E).
44	
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/adr/0019-custom-sql-check-kind.md",
  "content": "# ADR 0019 — Custom-SQL checks ride `kind='expectation'` via GX `UnexpectedRowsExpectation`\n\n- **Status:** Accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-06-14\n- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771\n- **Related:** ADR [0003](0003-gx-only-for-v1.md) (GX-only v1), [0012](0012-monitor-kind-seam.md) (the `check.kind` seam — and why custom-SQL is *not* a new kind), [0016](0016-severity-derivation-semantics.md) (binary fallback when there's no bandable metric), [0010](0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) (least-privilege connection roles)\n\n## Context\n\nThe Week-4 plan calls for a Monaco custom-SQL check editor, and the progress ledger flagged it **backend-blocked: \"need a custom-SQL check kind.\"** That assumption predates a close look at GX Core.\n\nGX Core ships [`UnexpectedRowsExpectation`](https://docs.greatexpectations.io/docs/reference/api/expectations/UnexpectedRowsExpectation_class): a Batch Expectation that runs a user-supplied SQL query and **fails if the query returns one or more rows** (success = zero rows). The query references the run target with a `{batch}` placeholder. Crucially, it rides the machinery we already have:\n\n- `Check` already has `expectation_type: str` (free-form, title-cased to a GX class at run time) + `config: JSONB` (free-form GX kwargs). Check CRUD validates neither — they are pass-through.\n- `gx_runner._to_gx_expectation` is generic: `getattr(gxe, PascalCase(expectation_type))(**config)`. `unexpected_rows_expectation` → `gxe.UnexpectedRowsExpectation(unexpected_rows_query=...)` needs **no runner change**.\n- The run / result / severity / dry-run path is `kind='expectation'`-shaped and already exercised.\n\nA de-risk run through the real path (an `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` against the dev Postgres) confirmed it end-to-end: a 0-row query → `success=True`, `observed_value=0`; a row-returning query → `success=False`, `observed_value=<unexpected row count>`; `{batch}` substitution and `to_suite_outcome` mapping both work, with **zero changes** to `gx_runner`.\n\nA distinct `kind='custom_sql'` (the original assumption) would mean a migration to add the kind **and** relax `expectation_type NOT NULL`, plus kind-based runner dispatch — all to re-implement what `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` already gives under `kind='expectation'`. The `check.kind` seam (ADR 0012) exists for **auto-monitors** (freshness / volume / …) that are *not* expectations and produce a measured scalar instead of a row-level assertion. Custom-SQL **is** a row-level assertion expressed in SQL — it belongs under `expectation`, not as a sibling kind.\n\n## Decision\n\n**A custom-SQL check is a GX `UnexpectedRowsExpectation`, persisted as a normal `kind='expectation'` check:** `expectation_type='unexpected_rows_expectation'`, `config={\"unexpected_rows_query\": \"<SQL with {batch}>\"}`. No new `kind`, no migration, no `gx_runner` change. The progress-ledger \"needs a new kind\" note is hereby revised.\n\nWhat v1 **does** add — guardrails, because this is the first path that executes user-authored SQL against a live warehouse:\n\n1. **Read-only, single-statement validation** (app layer). The query must be a single statement and read-only: `SELECT`/`WITH` only; reject DML/DDL/DCL (`INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/TRUNCATE/DROP/ALTER/CREATE/GRANT/REVOKE/…`) and statement-chaining (a stray `;` with a trailing statement). Enforced in `check_service` create/update **and** suite import, so it can't be smuggled in through any authoring path.\n2. **Datasource gating.** Custom-SQL is offered only for **SQL-queryable** datasources — Snowflake and Unity Catalog. Flat-file stores (ADLS / S3) are GX DataFrame assets, not SQL, so a custom-SQL check there can never run; reject it at author time against the suite's connection type.\n3. **Defense-in-depth, not app-layer-only.** App-layer parsing is best-effort (it is not a SQL firewall); the real boundary is the **connection's least-privilege role** (ADR 0010). The ADR + connection docs state that a connection used for custom-SQL should authenticate as a read-only role, and warehouse statement timeouts bound runaway queries.\n4. **Binary pass/fail in v1.** `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` emits an unexpected **row count** (`observed_value`), not an unexpected-percent, so `severity.extract_metric` finds no bandable metric and the check resolves binary `pass`/`fail` (ADR 0016 fallback) — exactly right for \"this query should return no rows.\" Banding severity on the row count (populating `metric_value` from the count) is a deferred enhancement, not a v1 need.\n\n## Consequences\n\n**Positive**\n- Smallest possible surface: no migration, no new `kind`, no runner branch. The custom-SQL check flows through the existing run/result/severity/dry-run path unchanged — the GX-only-v1 architecture (ADR 0003) pays off again.\n- Security is concentrated in one validation module reused by every authoring path, with the connection role as the real backstop.\n- Forward-compatible: if count-based severity is wanted later, it's an additive change in `severity.extract_metric` (read `observed_value` for this expectation_type), no schema change.\n\n**Negative / watch**\n- `expectation_type` stays free-form (no server allowlist), so the SQL guardrail — not a type allowlist — is the control for this path. A general `expectation_type` allowlist is noted as optional later hardening (it would also catch typo'd expectation types).\n- App-layer read-only parsing can be fooled by exotic SQL; we accept that and lean on the least-privilege role. We do **not** claim the parser is a security boundary.\n- `{batch}` is a GX-owned placeholder; the editor/docs must teach it, and a query that forgets it (a bare table name) runs against whatever the author typed, not the suite's run target — a correctness footgun the dry-run preview helps surface.\n\n## Validation\n\nDe-risk script confirmed the GX round-trip (pass/fail + `observed_value` + `{batch}`) through the unchanged `gx_runner` against the dev Postgres. PR 1 lands the validation module + datasource gating + an adversarial SQL battery (DML / multi-statement / comment-smuggled / empty) and the GX round-trip test; the dry-run path (PR 2) lets the editor preview before save; the Monaco editor (PR 3) authors `unexpected_rows_query` and mirrors the read-only validation client-side.\n"
}
```

```
120	    expectation_type: str | None = None,

126	    """Partial update. `suite_id` and `kind` are immutable.
127	
128	    Follows the codebase PATCH convention (connections / suites): a `None`
129	    argument means "not provided", so an omitted field is left unchanged. v1 has
130	    no clear-to-NULL path for thresholds; recreate the check to drop one.
131	    """
132	    check = get_check(session, suite_id, check_id)
133	    if name is not None:

136	        check.expectation_type = expectation_type

143	    if critical_threshold is not None:
144	        check.critical_threshold = critical_threshold
145	    session.commit()
146	    session.refresh(check)
147	    log.info("check_updated", check_id=str(check.id))
148	    return check
149
```

```
    connection = session.get(Connection, connection_id)
    if connection is None:
        raise SuiteImportConnectionInvalidError(
            "connection not found", detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id)}
        )
    if connection.type in ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS:
        # Orchestration providers (ADF/Airflow) are never suite datasources
        # (CLAUDE.md §4) — same guard as create_suite, applied at import time.
        raise SuiteImportConnectionInvalidError(
            "orchestration providers cannot be a suite's datasource; "
            "they trigger suites via trigger bindings",
            detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id), "type": connection.type},
        )
    # Validate every check kind up front so a bad document writes nothing.
    for c in checks:
        validate_kind(c["kind"])

    suite = Suite(
        name=name,
        description=description,
        connection_id=connection_id,
        created_by=created_by,
    )
    suite.checks = [
        Check(
            name=c["name"],
            kind=c["kind"],
            expectation_type=c["expectation_type"],
            config=c["config"],
            warn_threshold=c["warn_threshold"],
            fail_threshold=c["fail_threshold"],
            critical_threshold=c["critical_threshold"],
        )
        for c in checks
    ]
    session.add(suite)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(suite)
    log.info(
        "suite_imported",
        suite_id=str(suite.id),
        connection_id=str(connection_id),
        check_count=len(checks),
    )
    return suite
```

```json
  "content": "\"\"\"Guardrails for custom-SQL checks (ADR 0019).\n\nA custom-SQL check is a GX ``UnexpectedRowsExpectation``: a normal\n``kind='expectation'`` check with ``expectation_type='unexpected_rows_expectation'``\nand ``config={'unexpected_rows_query': '<SQL with {batch}>'}``. It rides the\nexisting model / runner / result path unchanged — the only thing v1 adds is this\nsingle guardrail, reused by every authoring path (check CRUD + suite import).\n\nTwo checks:\n\n1. **Datasource gating** — custom-SQL is offered only for SQL-queryable\n   datasources (Snowflake, Unity Catalog). Flat-file stores (ADLS / S3) are GX\n   DataFrame assets, not SQL, so the query could never run there.\n2. **Read-only, single statement** — the query must be a single ``SELECT`` /\n   ``WITH`` statement with no DML/DDL/DCL. This is **best-effort, defence-in-depth,\n   not a SQL firewall** (ADR 0019): the real boundary is the connection's\n   least-privilege role. We strip string literals / quoted identifiers / comments\n   before scanning so a literal ``'delete'`` or a column named ``\"update\"`` is not\n   mistaken for a keyword, then require a read-only shape.\n\nFastAPI-free like the sibling services: raises ``DataQError`` subclasses.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom backend.app.core.errors import DataQError\n\n# The GX expectation a custom-SQL check maps to (ADR 0019).\nCUSTOM_SQL_EXPECTATION_TYPE = \"unexpected_rows_expectation\"\n# The GX kwarg holding the user's query.\nQUERY_KEY = \"unexpected_rows_query\"\n\n# Datasources GX can run SQL against (ADR 0019). Flat files (adls_gen2 / s3) are\n# DataFrame assets; orchestration types (adf / airflow) aren't datasources at all.\nSQL_QUERYABLE_TYPES = frozenset({\"snowflake\", \"unity_catalog\"})\n\n# Statement keywords that mutate data, schema, permissions, or transaction state.\n# A read-only check query must contain none of them (as a bareword, after string\n# literals / quoted identifiers / comments are stripped). `replace` is deliberately\n# absent — it collides with the very common `replace()` string function; a\n# `CREATE OR REPLACE` is already caught by `create`.\n_FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS = frozenset(\n    {\n        \"insert\",\n        \"update\",\n        \"delete\",\n        \"merge\",\n        \"upsert\",\n        \"truncate\",\n        \"drop\",\n        \"alter\",\n        \"create\",\n        \"grant\",\n        \"revoke\",\n        \"commit\",\n        \"rollback\",\n        \"into\",  # SELECT ... INTO <table> creates a table in some dialects\n    }\n)\n\n_LEADING_KEYWORD = re.compile(r\"[\\s(]*([a-zA-Z]+)\")\n_WORD = re.compile(r\"[a-zA-Z_]+\")\n\n\nclass CustomSqlInvalidError(DataQError):\n    status_code = 422\n    code = \"custom_sql_invalid\"\n\n\ndef is_custom_sql(expectation_type: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if `expectation_type` is the custom-SQL expectation (ADR 0019).\"\"\"\n    return expectation_type == CUSTOM_SQL_EXPECTATION_TYPE\n\n\ndef _strip_comments(sql: str) -> str:\n    sql = re.sub(r\"/\\*.*?\\*/\", \" \", sql, flags=re.DOTALL)  # /* block */\n    return re.sub(r\"--[^\\n]*\", \" \", sql)  # -- line\n\n\ndef _strip_quoted(sql: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Blank out string literals + quoted identifiers so their contents can't be\n    mistaken for SQL keywords or statement separators.\"\"\"\n    sql = re.sub(r\"'(?:[^']|'')*'\", \" \", sql)  # 'single' strings ('' escape)\n    sql = re.sub(r'\"(?:[^\"]|\"\")*\"', \" \", sql)  # \"quoted\" identifiers\n    return re.sub(r\"`[^`]*`\", \" \", sql)  # `backtick` identifiers (Databricks/UC)\n\n\ndef validate_query(raw_query: Any) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Reject a non-read-only or multi-statement custom-SQL query (422).\n\n    Best-effort lexical guard (ADR 0019), not a SQL firewall — paired with the\n    connection's least-privilege role as the real boundary.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(raw_query, str) or not raw_query.strip():\n        raise CustomSqlInvalidError(\n            f\"custom-SQL check requires a non-empty {QUERY_KEY!r}\",\n            detail={\"query_key\": QUERY_KEY},\n        )\n\n    analysis = re.sub(r\"[;\\s]+$\", \"\", _strip_quoted(_strip_comments(raw_query)).strip())\n    if not analysis:\n        raise CustomSqlInvalidError(\n            \"custom-SQL query is empty after removing comments\",\n            detail={\"query_key\": QUERY_KEY},\n        )\n\n    if \";\" in analysis:\n        raise CustomSqlInvalidError(\n            \"custom-SQL must be a single statement (no ';'-chained statements)\",\n            detail={\"query_key\": QUERY_KEY},\n        )\n\n    leading = _LEADING_KEYWORD.match(analysis)\n    first_kw = leading.group(1).lower() if leading else \"\"\n    if first_kw not in {\"select\", \"with\"}:\n        raise CustomSqlInvalidError(\n            \"custom-SQL must be a read-only SELECT / WITH query\",\n            detail={\"query_key\": QUERY_KEY, \"first_keyword\": first_kw or None},\n        )\n\n    forbidden = sorted(set(w.lower() for w in _WORD.findall(analysis)) & _FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS)\n    if forbidden:\n        raise CustomSqlInvalidError(\n            \"custom-SQL must be read-only; remove the disallowed keyword(s)\",\n            detail={\"query_key\": QUERY_KEY, \"forbidden\": forbidden},\n        )\n\n\ndef validate_custom_sql_check(\n    *, expectation_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], connection_type: str\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Guardrail for a custom-SQL check; a no-op for any other expectation.\n\n    Rejects (422) a custom-SQL check on a non-SQL datasource, or one whose query\n    isn't a single read-only statement.\n    \"\"\"\n    if > AGENT
```

Wait — I spotted a real bug in my own validator before writing tests: stripping comments *before* string literals lets a `--` **inside a string** mask a trailing statement (e.g. `SELECT 1 WHERE x='a--'; DROP TABLE y` would strip the `; DROP` as a "comment" and wrongly pass). For a security guard that's a bypass. I'll replace the two regex passes with a single-pass scanner that handles strings and comments together:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_014SgMizUtGAoNmNhjdPCnLj
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/services/custom_sql.py",
  "old_string": "def _strip_comments(sql: str) -> str:\n    sql = re.sub(r\"/\\*.*?\\*/\", \" \", sql, flags=re.DOTALL)  # /* block */\n    return re.sub(r\"--[^\\n]*\", \" \", sql)  # -- line\n\n\ndef _strip_quoted(sql: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Blank out string literals + quoted identifiers so their contents can't be\n    mistaken for SQL keywords or statement separators.\"\"\"\n    sql = re.sub(r\"'(?:[^']|'')*'\", \" \", sql)  # 'single' strings ('' escape)\n    sql = re.sub(r'\"(?:[^\"]|\"\")*\"', \" \", sql)  # \"quoted\" identifiers\n    return re.sub(r\"`[^`]*`\", \" \", sql)  # `backtick` identifiers (Databricks/UC)",
  "new_string": "def _strip_noncode(sql: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Replace comments, string literals, and quoted identifiers with spaces in a\n    single left-to-right pass, leaving only executable code.\n\n    A single pass (not sequential regexes) is required so neither construct can\n    mask the other: a ``--`` *inside* a string must not be read as a comment (which\n    could hide a trailing ``; DROP ...`` from the keyword scan), and a quote inside\n    a comment must not start a bogus string. Handles ``--`` line comments, ``/* */``\n    block comments, and ``'`` / ``\"`` / `` ` `` quotes (``''``/``\"\"`` doubled-escape).\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    i, n = 0, len(sql)\n    while i < n:\n        pair = sql[i : i + 2]\n        if pair == \"--\":\n            nl = sql.find(\"\\n\", i)\n            i = n if nl == -1 else nl\n            out.append(\" \")\n        elif pair == \"/*\":\n            end = sql.find(\"*/\", i + 2)\n            i = n if end == -1 else end + 2\n            out.append(\" \")\n        elif sql[i] in \"'\\\"`\":\n            quote = sql[i]\n            i += 1\n            while i < n:\n                if sql[i] == quote:\n                    if quote in \"'\\\"\" and sql[i + 1 : i + 2] == quote:\n                        i += 2  # doubled quote = escaped, stay in the string\n                        continue\n                    i += 1\n                    break\n                i += 1\n            out.append(\" \")\n        else:\n            out.append(sql[i])\n            i += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)"
}
```

```
"""End-to-end suite runs across the three datasource runner types.

Real `run_service.execute_run` + real Postgres persistence + (for flat-file and
Unity Catalog) **real GX execution** on an in-memory DataFrame — the whole path:
`check.kind` dispatch → runner → GX validation → severity derivation → `Result`
rows. Only the file download / table read is stubbed with a canned frame; the
warehouse runners' live connect is the deferred-smoke seam, so Snowflake runs
through a canned outcome (its GX result-mapping is covered in
`datasources/test_snowflake.py`).

Skips without `TEST_DATABASE_URL` (the `db_session` fixture).
"""

import uuid
from typing import Any

import pandas as pd
import pytest
from sqlalchemy import select

from backend.app.datasources import flatfile
from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckOutcome, CheckSpec, SuiteOutcome
from backend.app.datasources.unity_catalog import UnityCatalogCheckRunner, UnityCatalogConfig
from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Result, Run, Suite, User
from backend.app.services import run_service
from backend.tests.support.adversarial import ADVERSARIAL_FRAMES

# Two checks every datasource test reuses: a column null-check (fails on a null)
# and a table row-count check (column-agnostic, passes).
_CHECKS = [
    {
        "name": "id_notnull",
        "type": "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
        "config": {"column": "id"},
    },
    {
        "name": "rowcount",
        "type": "expect_table_row_count_to_be_between",
        "config": {"min_value": 1, "max_value": 100},
    },
]


def _seed(
    db_session: Any,
    *,
    conn_type: str,
    config: dict[str, Any],
    checks_spec: list[dict[str, Any]] = _CHECKS,
) -> tuple[Suite, list[Check]]:
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"{conn_type}@ex")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"{conn_type}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}",
        type=conn_type,
        env="dev",
        config=config,
        secret_ref="kv-ref",
        created_by=owner.id,
```

> AGENT

All three issues you raised are resolved. Summary:

## 1. Why CI was red
The Stryker harness README (`frontend/mutation/README.md`, from #255) was never run through Prettier, so the frontend `prettier --check .` job failed on **every** push to `main` afterward. Fixed in **[#257](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/257)** — `main` is green again (`50d00e1`).

## 2. How #255/#256 merged while red
`main`'s protection is a **ruleset** that required *a PR + linear history + no force-push* — but had **no `required_status_checks` rule**. So CI ran purely as information, never as a gate. My `gh pr merge --auto` only waits for *required* checks; with none required (and 0 approvals needed in solo-dev), it collapsed to an immediate squash. The Prettier failure had nothing configured to block it.

## 3. Enforcing CI (done)
Added a `required_status_checks` rule to the ruleset — **12 checks now block merge**: all Backend (lint/type/tests/Bandit/pip-audit), all Frontend (lint/tests/pnpm-audit/Playwright E2E), Secret scanning (betterleaks), and both CodeQL analyses. Verified `prettier`-class failures will now hold a PR. I confirmed these jobs run unconditionally on every PR (a docs-only PR triggered all of them), so there's **no "required check never reports" deadlock**. `strict` policy is off (no forced branch-up-to-date churn). The `RepositoryRole … always` bypass remains so you keep an admin override — say the word if you want a hard gate with no bypass.

One process note for myself: I've switched to verifying CI green **before** merging (not blind `--auto`), and to running `prettier --check .` (whole tree) locally on frontend changes.

Summary of what I verified as correct (no finding):
- create_check, update_check, and import_suite all wire the guard correctly. update_check validates POST-patch effective state (`check.expectation_type`/`check.config` after applying the partial), before `session.commit()`, so a rejected update persists nothing; a config-only PATCH on an already-custom check and a type-flip-to-custom on an old config are both caught.
- `_connection_type`'s `assert connection is not None` is sound: `Suite.connection_id` is `nullable=False` (models.py:139-141).

- `CustomSqlInvalidError` subclasses `DataQError` (422) and is mapped by the registered `DataQError` handler, so it propagates as 422 like its siblings.
- The 4 `custom_sql`-keyed API tests pass.

```
78	def _strip_noncode(sql: str) -> str:
79	    """Replace comments, string literals, and quoted identifiers with spaces in a
80	    single left-to-right pass, leaving only executable code.
81	
82	    A single pass (not sequential regexes) is required so neither construct can
83	    mask the other: a ``--`` *inside* a string must not be read as a comment (which
84	    could hide a trailing ``; DROP ...`` from the keyword scan), and a quote inside
85	    a comment must not start a bogus string. Handles ``--`` line comments, ``/* */``
86	    block comments, and ``'`` / ``"`` / `` ` `` quotes (``''``/``""`` doubled-escape).
87	    """
88	    out: list[str] = []
89	    i, n = 0, len(sql)
90	    while i < n:
91	        pair = sql[i : i + 2]
92	        if pair == "--":
93	            nl = sql.find("\n", i)
94	            i = n if nl == -1 else nl
95	            out.append(" ")
96	        elif pair == "/*":
97	            end = sql.find("*/", i + 2)
98	            i = n if end == -1 else end + 2
99	            out.append(" ")
100	        elif sql[i] in "'\"`":
101	            quote = sql[i]
102	            i += 1
103	            while i < n:
104	                if sql[i] == quote:
105	                    if quote in "'\"" and sql[i + 1 : i + 2] == quote:
106	                        i += 2  # doubled quote = escaped, stay in the string
107	                        continue
108	                    i += 1
109	                    break
110	                i += 1
111	            out.append(" ")
112	        else:
113	            out.append(sql[i])
114	            i += 1
115	    return "".join(out)
116
```

```json
  "old_string": "def _strip_noncode(sql: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Replace comments, string literals, and quoted identifiers with spaces in a\n    single left-to-right pass, leaving only executable code.\n\n    A single pass (not sequential regexes) is required so neither construct can\n    mask the other: a ``--`` *inside* a string must not be read as a comment (which\n    could hide a trailing ``; DROP ...`` from the keyword scan), and a quote inside\n    a comment must not start a bogus string. Handles ``--`` line comments, ``/* */``\n    block comments, and ``'`` / ``\"`` / `` ` `` quotes (``''``/``\"\"`` doubled-escape).\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    i, n = 0, len(sql)\n    while i < n:\n        pair = sql[i : i + 2]\n        if pair == \"--\":\n            nl = sql.find(\"\\n\", i)\n            i = n if nl == -1 else nl\n            out.append(\" \")\n        elif pair == \"/*\":\n            end = sql.find(\"*/\", i + 2)\n            i = n if end == -1 else end + 2\n            out.append(\" \")\n        elif sql[i] in \"'\\\"`\":\n            quote = sql[i]\n            i += 1\n            while i < n:\n                if sql[i] == quote:\n                    if quote in \"'\\\"\" and sql[i + 1 : i + 2] == quote:\n                        i += 2  # doubled quote = escaped, stay in the string\n                        continue\n                    i += 1\n                    break\n                i += 1\n            out.append(\" \")\n        else:\n            out.append(sql[i])\n            i += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)",
  "new_string": "def _strip_noncode(sql: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Replace comments and string literals with spaces in a single left-to-right\n    pass, leaving only executable code. Returns ``(code, well_formed)``.\n\n    A single pass (not sequential regexes) is required so neither construct can\n    mask the other: a ``--`` *inside* a string must not be read as a comment (which\n    could hide a trailing ``; DROP ...`` from the keyword scan), and a quote inside\n    a comment must not start a bogus string. Handles ``--`` line comments, ``/* */``\n    block comments, and ``'`` / ``\"`` string/identifier quotes (``''``/``\"\"``\n    doubled-escape).\n\n    **Backtick is intentionally NOT a quote here.** Our SQL datasources (Snowflake,\n    Unity Catalog) don't delimit strings with `` ` ``, so treating a backtick span as\n    a string would blank it out and let a ``; DROP`` hide inside it. Backticks stay\n    as code, so anything between them is keyword/`;`-scanned like the rest.\n\n    ``well_formed`` is ``False`` if a string or block comment is left unterminated:\n    the lexical analysis is then unreliable (the rest of the query was swallowed as\n    \"string\"/\"comment\"), so the caller must **fail closed** and reject.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    i, n = 0, len(sql)\n    well_formed = True\n    while i < n:\n        pair = sql[i : i + 2]\n        if pair == \"--\":\n            nl = sql.find(\"\\n\", i)\n            i = n if nl == -1 else nl\n            out.append(\" \")\n        elif pair == \"/*\":\n            end = sql.find(\"*/\", i + 2)\n            if end == -1:\n                well_formed = False  # unterminated block comment\n                i = n\n            else:\n                i = end + 2\n            out.append(\" \")\n        elif sql[i] in \"'\\\"\":\n            quote = sql[i]\n            i += 1\n            closed = False\n            while i < n:\n                if sql[i] == quote:\n                    if sql[i + 1 : i + 2] == quote:\n                        i += 2  # doubled quote = escaped, stay in the string\n                        continue\n                    i += 1\n                    closed = True\n                    break\n                i += 1\n            if not closed:\n                well_formed = False  # unterminated string literal\n            out.append(\" \")\n        else:\n            out.append(sql[i])\n            i += 1\n    return \"\".join(out), well_formed"
}
```

```
29	2. **Datasource gating.** Custom-SQL is offered only for **SQL-queryable** datasources — Snowflake and Unity Catalog. Flat-file stores (ADLS / S3) are GX DataFrame assets, not SQL, so a custom-SQL check there can never run; reject it at author time against the suite's connection type.
30	3. **Defense-in-depth, not app-layer-only.** App-layer parsing is best-effort (it is not a SQL firewall); the real boundary is the **connection's least-privilege role** (ADR 0010). The ADR + connection docs state that a connection used for custom-SQL should authenticate as a read-only role, and warehouse statement timeouts bound runaway queries.
31	4. **Binary pass/fail in v1.** `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` emits an unexpected **row count** (`observed_value`), not an unexpected-percent, so `severity.extract_metric` finds no bandable metric and the check resolves binary `pass`/`fail` (ADR 0016 fallback) — exactly right for "this query should return no rows." Banding severity on the row count (populating `metric_value` from the count) is a deferred enhancement, not a v1 need.
32	
33	## Consequences
34	
35	**Positive**
36	- Smallest possible surface: no migration, no new `kind`, no runner branch. The custom-SQL check flows through the existing run/result/severity/dry-run path unchanged — the GX-only-v1 architecture (ADR 0003) pays off again.
37	- Security is concentrated in one validation module reused by every authoring path, with the connection role as the real backstop.
38	- Forward-compatible: if count-based severity is wanted later, it's an additive change in `severity.extract_metric` (read `observed_value` for this expectation_type), no schema change.
39	
40	**Negative / watch**
```

```
1	import { Divider, Flex, Form, Input, InputNumber, Typography } from 'antd';
2	import type { Rule } from 'antd/es/form';
3	
4	import { parseList } from './checkForm';
5	import type { ConfigField } from './expectationCatalog';
6	
7	/**
8	 * Shared check-form field components, used by both the edit drawer (`CheckDrawer`)
9	 * and the dedicated create page (`CheckNew`): the dynamic config-field renderer
10	 * and the severity-threshold block. Pure conversions live in `checkForm.ts`.
11	 */
12	
13	export function ConfigFieldItem({ field }: { field: ConfigField }) {
14	  const label = field.optional ? `${field.label} (optional)` : field.label;
15	  const rules: Rule[] = field.optional ? [] : [{ required: true }];
16	  // A required list of only delimiters ("," / " , ") is non-empty (so it passes
17	  // `required`) but parses to zero items — reject it inline rather than letting
18	  // the check save with an empty value_set that only fails later at GX run time.
19	  if (field.type === 'list' && !field.optional) {
20	    rules.push({
21	      validator: (_: unknown, value: unknown) =>
22	        parseList(value).length > 0
23	          ? Promise.resolve()
24	          : Promise.reject(new Error('Enter at least one value')),
25	    });
26	  }
27	  return (
28	    <Form.Item name={['config', field.name]} label={label} rules={rules} extra={field.help}>
29	      {field.type === 'number' ? (
30	        <InputNumber style={{ width: '100%' }} />
31	      ) : (
32	        <Input placeholder={field.type === 'list' ? 'value1, value2, value3' : undefined} />
33	      )}
34	    </Form.Item>
35	  );
36	}
```

```
1	import type { CheckCreate } from '../../api/suites';
2	import { EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE, type ExpectationSpec } from './expectationCatalog';
3	
4	/**
5	 * Pure check-authoring form helpers shared by the edit drawer (`CheckDrawer`)
6	 * and the dedicated create page (`CheckNew`): the form↔payload conversions, so
7	 * the two surfaces can't drift on kwarg shaping. The matching field components
8	 * live in `checkFormFields.tsx`.
9	 */
10	
11	/** Split a comma-separated list field into trimmed, non-empty items. */
12	export function parseList(value: unknown): string[] {
13	  return String(value ?? '')
14	    .split(',')
15	    .map((s) => s.trim())
16	    .filter(Boolean);
17	}
18	
19	function numOrNull(v: unknown): number | null {
20	  return typeof v === 'number' ? v : null;
21	}
22	
23	/** Build the GX `config` kwargs from only the selected expectation's fields. */
24	function formToConfig(
25	  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,
26	  raw: Record<string, unknown>,
27	): Record<string, unknown> {
28	  const config: Record<string, unknown> = {};
29	  if (!spec) return config;
30	  for (const field of spec.fields) {
31	    const value = raw[field.name];
32	    if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') continue;
33	    if (field.type === 'list') {
34	      const items = parseList(value);
35	      if (items.length > 0) config[field.name] = items;
36	    } else {
37	      config[field.name] = value;
38	    }
39	  }
40	  return config;
41	}
42	
43	/** Inverse of formToConfig for edit-mode prefill (list array → comma string). */
44	export function configToForm(
45	  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,
46	  config: Record<string, unknown>,
47	): Record<string, unknown> {
48	  const form: Record<string, unknown> = {};
49	  if (!spec) return form;
50	  for (const field of spec.fields) {
51	    const value = config[field.name];
52	    if (value === undefined) continue;
53	    form[field.name] = field.type === 'list' && Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : value;
54	  }
55	  return form;
56	}
57	
58	/** Assemble the create/update payload from validated form values. Rebuilds
59	 *  `config` from only the selected expectation's fields, so switching types
60	 *  never leaks stale kwargs. */
61	export function buildCheckPayload(values: Record<string, unknown>): CheckCreate {
62	  const spec = EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[values.expectation_type as string];
63	  return {
64	    name: values.name as string,
65	    expectation_type: values.expectation_type as string,
66	    config: formToConfig(spec, (values.config ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>),
67	    warn_threshold: numOrNull(values.warn_threshold),
68	    fail_threshold: numOrNull(values.fail_threshold),
69	    critical_threshold: numOrNull(values.critical_threshold),
70	  };
71	}
72
```

```
26	export function CheckNew() {
27	  const navigate = useNavigate();
28	  const { suiteId } = useParams<{ suiteId: string }>();
29	  const { message } = App.useApp();
30	  const [category, setCategory] = useState<ExpectationCategory>();
31	  const [expectationType, setExpectationType] = useState<string>();
32	  const [form] = Form.useForm();
33	  const column = Form.useWatch(['config', 'column'], form) as string | undefined;
34	  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
35	  // The suite's run target (#215) drives the dry-run preview's table/schema.
36	  const { state: suiteState } = useAsyncData(() =>
37	    suiteId ? getSuite(suiteId) : Promise.reject(new Error('no suite')),
38	  );
39	  const target = suiteState.status === 'ok' ? suiteState.data.target : null;
40	
41	  const backToSuite = () => navigate(suiteId ? `/suites/${suiteId}` : '/suites');
42	  const spec = expectationType ? EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[expectationType] : undefined;
43	
44	  // Start the config form clean each time an expectation is (re)picked — after
45	  // the <Form> mounts (it only renders in the config step), so the store is
46	  // connected and a re-pick can't leak the prior expectation's fields.
47	  useEffect(() => {
48	    if (expectationType) form.resetFields();
49	  }, [expectationType, form]);
50	
51	  const onFinish = async (values: Record<string, unknown>) => {
52	    if (!suiteId || !expectationType) return;
53	    setSubmitting(true);
54	    try {
55	      await createCheck(
56	        suiteId,
57	        buildCheckPayload({ ...values, expectation_type: expectationType }),
58	      );
59	      message.success(`${values.name as string}: created`);
60	      backToSuite();
61	    } catch (err) {
62	      message.error(`Create failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
```

```
4	import { type Check, updateCheck } from '../../api/suites';
5	import { buildCheckPayload, configToForm } from './checkForm';
6	import { ConfigFieldItem, SeverityThresholdFields } from './checkFormFields';
7	import { ColumnProfilePanel } from './ColumnProfilePanel';
8	import { DryRunPreview } from './DryRunPreview';
9	import { EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE, EXPECTATIONS_BY_CATEGORY } from './expectationCatalog';
10	
11	/**
12	 * Edit a GX check. The expectation Select (grouped by category) drives which
13	 * config fields render (from the expectation catalog); the submitted `config` is
14	 * rebuilt from only the selected expectation's declared fields, so switching
15	 * types never leaks stale kwargs. Creating a check is the dedicated
16	 * `/suites/:suiteId/checks/new` page, not this drawer.
17	 */
18	export function CheckDrawer({
19	  open,
20	  suiteId,
21	  check,
22	  target,
23	  onClose,
24	  onSaved,
25	}: {
26	  open: boolean;
27	  suiteId: string;
28	  check?: Check;
29	  /** The suite's run target (#215) — drives the dry-run preview's table/schema. */
30	  target: Record<string, unknown> | null;
31	  onClose: () => void;
32	  onSaved: () => void;
33	}) {
34	  const { message } = App.useApp();
35	  const [form] = Form.useForm();
36	  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
37	  const selectedType = Form.useWatch('expectation_type', form) as string | undefined;
38	  const column = Form.useWatch(['config', 'column'], form) as string | undefined;
39	  const spec = selectedType ? EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[selectedType] : undefined;
40	
41	  // Reset first (antd keeps values for unmounted fields, so stale config can
42	  // survive an open→close→open with a different check), then prefill.
43	  useEffect(() => {
44	    if (!open || !check) return;
45	    form.resetFields();
46	    form.setFieldsValue({
47	      name: check.name,
48	      expectation_type: check.expectation_type,
49	      config: configToForm(EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[check.expectation_type], check.config),
50	      warn_threshold: check.warn_threshold ?? undefined,
51	      fail_threshold: check.fail_threshold ?? undefined,
52	      critical_threshold: check.critical_threshold ?? undefined,
53	    });
54	  }, [open, check, form]);
55	
56	  const onSubmit = async () => {
57	    if (!check) return;
58	    let values: Record<string, unknown>;
59	    try {
60	      values = await form.validateFields();
61	    } catch {
62	      return; // inline validation errors
63	    }
64	    const payload = buildCheckPayload(values);
65	    setSubmitting(true);
66	    try {
67	      await updateCheck(suiteId, check.id, payload);
68	      message.success(`${payload.name}: saved`);
69	      onSaved();
70	    } catch (err) {
71	      message.error(`Save failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
72	    } finally {
73	      setSubmitting(false);
74	    }
75	  };
76	
77	  return (
78	    <Drawer
79	      title={check ? `Edit “${check.name}”` : 'Edit check'}
80	      open={open}
81	      onClose={onClose}
82	      width={520}
83	      destroyOnHidden
84	      extra={
85	        <Flex gap={8}>
86	          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
87	          <Button type="primary" loading={submitting} onClick={onSubmit}>
88	            Save
89	          </Button>
90	        </Flex>
91	      }
92	    >
93	      <Form form={form} layout="vertical">
94	        <Form.Item name="name" label="Name" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
95	          <Input placeholder="e.g. order_id not null" />
96	        </Form.Item>
97	        <Form.Item name="expectation_type" label="Expectation" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
98	          <Select
99	            placeholder="Select an expectation"
100	            // Grouped by category (antd optgroups) — the GX-Cloud-style picker.
101	            options={EXPECTATIONS_BY_CATEGORY.map((g) => ({
102	              label: g.category,
103	              options: g.specs.map((e) => ({ value: e.type, label: e.label })),
104	            }))}
105	          />
106	        </Form.Item>
107	
108	        {spec && (
109	          <>
110	            <Typography.Paragraph type="secondary" style={{ marginTop: -8 }}>
111	              {spec.description}
112	            </Typography.Paragraph>
113	            {spec.fields.map((field) => (
114	              <ConfigFieldItem key={field.name} field={field} />
115	            ))}
116	          </>
117	        )}
118	
119	        <SeverityThresholdFields />
120	
121	        <ColumnProfilePanel suiteId={suiteId} target={target} column={column} />
122	
123	        <DryRunPreview
124	          suiteId={suiteId}
125	          expectationType={selectedType}
126	          target={target}
127	          form={form}
128	        />
129	      </Form>
130	    </Drawer>
131	  );
132	}
```

```
/** Mirrors the backend `ConnectionCreate` schema (secret is write-only). */
export interface ConnectionCreate {
  name: string;
  type: ConnectionType;
  env: ConnectionEnv;
  config: Record<string, unknown>;
  secret?: string;
}

export async function createConnection(payload: ConnectionCreate): Promise<Connection> {
  const { data } = await api.post<Connection>('/connections', payload);
  return data;
}

/** Mirrors the backend `ConnectionUpdate` schema — type/env are immutable. */
export interface ConnectionUpdate {
  name?: string;
  config?: Record<string, unknown>;
  secret?: string;
}

export async function updateConnection(id: string, payload: ConnectionUpdate): Promise<Connection> {
  const { data } = await api.patch<Connection>(`/connections/${id}`, payload);
  return data;
}

export async function deleteConnection(id: string): Promise<void> {
  await api.delete(`/connections/${id}`);
}

/** Rotate the credential and verify it in one step (bad credential → error). */
export async function reauthConnection(id: string, secret: string): Promise<{ ok: boolean }> {
  const { data } = await api.post<{ ok: boolean }>(`/connections/${id}/reauth`, { secret });
  return data;
}
```
