{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/components/checks/customSql.ts",
  "content": "/**\n * Client-side mirror of the backend custom-SQL guardrail (ADR 0019) for inline\n * editor feedback. The backend `custom_sql.validate_query` is the authoritative\n * boundary (and runs with extra=\"forbid\" + a least-privilege role); this is a\n * lighter, best-effort pre-check so the editor flags an obviously non-read-only\n * or multi-statement query before the save round-trips to a 422.\n *\n * Kept pure (no React) so it's unit- and mutation-testable in isolation.\n */\n\n/** The GX expectation a custom-SQL check maps to (ADR 0019). */\nexport const CUSTOM_SQL_EXPECTATION_TYPE = 'unexpected_rows_expectation';\n/** The GX kwarg / config key holding the user's query. */\nexport const CUSTOM_SQL_QUERY_KEY = 'unexpected_rows_query';\n\nexport const isCustomSql = (expectationType: string | undefined): boolean =>\n  expectationType === CUSTOM_SQL_EXPECTATION_TYPE;\n\n// State-mutating / proc-invoking statement keywords — a read-only check query\n// must contain none of them (as a bareword, after strings/comments are stripped).\n// `comment` / `replace` are omitted (common column name / `replace()` function),\n// matching the backend set.\nconst FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS = new Set([\n  'insert',\n  'update',\n  'delete',\n  'merge',\n  'upsert',\n  'truncate',\n  'drop',\n  'alter',\n  'create',\n  'grant',\n  'revoke',\n  'commit',\n  'rollback',\n  'into',\n  'call',\n  'exec',\n  'execute',\n  'do',\n  'copy',\n  'lock',\n  'set',\n  'reset',\n  'discard',\n  'prepare',\n  'deallocate',\n  'vacuum',\n  'analyze',\n  'use',\n  'attach',\n  'detach',\n  'unload',\n]);\n\n/**\n * Replace comments and string literals with spaces in a single left-to-right pass\n * so neither can mask the other. Backtick is intentionally NOT a quote (Snowflake\n * / Unity Catalog don't delimit strings with it). Returns `null` if a string or\n * block comment is left unterminated — the caller fails closed.\n */\nfunction stripNonCode(sql: string): string | null {\n  let out = '';\n  let i = 0;\n  const n = sql.length;\n  let wellFormed = true;\n  while (i < n) {\n    const pair = sql.slice(i, i + 2);\n    if (pair === '--') {\n      const nl = sql.indexOf('\\n', i);\n      i = nl === -1 ? n : nl;\n      out += ' ';\n    } else if (pair === '/*') {\n      const end = sql.indexOf('*/', i + 2);\n      if (end === -1) {\n        wellFormed = false;\n        i = n;\n      } else {\n        i = end + 2;\n      }\n      out += ' ';\n    } else if (sql[i] === \"'\" || sql[i] === '\"') {\n      const quote = sql[i];\n      i += 1;\n      let closed = false;\n      while (i < n) {\n        if (sql[i] === quote) {\n          if (sql[i + 1] === quote) {\n            i += 2; // doubled quote = escaped, stay in the string\n            continue;\n          }\n          i += 1;\n          closed = true;\n          break;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n      }\n      if (!closed) wellFormed = false;\n      out += ' ';\n    } else {\n      out += sql[i];\n      i += 1;\n    }\n  }\n  return wellFormed ? out : null;\n}\n\nconst TRAILING = /[\\s;]+$/;\nconst LEADING_KEYWORD = /^[\\s(]*([a-zA-Z]+)/;\nconst WORD = /[a-zA-Z_]+/g;\n\n/**\n * Best-effort read-only / single-statement check. Returns an error message, or\n * `null` if the query looks acceptable. The backend is authoritative.\n */\nexport function validateCustomSqlQuery(query: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!query || !query.trim()) return 'Enter a SQL query.';\n\n  const code = stripNonCode(query);\n  if (code === null) return 'Unterminated string literal or comment.';\n\n  const analysis = code.trim().replace(TRAILING, '');\n  if (!analysis) return 'Query is empty after removing comments.';\n  if (analysis.includes(';')) return 'Use a single statement (no “;”-chained statements).';\n\n  const first = LEADING_KEYWORD.exec(analysis)?.[1]?.toLowerCase();\n  if (first !== 'select' && first !== 'with') {\n    return 'Must be a read-only SELECT / WITH query.';\n  }\n\n  const words = analysis.toLowerCase().match(WORD) ?? [];\n  const forbidden = words.find((w) => FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS.has(w));\n  if (forbidden) return `Must be read-only; remove “${forbidden}”.`;\n\n  return null;\n}\n"
}

1	import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react';
2	
3	/** Three-state result of an async fetch. */
4	export type AsyncState<T> =
5	  | { status: 'loading' }
6	  | { status: 'ok'; data: T }
7	  | { status: 'error'; error: string };
8	
9	/**
10	 * Fetch on mount (and on `reload()`), with a cancelled-guard so a late
11	 * resolution after unmount doesn't set state, and rejection normalised to a
12	 * string `error`. Shared by the data pages (Home, Connections, …) so the
13	 * cancelled-effect dance lives in one place rather than being re-derived per page.
14	 *
15	 * `reload` re-runs the fetcher (e.g. after a mutation) while keeping the current
16	 * data visible until the refetch resolves — no flash back to the loading state.
17	 */
18	export function useAsyncData<T>(fetcher: () => Promise<T>): {
19	  state: AsyncState<T>;
20	  reload: () => void;
21	} {
22	  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T>>({ status: 'loading' });
23	  const [nonce, setNonce] = useState(0);
24	
25	  useEffect(() => {
26	    let cancelled = false;
27	    fetcher()
28	      .then((data) => {
29	        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });
30	      })
31	      .catch((err: unknown) => {
32	        if (!cancelled) {
33	          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
34	        }
35	      });
36	    return () => {
37	      cancelled = true;
38	    };
39	    // Re-run on mount and whenever `reload` bumps the nonce; the fetcher identity
40	    // is intentionally not a dependency.
41	    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
42	  }, [nonce]);
43	
44	  const reload = useCallback(() => setNonce((n) => n + 1), []);
45	  return { state, reload };
46	}
47

{

  "content": "import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';\n\nimport {\n  CUSTOM_SQL_EXPECTATION_TYPE,\n  isCustomSql,\n  validateCustomSqlQuery,\n} from '../../src/components/checks/customSql';\n\n/**\n * Client-side mirror of the backend custom-SQL guardrail (ADR 0019). The backend\n * `validate_query` is authoritative; this is the inline editor pre-check. Mirrors\n * the backend battery's hostile cases so the two don't drift on what they reject.\n */\n\nconst VALID = [\n  'SELECT * FROM {batch} WHERE amount IS NULL',\n  'select count(*) from {batch}',\n  'WITH t AS (SELECT * FROM {batch}) SELECT * FROM t WHERE n > 0',\n  'SELECT 1 FROM {batch};', // single trailing semicolon is fine\n  '(SELECT * FROM {batch}) UNION (SELECT * FROM {batch})',\n  \"SELECT replace(name, 'a', 'b') AS r FROM {batch} WHERE action <> 'delete'\",\n  \"SELECT * FROM {batch} WHERE note = 'a;b'\", // ';' inside a string\n  'SELECT * FROM {batch} -- drop table evil\\nWHERE 1 = 1', // keyword in a comment\n];\n\nconst INVALID = [\n  '',\n  '   ',\n  '-- just a comment',\n  'DELETE FROM {batch}',\n  'UPDATE {batch} SET x = 1',\n  'DROP TABLE secrets',\n  'INSERT INTO t VALUES (1)',\n  'SELECT * INTO new_table FROM {batch}',\n  'SELECT 1 FROM a; SELECT 2 FROM b', // two statements\n  'SELECT 1 FROM {batch}; DROP TABLE x',\n  'WITH t AS (INSERT INTO x VALUES (1) RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM t', // CTE DML\n  \"SELECT 1 FROM {batch} WHERE x = 'a--'; DROP TABLE y\", // '--' in a string masks nothing\n  'SELECT 1 FROM {batch} /* unterminated ; DROP TABLE y', // unterminated comment → fail closed\n  \"SELECT 1 FROM {batch} WHERE n = 'unterminated ; DROP\", // unterminated string → fail closed\n  'SELECT 1 FROM {batch} WHERE x = 1 `; DROP TABLE y; SELECT *`', // backtick is not a quote\n];\n\ndescribe('validateCustomSqlQuery', () => {\n  it.each(VALID)('accepts %j', (q) => {\n    expect(validateCustomSqlQuery(q)).toBeNull();\n  });\n\n  it.each(INVALID)('rejects %j', (q) => {\n    expect(validateCustomSqlQuery(q)).not.toBeNull();\n  });\n\n  it('reports the offending keyword in the message', () => {\n    expect(validateCustomSqlQuery('SELECT 1 FROM {batch} WHERE drop = 1')).toContain('drop');\n  });\n\n  it('handles a huge trailing-whitespace query without hanging', () => {\n    // Guards against a polynomial-ReDoS in the trailing strip (the backend hit\n    // this — str-based / anchored linear regex, not catastrophic backtracking).\n    expect(validateCustomSqlQuery('SELECT 1 FROM {batch}' + '\\t'.repeat(50_000))).toBeNull();\n  });\n});\n\ndescribe('isCustomSql', () => {\n  it('matches only the custom-SQL expectation type', () => {\n    expect(isCustomSql(CUSTOM_SQL_EXPECTATION_TYPE)).toBe(true);\n    expect(isCustomSql('unexpected_rows_expectation')).toBe(true);\n    expect(isCustomSql('expect_column_values_to_not_be_null')).toBe(false);\n    expect(isCustomSql(undefined)).toBe(false);\n  });\n});\n"
}

This is all clean. Now let me do a final careful check on the one remaining genuine concern: the `CheckDrawer` edit-mode prefill. When editing an existing custom-SQL check, `configToForm` runs on `EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[check.expectation_type]` with `check.config`. The sql field goes through the `else`-equivalent branch: `field.type === 'list' && Array.isArray(value) ? ... : value` → returns `value` (the query string). So prefill works. 

Let me verify one thing about edit-mode and the lazy chunk: when `CheckDrawer` opens with a custom-SQL check, `form.setFieldsValue` sets `config.unexpected_rows_query`. The `SqlEditorControl` mounts via Suspense. While the chunk loads, antd holds the value. When Monaco mounts, it receives `value`. Good — no prefill loss.

I've thoroughly traced all five points. The code is genuinely clean — typecheck passes, tests pass, value plumbing is correct, the validator rejects empty on submit, conversions handle 'sql' via the string path, and the worker/loader setup is the standard documented Vite pattern that's safe under repeated mounts. The only observations are minor/non-blocking robustness notes rather than correctness bugs. Let me report.

Based on my full review — reading all the files, tracing the form↔config conversions, checking the validator semantics, and confirming `tsc --noEmit` and the 58 vitest cases pass — I did not find correctness bugs in the five hunted areas. Here is the trace that cleared each:

1. **Suspense plumbing (clean):** `SqlEditorControl` is the direct `Form.Item` child, so antd injects `value`/`onChange` into it and it forwards both to `LazySqlEditor`. antd holds the field value in its store independent of the rendered control, so during the Suspense fallback the value is preserved and reaches Monaco on mount; edit-mode prefill (`setFieldsValue` before chunk loads) survives the same way. No onChange-before-mount race (Monaco only fires onChange after it mounts).
2. **Worker/loader (clean):** module top-level `self.MonacoEnvironment` + `loader.config({ monaco })` run once (module is import-cached), so repeated lazy mounts / drawer reopen don't re-run them; ordering is guaranteed since both live in the same module as `<Editor>`. Browser-only Vite app, no SSR path touches `self`.
3. **'sql' conversions (clean):** `field.type === 'sql'` falls through the `else` branch in both `formToConfig` (`config[name] = value`) and `configToForm` (the non-list ternary returns `value`), i.e. it behaves exactly like `'string'`. Query is passed through on save and prefilled on edit.
4. **Empty/required (clean):** both surfaces validate via `validateFields()` (drawer) / `onFinish` (CheckNew), which validate all name-registered fields regardless of touched state; `validateCustomSqlQuery('')` returns `'Enter a SQL query.'`, so empty is rejected on submit.
5. **onChange undefined (clean):** `onChange?.(next ?? '')` correctly coerces Monaco's possible `undefined` to `''`, so clearing the editor stores `''` and the validator sees an empty string (rejected).

Minor non-blocking observations (not correctness bugs, not returned as findings):
- No component-level render test exercises the actual `SqlEditorControl`→Monaco value injection or the empty-submit rejection; coverage is only on the pure `validateCustomSqlQuery`. Worth a `CheckDrawer`/`CheckNew` test that mounts the sql field (mocking the lazy editor) to lock the plumbing.
- An untracked local scratch file `frontend/tests/components/_scratch_customsql.test.ts` exists in the working tree but is not part of `main...HEAD`, so it is out of scope for this diff.

**PR3 merged — the Monaco custom-SQL editor is on `main`** (`1d53e94`). The full SQL-editor feature is now complete end-to-end.

## The SQL editor, shipped across 2 PRs
- **#258 (backend)** — custom-SQL via GX `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` (ADR 0019), read-only guardrail on every authoring + execution path.
- **#259 (frontend)** — the "Custom SQL" category with a lazy, locally-bundled Monaco editor, a client-side validation mirror, and datasource gating in both the create page and edit drawer.

## What the layered review caught (and would've shipped otherwise)
- **#258:** 4 fail-open/security bugs — dry-run bypass, unterminated-string swallow, backtick hiding-spot, and a CodeQL-found ReDoS.
- **#259:** 2 real gating-edge bugs — the edit-drawer orphaning a custom-SQL check during the connection-load window, and CheckNew degrading the whole page on an unreadable connection.

Every PR went through spawned `/code-review` agents + the now-enforced 12-check CI gate (held for CodeQL each time), with `fixup:` commits + plain pushes.

=== current mutmut config ===

=== requirements-mutation.txt ===
mutmut==2.5.0

=== CONTRIBUTING rule 4a (mutmut section) ===
14:   **4a. Test for failure modes, not just the happy path.** Lesson from the column-profiler bugs ([#145](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/145)/[#147](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/147)): the profiler sat at ~94% line coverage and still `500`d on a mixed-type column — *line coverage measures lines, not input space*. So:
18:   - **Periodic mutation spikes** on critical pure modules to find *covered-but-unasserted* logic (e.g. an over-narrow `except`): `pip install -r backend/requirements-mutation.txt` then `mutmut run --paths-to-mutate <file> --tests-dir backend/tests/<area> --runner "python -m pytest -x -q --no-cov <unit-test-file>"`. Manual/periodic — **not** a CI gate (too slow). `mutmut` is pinned in its **own** `requirements-mutation.txt`, deliberately **not** `-r`'d by `requirements-dev.txt`, so it stays off CI's install + `pip-audit` merge-gate surface.
19:     - **Reading survivors on Python 3.13:** `mutmut results` / `mutmut show` crash on 3.13 (mutmut 2.5.0's pony-ORM decompiler chokes on 3.13 bytecode — [#253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/253)); `mutmut run` is unaffected. Query the cache it writes instead — `sqlite3 .mutmut-cache` then `select s.filename, l.line_number, l.line from Mutant m join Line l on m.line=l.id join SourceFile s on l.sourcefile=s.id where m.status != 'killed';` — and `mutmut apply <id>` (to materialize a survivor on disk) still works. Sanity-check each survivor: a mutated **type annotation** (e.g. `| None` → `& None`) is an equivalent mutant, not a gap.
20:   - **Frontend mutation spikes (Stryker)** are the same idea for pure TS (conversion/resolver utils — `suiteTarget.ts`, `checkForm.ts`, …): `frontend/mutation/run.sh [--mutate '<glob>']`. Like mutmut, it's **manual/periodic, not CI**; Stryker is kept **out of `frontend/package.json`** (off the `pnpm audit` gate) — the script installs it ad-hoc (pinned) and restores the manifest on exit. Config in `frontend/stryker.conf.json`; details + survivor-triage notes in [`frontend/mutation/README.md`](frontend/mutation/README.md).
```

Working tree clean, env restored to the committed mutmut 2.5.0 pin. Here's the honest checkpoint — **"upgrade mutmut to 3.x" turns out to be a breaking rewrite, not a version bump.**

What I verified by actually running 3.6.0:
- ✅ **3.x drops pony-ORM** (the exact cause of the #253 `results`/`show` crash on 3.13) — so the direction genuinely fixes #253.
- ❌ But 3.x is incompatible with our current setup in three ways:
  1. **CLI gone:** `--paths-to-mutate / --tests-dir / --runner` flags were removed — the exact invocation documented in CONTRIBUTING rule 4a no longer exists. Config is file-only (`[mutmut]` `source_paths` + `pytest_add_cli_args*`).
  2. **New execution model:** it copies `source_paths` into a `mutants/` dir, `chdir`s into it, and runs tests *there* — so the whole importable `app/` package **plus** the tests + conftest must be copied in via `also_copy`. That's a structural change from 2.5.0's in-place per-file mutation (and it broke every run until I traced it to the `change_cwd("mutants")` model).
  3. **Cache obsolete:** the `.mutmut-cache` SQLite workaround we documented for #253 no longer applies (different results store).

So a clean adoption = write a new `[mutmut]` config (copy app + tests into mutants/), re-establish a per-file spike workflow, rewrite CONTRIBUTING rule 4a end-to-end, bump `requirements-mutation.txt`, and close #253 — a real chunk of work, versus the one-line bump #266 implied.

=== copy_also_copy_files body (does it skip existing / clobber?) ===
def copy_also_copy_files() -> None:
    assert isinstance(Config.get().also_copy, list)
    for path in Config.get().also_copy:
        print("     also copying", path)
        path = Path(path)
        destination = Path("mutants") / path
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        if path.is_file():
            shutil.copy2(path, destination)
        else:
            shutil.copytree(path, destination, dirs_exist_ok=True)


def create_mutants_for_file(filename: Path, output_path: Path) -> FileMutationResult:
    warnings: list[Warning] = []

    try:
        source_mtime = os.path.getmtime(filename)
        mutant_mtime = os.path.getmtime(output_path)
        # We have three possible cases here:
        # source_mtime > mutant_mtime: the source file was modified after the mutant has been created
        # source_mtime == mutant_mtime: only copied, otherwise the mutant file is untouched
        # source_mtime < mutant_mtime: the mutations have been saved after copying; source file untouched
        if source_mtime < mutant_mtime:
            # reset the mutation stats
            source_file_mutation_data = SourceFileMutationData(path=filename)
            source_file_mutation_data.load()

14	   **4a. Test for failure modes, not just the happy path.** Lesson from the column-profiler bugs ([#145](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/145)/[#147](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/147)): the profiler sat at ~94% line coverage and still `500`d on a mixed-type column — *line coverage measures lines, not input space*. So:
15	   - **Adversarial inputs for data-ingesting code.** Any function that processes external data (a file, a DataFrame, a user query) gets swept with the shared hostile-input battery in [`backend/tests/support/adversarial.py`](backend/tests/support/adversarial.py) — mixed types, unhashable cells, NaN/Inf, bytes, empty, and **both numpy & pyarrow backends** (they raise different exception types). The contract: *never raise, emit plain JSON* (`assert_json_safe`).
16	   - **Don't mock the seam you're validating.** If the behaviour under test lives inside a function you stub, the test proves nothing about it — exercise the real path (or at least assert the error mapping) for negative cases like a missing credential.
17	   - **An independent lens on negative paths.** A test written alongside the code shares its blind spots; let `/code-review` (or a second pass) scrutinise the failure-mode tests, not just the happy ones.
18	   - **Periodic mutation spikes** on critical pure modules to find *covered-but-unasserted* logic (e.g. an over-narrow `except`): `pip install -r backend/requirements-mutation.txt` then `mutmut run --paths-to-mutate <file> --tests-dir backend/tests/<area> --runner "python -m pytest -x -q --no-cov <unit-test-file>"`. Manual/periodic — **not** a CI gate (too slow). `mutmut` is pinned in its **own** `requirements-mutation.txt`, deliberately **not** `-r`'d by `requirements-dev.txt`, so it stays off CI's install + `pip-audit` merge-gate surface.
19	     - **Reading survivors on Python 3.13:** `mutmut results` / `mutmut show` crash on 3.13 (mutmut 2.5.0's pony-ORM decompiler chokes on 3.13 bytecode — [#253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/253)); `mutmut run` is unaffected. Query the cache it writes instead — `sqlite3 .mutmut-cache` then `select s.filename, l.line_number, l.line from Mutant m join Line l on m.line=l.id join SourceFile s on l.sourcefile=s.id where m.status != 'killed';` — and `mutmut apply <id>` (to materialize a survivor on disk) still works. Sanity-check each survivor: a mutated **type annotation** (e.g. `| None` → `& None`) is an equivalent mutant, not a gap.
20	   - **Frontend mutation spikes (Stryker)** are the same idea for pure TS (conversion/resolver utils — `suiteTarget.ts`, `checkForm.ts`, …): `frontend/mutation/run.sh [--mutate '<glob>']`. Like mutmut, it's **manual/periodic, not CI**; Stryker is kept **out of `frontend/package.json`** (off the `pnpm audit` gate) — the script installs it ad-hoc (pinned) and restores the manifest on exit. Config in `frontend/stryker.conf.json`; details + survivor-triage notes in [`frontend/mutation/README.md`](frontend/mutation/README.md).
21	5. **Definition of Done (DoD)** per task:

Found it: in 0.5.x the plugin became an ESM module — `require()` now returns `{ __esModule, default, reactRefresh }`, so our `eslint.config.cjs` was passing the *interop wrapper* (no top-level `.rules`) as the plugin. The rule still exists under `.default`. The fix is a one-line import change. Let me read and fix.

    - **Adversarial inputs for data-ingesting code.** Any function that processes external data (a file, a DataFrame, a user query) gets swept with the shared hostile-input battery in [`backend/tests/support/adversarial.py`](backend/tests/support/adversarial.py) — mixed types, unhashable cells, NaN/Inf, bytes, empty, and **both numpy & pyarrow backends** (they raise different exception types). The contract: *never raise, emit plain JSON* (`assert_json_safe`).
    - **Don't mock the seam you're validating.** If the behaviour under test lives inside a function you stub, the test proves nothing about it — exercise the real path (or at least assert the error mapping) for negative cases like a missing credential.
    - **An independent lens on negative paths.** A test written alongside the code shares its blind spots; let `/code-review` (or a second pass) scrutinise the failure-mode tests, not just the happy ones.
-   - **Periodic mutation spikes** on critical pure modules to find *covered-but-unasserted* logic (e.g. an over-narrow `except`): `pip install -r backend/requirements-mutation.txt` then `mutmut run --paths-to-mutate <file> --tests-dir backend/tests/<area> --runner "python -m pytest -x -q --no-cov <unit-test-file>"`. Manual/periodic — **not** a CI gate (too slow). `mutmut` is pinned in its **own** `requirements-mutation.txt`, deliberately **not** `-r`'d by `requirements-dev.txt`, so it stays off CI's install + `pip-audit` merge-gate surface.
-     - **Reading survivors on Python 3.13:** `mutmut results` / `mutmut show` crash on 3.13 (mutmut 2.5.0's pony-ORM decompiler chokes on 3.13 bytecode — [#253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/253)); `mutmut run` is unaffected. Query the cache it writes instead — `sqlite3 .mutmut-cache` then `select s.filename, l.line_number, l.line from Mutant m join Line l on m.line=l.id join SourceFile s on l.sourcefile=s.id where m.status != 'killed';` — and `mutmut apply <id>` (to materialize a survivor on disk) still works. Sanity-check each survivor: a mutated **type annotation** (e.g. `| None` → `& None`) is an equivalent mutant, not a gap.
+   - **Periodic mutation spikes** on critical pure modules to find *covered-but-unasserted* logic (e.g. an over-narrow `except`). Per spike, point `source_paths` at the one module you're spiking and narrow `pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection` to its tests, then `pip install -r backend/requirements-mutation.txt` and run **from the repo root**:
+     ```bash
+     mutmut run            # mutate + run; copies the tree into ./mutants/ (gitignored) and runs pytest there
+     mutmut results        # list survivors (🙁) — works natively on 3.13 again (see below)
+     mutmut show <name>    # diff one survivor, e.g. backend.app.services.custom_sql.x_validate_query__mutmut_44

+     - **Why the config looks the way it does:** 3.x copies `source_paths` into `./mutants/`, `chdir`s in, and runs pytest there — so `also_copy` must bring the whole importable package + tests (+ `pyproject.toml`), and `pytest_add_cli_args = ["-o", "addopts="]` strips the repo's `--cov` flags (mutmut runs its own coverage plugin; a second `--cov` is a pytest *usage error* in-process, exit 4).

Sanity-check each survivor: a mutated **type annotation** (e.g. `| None` → `& None`) or an unasserted-detail string (e.g. a dict key) is an equivalent/uninteresting mutant, not a real gap.

All four steps done and the board is clean — **0 open PRs, 0 open security alerts, `main` clean**. Here's the full rundown of the triage execution.

## What shipped (8 PRs merged, 1 closed)

**Step 1 — Dependabot queue.** Merged the 9 green PRs (#263, #264, #267, #268, #269, #271, #272, #273). Merging #271 surfaced that the **end-of-week audit gate had gone red on `main`** from two freshly-published advisories — that became the critical path:

**Security sweep (#276)** — filed #274/#275, fixed and verified:
- `cryptography 46.0.7 → 48.0.1` (GHSA-537c…) + `msal 1.32.3 → 1.37.0` (lifts the `cryptography<47` cap I caught via `pip check`)
- `form-data 4.0.5 → 4.0.6` (high, CRLF injection, transitive via axios)
- `dompurify → 3.4.10` + `js-yaml → 4.2.0` via `pnpm.overrides` — cleared the remaining 16 transitive alerts. **All 17 Dependabot alerts now closed.** (Caught the local-pnpm-11-vs-CI-pnpm-9 override-location trap en route.)

**Step 2 — mutmut 3.x (#277, closes #253).** This was a breaking rewrite, not a bump, as you approved. New `[tool.mutmut]` config (copies the tree into `mutants/` + `chdir`s in to run; `also_copy` + `-o addopts=` to dodge the in-process double-`--cov` usage error), `requirements-mutation.txt → 3.6.0`, `.gitignore`, and a full CONTRIBUTING rule 4a rewrite. Verified end-to-end (`run`/`results`/`show` all crash-free on 3.13 — 185 mutants). Closed #266 as superseded.

**Step 3 — the two blocked PRs.** #265 (structlog 25→26: synced the pre-commit hook + ran the full backend suite, 440 passed) and #270 (eslint-plugin-react-refresh 0.5.x: it ships ESM now, so `require(...).default`). Both fixed, reviewed, merged.

**Step 4 — re-milestoned** the 6 Week-4 P3 cleanups (#197, #199, #204, #229, #236, #237) to Backlog. Week 4 now holds only real bugs: **#240, #235, #192**.

## On your code-review question
You were right to flag it. I ran proper **agent** reviews on all three open PRs: #277 surfaced a real stale-id comment (`mutmut id=155` → meaningless under 3.x named mutants), which I fixed; #265 and #270 came back clean. The honest gap: **#276 and #271 merged before I reviewed them** — #271 was a patch, but #276 touched dependency logic and I leaned on heavy verification instead of the review step. Won't repeat that ordering.

Bash-tool commands are initialized from the user's Fish profile, so common bash-isms fail:\n\n- **Unquoted glob flags error.** `grep --include=*.md` → `no matches found: --include=*.md`. Quote them: `grep --include=\"*.md\"`.\n- **`timeout` is absent** (no GNU coreutils by default on macOS) → `command not found: timeout`. Use the Bash tool's `run_in_background` instead of wrapping in `timeout`.\n- **Avoid `cd /path && cmd` chaining** and chained `sleep` (the harness blocks long/compound sleeps); prefer absolute paths and `run_in_background` + Monitor for waits.\n\n**Why:** several commands broke exactly this way during the 2026-06-15 PR-triage session.\n**How to apply:** prefer the dedicated file/search tools; when writing Bash, quote globs, never use `timeout`, and pass absolute paths rather than `cd &&`.\n"
}

185	function AddCollaborator({
186	  suiteId,
187	  excludedIds,
188	  onAdded,
189	}: {
190	  suiteId: string;
191	  /** Owner + already-shared users — hidden from the picker (backend rejects them too). */
192	  excludedIds: string[];
193	  onAdded: () => void;
194	}) {
195	  const { message } = App.useApp();
196	  const [options, setOptions] = useState<UserSummary[]>([]);
197	  const [searching, setSearching] = useState(false);
198	  const [userId, setUserId] = useState<string>();
199	  const [permission, setPermission] = useState<SharePermission>('view');
200	  const [adding, setAdding] = useState(false);
201	  const timer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(undefined);
202	  // Monotonic token so a slow earlier search can't overwrite a newer one's
203	  // results (last-wins); unmount bumps it to a sentinel to drop any in-flight
204	  // response, and clears the pending debounce so it never fires post-unmount.
205	  const latest = useRef(0);
206	  useEffect(
207	    () => () => {
208	      clearTimeout(timer.current);
209	      latest.current = -1;
210	    },
211	    [],
212	  );
213	
214	  // Debounce the directory query so a fast typist fires one search, not one per
215	  // keystroke. The 2-char floor mirrors the backend (a shorter query returns []).
216	  const onSearch = (raw: string) => {
217	    const q = raw.trim();
218	    clearTimeout(timer.current);
219	    if (q.length < 2) {
220	      setOptions([]);
221	      setSearching(false); // a pending debounce was cancelled — drop its spinner
222	      return;
223	    }
224	    setSearching(true);
225	    const token = (latest.current += 1);
226	    timer.current = setTimeout(() => {
227	      searchUsers(q)
228	        .then((users) => {
229	          if (token !== latest.current) return; // superseded by a newer search
230	          setOptions(users.filter((u) => !excludedIds.includes(u.id)));
231	        })
232	        .catch(() => {
233	          if (token === latest.current) setOptions([]);
234	        })
235	        .finally(() => {
236	          if (token === latest.current) setSearching(false);
237	        });
238	    }, 300);
239	  };

241	  const onAdd = async () => {
242	    if (!userId) return;
243	    setAdding(true);

25	/**
26	 * Import a portable suite document (the JSON produced by "Export") onto a chosen
27	 * connection. The file is parsed + shape-checked client-side, then handed back to
28	 * the backend unchanged (`POST /suites/import`) so thresholds/config round-trip
29	 * exactly — the connection is the only thing the importer supplies. The new suite
30	 * is owned by the importing user, like create.
31	 */
32	export function ImportSuiteDrawer({
33	  open,
34	  connections,
35	  onClose,
36	  onImported,
37	}: {
38	  open: boolean;
39	  /** Datasource connections the document can be imported onto. */
40	  connections: Connection[];
41	  onClose: () => void;
42	  onImported: (suite: Suite) => void;
43	}) {
44	  const { message } = App.useApp();
45	  // A suite imports onto a datasource — orchestration providers (ADF/Airflow)
46	  // are never queryable, so they can't back a suite (CLAUDE.md §4, #242).
47	  const datasourceConnections = connections.filter((c) => CONNECTION_KIND[c.type] === 'datasource');
48	  const [connectionId, setConnectionId] = useState<string>();
49	  const [doc, setDoc] = useState<SuiteDocument | null>(null);
50	  const [fileName, setFileName] = useState<string>();
51	  const [parseError, setParseError] = useState<string>();
52	  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
53	
54	  // Reset everything when the drawer (re)opens — a stale document/connection from
55	  // a previous (possibly cancelled) import must not leak into the next one. The
56	  // Drawer host stays mounted across open/close (it isn't destroyed), so this is
57	  // a render-phase "adjust state when a prop changes" reset, matching the editor
58	  // panels — not an effect.
59	  const [prevOpen, setPrevOpen] = useState(open);
60	  if (open !== prevOpen) {
61	    setPrevOpen(open);
62	    if (open) {
63	      setConnectionId(undefined);
64	      setDoc(null);
65	      setFileName(undefined);
66	      setParseError(undefined);
67	    }
68	  }
69	
70	  // Parse + shape-check the dropped file; return false so antd never uploads it.
71	  const onFile = (file: File) => {
72	    file
73	      .text()
74	      .then((text) => {
75	        const parsed = parseSuiteDocument(text);
76	        setDoc(parsed);
77	        setFileName(file.name);
78	        setParseError(undefined);
79	      })
80	      .catch((err: unknown) => {
81	        setDoc(null);
82	        setFileName(file.name);
83	        setParseError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Could not read the file.');
84	      });
85	    return false;
86	  };
87	
88	  const onSubmit = async () => {
89	    if (!doc || !connectionId) return;
90	    setSubmitting(true);
91	    try {
92	      const suite = await importSuite({ connection_id: connectionId, document: doc });
93	      message.success(`${suite.name}: imported`);
94	      onImported(suite);
95	    } catch (err) {
96	      message.error(`Import failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
97	    } finally {
98	      setSubmitting(false);
99	    }
100	  };
101	
102	  const fileList: UploadFile[] = fileName
103	    ? [{ uid: '1', name: fileName, status: parseError ? 'error' : 'done' }]
104	    : [];
105	
106	  return (
107	    <Drawer
108	      title="Import suite"
109	      open={open}
110	      onClose={onClose}
111	      width={480}
112	      destroyOnHidden
113	      extra={
114	        <Flex gap={8}>
115	          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
116	          <Button
117	            type="primary"
118	            loading={submitting}
119	            disabled={!doc || !connectionId}
120	            onClick={onSubmit}
121	          >
122	            Import
123	          </Button>
124	        </Flex>
125	      }
126	    >
127	      <Flex vertical gap={16}>
128	        <Upload.Dragger
129	          accept="application/json,.json"
130	          multiple={false}
131	          maxCount={1}
132	          beforeUpload={onFile}
133	          fileList={fileList}
134	          onRemove={() => {
135	            setDoc(null);
136	            setFileName(undefined);
137	            setParseError(undefined);
138	          }}
139	        >
140	          <p className="ant-upload-drag-icon">
141	            <InboxOutlined />
142	          </p>
143	          <p className="ant-upload-text">Click or drag a suite export (.json) here</p>
144	          <p className="ant-upload-hint">
145	            A document produced by “Export” on any suite — checks, thresholds and config.
146	          </p>
147	        </Upload.Dragger>
148	
149	        {parseError && (
150	          <Alert type="error" showIcon message="Invalid document" description={parseError} />
151	        )}
152	
153	        {doc && (
154	          <Descriptions size="small" column={1} bordered styles={{ label: { width: 120 } }}>
155	            <Descriptions.Item label="Name">{doc.name}</Descriptions.Item>
156	            <Descriptions.Item label="Checks">{doc.checks.length}</Descriptions.Item>
157	            {doc.description && (
158	              <Descriptions.Item label="Description">{doc.description}</Descriptions.Item>
159	            )}
160	          </Descriptions>
161	        )}
162	
163	        <Form layout="vertical">
164	          <Form.Item
165	            label="Import onto connection"
166	            required
167	            extra="The imported suite runs against this connection’s datasource."
168	          >
169	            <Select
170	              value={connectionId}
171	              onChange={setConnectionId}
172	              placeholder="Select a datasource connection"
173	              options={datasourceConnections.map((c) => ({
174	                value: c.id,
175	                label: `${c.name} · ${CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[c.type]} · ${envLabel(c.env)}`,
176	              }))}
177	            />
178	          </Form.Item>
179	        </Form>
180	
181	        {datasourceConnections.length === 0 && (
182	          <Typography.Text type="secondary">
183	            Create a datasource connection first — a suite must import onto one.
184	          </Typography.Text>
185	        )}
186	      </Flex>
187	    </Drawer>
188	  );
189	}
190	
191	/**
192	 * Parse the uploaded text as a suite export document, validating just enough of
193	 * the shape to fail fast on the wrong file (a random JSON, a half-document). The
194	 * object is otherwise passed through untouched so thresholds/config round-trip
195	 * exactly on import. Throws an `Error` with a user-facing message on any miss.
196	 */
197	function parseSuiteDocument(text: string): SuiteDocument {
198	  let parsed: unknown;
199	  try {
200	    parsed = JSON.parse(text);
201	  } catch {
202	    throw new Error('Not valid JSON.');
203	  }
204	  if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') {
205	    throw new Error('Expected a suite document object.');
206	  }
207	  const obj = parsed as Record<string, unknown>;
208	  if (typeof obj.name !== 'string' || !obj.name) {
209	    throw new Error('Missing a suite “name” — is this a suite export?');
210	  }
211	  if (!Array.isArray(obj.checks)) {
212	    throw new Error('Missing a “checks” list — is this a suite export?');
213	  }
214	  return parsed as SuiteDocument;
215	}

The\n  // Drawer host stays mounted across open/close (it isn't destroyed), so this is\n  // a render-phase \"adjust state when a prop changes\" reset, matching the editor\n  // panels — not an effect.\n  const [prevOpen, setPrevOpen] = useState(open);\n  if (open !== prevOpen) {\n    setPrevOpen(open);\n    if (open) {\n      latestFile.current += 1;\n      setConnectionId(undefined);\n      setDoc(null);\n      setFileName(undefined);\n      setParseError(undefined);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Parse + shape-check the dropped file; return false so antd never uploads it.\n  const onFile = (file: File) => {\n    const token = (latestFile.current += 1);\n    file\n      .text()\n      .then((text) => {\n        if (token !== latestFile.current) return; // superseded by a newer pick\n        const parsed = parseSuiteDocument(text);\n        setDoc(parsed);\n        setFileName(file.name);\n        setParseError(undefined);\n      })\n      .catch((err: unknown) => {\n        if (token !== latestFile.current) return; // superseded by a newer pick\n        setDoc(null);\n        setFileName(file.name);\n        setParseError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Could not read the file.');\n      });\n    return false;\n  };"
}

The viewer is led to believe they could change everyone else's access but are specially blocked from changing their own — false; they have no management rights at all. The lock+tooltip semantics are only correct for a manager (admin/owner); for a viewer the '· You' tag is fine but the tooltip is inaccurate. Consider gating the tooltip text on canManage."
  },

When they differ, `share.email.toLowerCase() === currentEmail.toLowerCase()` is false, isSelf stays false, and a non-owner admin still gets a live Remove button / permission Select on their own row — they can self-revoke and brick the panel (the exact #240 bug). The fix is best-effort because the frontend has no current-user user_id/oid to match on; a robust fix needs the backend to flag the self row (e.g. an is_self field or exposing the caller's user_id) rather than client-side email matching."
  }
]

Notes on the other two bugs (no findings):

- **ImportSuiteDrawer re-pick race (#235):** Token sequence is correct. On first mount with `open=true` the effect bumps `latestFile.current` to 1 *before* any file pick; `onFile` then does `token = (latestFile.current += 1)` = 2 and compares against the same ref at resolve time, so the first file's parse is NOT dropped. The mount-time effect bump only invalidates parses that were in flight from a *prior* open, which is the intended last-wins/reopen guard. `onRemove` bumps correctly. No off-by-one. The component stays mounted across open/close (only the Drawer's inner content is `destroyOnHidden`), so the ref + render-phase reset cooperate cleanly.

- **Nav prefix match (#192):** Keys `/connections /suites /results /profile` are mutually non-prefixing, so no double-highlight is possible. All real sub-routes (`/connections/new`, `/suites/:id`, `/suites/:id/checks/new`) highlight their parent via the `${k}/` boundary check, and `/profile` highlights exactly. The fix is correct.

1	"""Suite sharing — grant / list / update / revoke per-user permissions.
2	
3	Managing shares requires `admin` on the suite (the owner always qualifies);
4	listing collaborators requires `view`. The target must be a real user and not
5	the suite's owner (the creator already has full, immutable access — a share row
6	for them would be meaningless). All authorization flows through
7	`suite_authz.require_permission`, so a caller without access gets a 404 (hidden)
8	and one with insufficient level gets a 403.
9	
10	FastAPI-free: takes a `Session` + ids; the API layer passes `current_user.id` as
11	the actor.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import uuid
17	
18	from sqlalchemy import select
19	from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
20	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, selectinload
21	
22	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
23	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
24	from backend.app.db.models import Share, User
25	from backend.app.services.suite_authz import require_permission
26	
27	log = get_logger(__name__)
28	
29	
30	class ShareNotFoundError(DataQError):
31	    status_code = 404
32	    code = "share_not_found"
33	
34	
35	class ShareConflictError(DataQError):
36	    status_code = 409
37	    code = "share_conflict"
38	
39	
40	class ShareTargetInvalidError(DataQError):
41	    status_code = 422
42	    code = "share_target_invalid"
43	
44	
45	def _get_share(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> Share:
46	    share = session.scalars(
47	        select(Share).where(Share.suite_id == suite_id, Share.user_id == user_id)
48	    ).first()
49	    if share is None:
50	        raise ShareNotFoundError(
51	            "no share for this user on this suite",
52	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "user_id": str(user_id)},
53	        )
54	    return share
55	
56	
57	def grant_share(
58	    session: Session,
59	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
60	    *,
61	    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
62	    target_user_id: uuid.UUID,
63	    permission: str,
64	) -> Share:
65	    """Grant `target_user_id` a permission on the suite. Actor needs `admin`."""
66	    suite = require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="admin")
67	    if target_user_id == suite.created_by:
68	        raise ShareTargetInvalidError(
69	            "cannot share a suite with its owner (already has full access)",
70	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "user_id": str(target_user_id)},
71	        )
72	    if session.get(User, target_user_id) is None:
73	        raise ShareTargetInvalidError(
74	            "target user does not exist", detail={"user_id": str(target_user_id)}
75	        )
76	
77	    share = Share(suite_id=suite_id, user_id=target_user_id, permission=permission)
78	    session.add(share)
79	    try:
80	        session.commit()
81	    except IntegrityError as exc:
82	        session.rollback()
83	        raise ShareConflictError(
84	            "user already has a share on this suite; use PATCH to change it",
85	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "user_id": str(target_user_id)},
86	        ) from exc
87	    session.refresh(share)
88	    log.info(
89	        "share_granted", suite_id=str(suite_id), user_id=str(target_user_id), permission=permission
90	    )
91	    return share
92	
93	
94	def list_shares(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID, *, actor_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[Share]:
95	    """List a suite's shares. Actor needs `view` (collaborators can see who else has access)."""
96	    require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="view")
97	    # Eager-load the grantee here (not model-wide) so the API can name each
98	    # collaborator without an N+1 — the only Share query that reads `.user`.
99	    return list(
100	        session.scalars(
101	            select(Share)
102	            .where(Share.suite_id == suite_id)
103	            .options(selectinload(Share.user))
104	            .order_by(Share.created_at)
105	        )
106	    )
107	
108	
109	def update_share(
110	    session: Session,
111	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
112	    target_user_id: uuid.UUID,
113	    *,
114	    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
115	    permission: str,
116	) -> Share:
117	    """Change a user's permission. Actor needs `admin`."""
118	    require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="admin")
119	    share = _get_share(session, suite_id, target_user_id)
120	    share.permission = permission
121	    session.commit()
122	    session.refresh(share)
123	    log.info(
124	        "share_updated", suite_id=str(suite_id), user_id=str(target_user_id), permission=permission
125	    )
126	    return share
127	
128	
129	def revoke_share(
130	    session: Session,
131	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
132	    target_user_id: uuid.UUID,
133	    *,
134	    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
135	) -> None:
136	    """Revoke a user's share. Actor needs `admin`."""
137	    require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="admin")
138	    share = _get_share(session, suite_id, target_user_id)
139	    session.delete(share)
140	    session.commit()
141	    log.info("share_revoked", suite_id=str(suite_id), user_id=str(target_user_id))
142

Done. The three Week-4 bugs are fixed, reviewed, and merged — **#240, #235, #192 all closed**. The Week-4 milestone now holds only the tracking epic #173 (which correctly stays open: the admin page + version-history drawer are still outstanding Week-4 work).

## What I did (PR #279)
I verified all three were genuinely **unfixed** before touching anything, then fixed each:

- **#240 (P2 bug)** — the important one. The `/code-review` agents caught that my initial frontend-only lock was the **wrong altitude**: the backend had *no* self-revoke guard, so a non-owner admin could still self-revoke via direct API/MCP and brick the panel. So I added the durable server-side guard (`share_service._reject_self_target`, rejecting `target == actor` in update + revoke), with 2 API tests **run against a real Postgres** (spun up a throwaway container — 676 backend tests pass). The frontend lock stays as best-effort UX, and I gated its tooltip on `canManage` so viewers don't see a misleading message.
- **#235 (P3 bug)** — generation-token guard on the async `file.text()` parse so a rapid re-pick can't land a stale document (same last-wins pattern as the share-search box).
- **#192 (P3)** — prefix-safe nav matching (exact or segment-boundary sub-path).

## Process notes
- Ran `/code-review` **before** merging (per your earlier reminder) — it found a real altitude gap + a misleading tooltip, both fixed in the PR rather than deferred.
- Added tests where they were clean (#240 self-lock front + back); dropped a fragile #235 UI race test that was exercising antd internals rather than the guard, and said so rather than ship a flaky test.
- 185 frontend + 676 backend tests green; lint/prettier/black/ruff/mypy all clean locally before push.

> AGENT

Quick correction first: **MUI isn't a Google product** — it's an independent company (MUI, formerly "Material-UI") that *implements* Google's Material Design spec. Google's own React-ish offering is Material Web Components, which you don't want here. So the real comparison is **Ant Design vs. MUI Core**.

## Is MUI suitable for DataQ?
Technically yes — it's mature, TypeScript-first, works fine with Vite. But for *this* app, Ant Design is actually the better-fit choice, and MUI would be a slight downgrade in fit:

- DataQ is a **dense enterprise/admin UI** (connection tables, suite lists, results grids, profiler panels, share management). AntD ships rich `Table`, `Form`, `Descriptions`, `Drawer` that cover exactly this out of the box.
- MUI shines for **brand-led, bespoke product UIs**. Its base `Table` is low-level; for the data grids you have (Results, Suites, pipeline-runs) you'd reach for **MUI X DataGrid** — and the good sorting/filtering features are gated behind the **paid Pro license**. AntD gives you those for free.

So there's no functional win to switching — if anything you lose ground on the data-heavy surfaces.

## How hard is the switch right now?
I checked the actual footprint. It's a **large, all-frontend rewrite** — not a swap:

| Area | Scope | Why it's painful |
|---|---|---|
| Component imports | **37 files**, ~38 distinct antd components | Every page/component touched |
| Imperative APIs | **60 call sites** of `App.useApp`/`message`/`Form.useForm`/`notification` | MUI has no equivalent — `message` → Snackbar/notistack (different model) |
| **Forms** (biggest) | `checkFormFields.tsx` + every drawer | AntD `Form`/`Form.Item`/`rules`/`useForm` is a whole declarative validation layer. **MUI has no form layer** — you'd add react-hook-form and rewrite all form logic |
| Search selects | `SharePanel`, connection pickers | AntD `Select showSearch/onSearch/filterOption` → MUI `Autocomplete` (different API & behavior) |
| Upload | `ImportSuiteDrawer` | AntD `Upload.Dragger` has **no MUI equivalent** — rebuild with react-dropzone |
| Theming | `theme.ts` + `ConfigProvider` in `App.tsx`/`main.tsx` | Full rewrite to MUI `createTheme`/`ThemeProvider` |
| **Tests** | **15 component test files** | They assert against antd's DOM (`role="combobox"`, List.Item structure, the `· You` tag). All need rewriting |

What *survives*: **Monaco** (independent of antd), your API layer, routing, and business logic. But the entire view + test layer is in scope.

Realistically that's **1–2 weeks of full-time frontend churn** with a high regression risk, landing right in the middle of your 8-week timeline (Week 4, with admin page + version-history drawer still to build).

## Recommendation
**Don't switch.** AntD is the better fit for an enterprise DQ console, and the migration is high-cost / zero functional gain at this stage. If MUI ever becomes a real requirement (e.g. a design-system mandate), treat it as a **deliberate post-v1 project** with its own ADR — not a Week-4 detour. Right now it'd just burn your remaining v1 runway.

Happy to sketch what a post-v1 migration ADR would look like if you ever want it on the books — but as a curiosity, the answer is "capable library, wrong time, no upside here."

> DEVELOPER

What about Material Web Components?

> AGENT

Material Web Components is a different beast from MUI, and for DataQ it's a **worse** fit — not better. Two things to untangle first, because the naming is a mess:

- **`@material/mwc-*`** ("Material Web Components", MWC) — the older generation. **Deprecated.**
- **`@material/web`** ("Material Web", M3) — the current Google library. This is what you'd actually evaluate.

## The dealbreakers for this project

**1. It's web components (Lit), not React.** `@material/web` ships custom elements, not React components. In a React + Vite app that means interop friction at every turn:
- Passing non-string props and wiring DOM events needs refs/`addEventListener` or thin wrappers (React's custom-element support only really got good in React 19; you're on the AntD/Vite stack).
- TypeScript/JSX typings for custom elements are clunky.
- **Forms are the killer** — custom elements integrate with forms via `ElementInternals`, which does *not* play nicely with the controlled-form patterns or react-hook-form you'd otherwise reach for. Your app is form-heavy (check editor, every drawer).

**2. It's incomplete — and missing exactly what you need.** `@material/web` has buttons, text fields, dialogs, menus, chips, etc., but **no data table, no rich date picker, thin navigation components.** DataQ is fundamentally tables + dense data (connections, suites, results, pipeline-runs, profiler). You'd be hand-building the most important surfaces *and* still bolting on a separate grid library. AntD gives all of that out of the box.

**3. Google has stepped back from it.** Material Web has been in a reduced/maintenance posture rather than active feature development. Adopting a stalling, intentionally-incomplete library for a v1 you're shipping in ~4 weeks is real maintenance risk — the opposite of what you want behind a product surface.

## Bottom line

| Option | Fit for DataQ | Migration cost now |
|---|---|---|
| **Ant Design** (current) | ✅ Best — dense enterprise tables/forms built in | — |
| MUI Core | 🟡 Capable, weaker on data grids (DataGrid Pro is paid) | High (1–2 wks, full FE rewrite) |
| Material Web (`@material/web`) | 🔴 Worst — web-components interop + missing data table + stalled | **Highest** (paradigm change *and* gap-filling) |

If MUI was "wrong time, no upside," Material Web is "wrong tool *and* wrong time." It's designed for greenfield Material Design 3 web apps that don't lean on rich data tables — basically the inverse of an enterprise DQ console. Keep AntD; it's genuinely the right choice for what DataQ is.

1	"""Check CRUD — checks are GX expectations nested under a suite.
2	
3	A check belongs to exactly one suite (FK + cascade). This layer validates the
4	suite exists, enforces the v1 monitor-kind limit, and treats the check's
5	`config` (the GX expectation kwargs) as free-form JSONB — per-expectation
6	schema validation against live data is the check dry-run path (a later Week-3
7	task), not CRUD.
8	
9	v1 monitor-kind limit (ADR 0012): although the schema CHECK reserves
10	`freshness / volume / schema_drift / anomaly / comparison`, v1 only *runs*
11	`expectation`. The API therefore refuses to author a non-`expectation` check —
12	a reserved kind is schema-valid for forward-compat but not yet runnable, so
13	letting a user create one would just produce a check that can never execute.
14	
15	FastAPI-free like the sibling services: takes a `Session`, returns ORM models,
16	raises `DataQError` subclasses.
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import uuid
22	from decimal import Decimal
23	from typing import Any
24	
25	from sqlalchemy import select
26	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

28	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
29	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
30	from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Suite
31	from backend.app.services.custom_sql import is_custom_sql, validate_custom_sql_check
32	from backend.app.services.suite_service import get_suite
33	
34	log = get_logger(__name__)
35	
36	# v1 authors only GX expectations; the other reserved kinds (ADR 0012) are
37	# schema-valid but have no runner yet, so CRUD refuses them.
38	_V1_SUPPORTED_KINDS = {"expectation"}
39	
40	
41	class CheckNotFoundError(DataQError):
42	    status_code = 404
43	    code = "check_not_found"
44	
45	
46	class CheckConfigInvalidError(DataQError):
47	    status_code = 422
48	    code = "check_config_invalid"

51	def _connection_type(session: Session, suite: Suite) -> str:
52	    """The datasource type of the suite's connection — for custom-SQL gating.
53	
54	    The suite's `connection_id` FK is NOT NULL, so the connection always exists.
55	    """
56	    connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)
57	    assert connection is not None
58	    return connection.type
59	
60	
61	def validate_kind(kind: str) -> None:
62	    """Reject a non-`expectation` kind (422). Shared by CRUD and suite import."""
63	    if kind not in _V1_SUPPORTED_KINDS:
64	        raise CheckConfigInvalidError(
65	            f"check kind {kind!r} is not supported in v1; only 'expectation'",
66	            detail={"kind": kind, "supported": sorted(_V1_SUPPORTED_KINDS)},
67	        )
68	
69	
70	def create_check(
71	    session: Session,
72	    *,
73	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
74	    name: str,
75	    kind: str,
76	    expectation_type: str,
77	    config: dict[str, Any],
78	    warn_threshold: Decimal | None,
79	    fail_threshold: Decimal | None,
80	    critical_threshold: Decimal | None,
81	) -> Check:
82	    """Create a check in a suite.
83	
84	    Raises `SuiteNotFoundError` (404) if the suite does not exist, or
85	    `CheckConfigInvalidError` (422) for an unsupported kind.
86	    """
87	    suite = get_suite(session, suite_id)  # 404 if the suite is missing
88	    validate_kind(kind)
89	    if is_custom_sql(expectation_type):
90	        validate_custom_sql_check(
91	            expectation_type=expectation_type,
92	            config=config,
93	            connection_type=_connection_type(session, suite),
94	        )
95	
96	    check = Check(
97	        suite_id=suite_id,
98	        name=name,
99	        kind=kind,
100	        expectation_type=expectation_type,
101	        config=config,
102	        warn_threshold=warn_threshold,
103	        fail_threshold=fail_threshold,
104	        critical_threshold=critical_threshold,
105	    )
106	    session.add(check)
107	    session.commit()
108	    session.refresh(check)
109	    log.info("check_created", check_id=str(check.id), suite_id=str(suite_id))
110	    return check

113	def list_checks(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[Check]:
114	    """List a suite's checks (404 if the suite does not exist)."""
115	    get_suite(session, suite_id)
116	    stmt = select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == suite_id).order_by(Check.created_at)
117	    return list(session.scalars(stmt))

120	def get_check(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID, check_id: uuid.UUID) -> Check:
121	    """Fetch a check, enforcing that it belongs to `suite_id` (else 404)."""
122	    check = session.get(Check, check_id)
123	    if check is None or check.suite_id != suite_id:
124	        raise CheckNotFoundError(
125	            "check not found",
126	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "check_id": str(check_id)},
127	        )
128	    return check

131	def update_check(
132	    session: Session,
133	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
134	    check_id: uuid.UUID,
135	    *,
136	    name: str | None = None,
137	    expectation_type: str | None = None,
138	    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
139	    warn_threshold: Decimal | None = None,
140	    fail_threshold: Decimal | None = None,
141	    critical_threshold: Decimal | None = None,
142	) -> Check:
143	    """Partial update. `suite_id` and `kind` are immutable.
144	
145	    Follows the codebase PATCH convention (connections / suites): a `None`
146	    argument means "not provided", so an omitted field is left unchanged. v1 has
147	    no clear-to-NULL path for thresholds; recreate the check to drop one.
148	    """
149	    check = get_check(session, suite_id, check_id)
150	    if name is not None:
151	        check.name = name
152	    if expectation_type is not None:
153	        check.expectation_type = expectation_type
154	    if config is not None:
155	        check.config = config
156	    if warn_threshold is not None:
157	        check.warn_threshold = warn_threshold
158	    if fail_threshold is not None:
159	        check.fail_threshold = fail_threshold
160	    if critical_threshold is not None:
161	        check.critical_threshold = critical_threshold
162	    # Re-validate against the post-patch state: a PATCH may change only the query
163	    # (config) or only the type, so guard the effective custom-SQL check before
164	    # commit (a rejected update persists nothing).

I've got the full shape now. The version-history drawer is genuinely backend-blocked: there's no history table, and [check_service.update_check](backend/app/services/check_service.py#L131) overwrites the row in place. So this is a backend-then-frontend build, not a frontend-only task. Here's the plan I'd execute:

**Backend (new PR):**
1. `CheckVersion` model + `check_versions` table — additive migration (backward-compatible: nothing else depends on it). Columns: `check_id` FK, `version_no`, snapshot of `name`/`expectation_type`/`config`/`kind`/thresholds, `changed_by` (user FK, nullable), `created_at`.
2. Snapshot wiring: write v1 in `create_check`, append a new version after each successful `update_check` (thread `actor_id` through the service + API, which I already have via `current_user`).
3. Read endpoint: `GET /suites/{suite_id}/checks/{check_id}/versions` (suite-authz `view`-gated), newest-first, with author display name.
4. Backend tests (against the throwaway Postgres, like the share tests).

**Frontend (follow-up PR):**
5. `listCheckVersions` in the check API, a `CheckHistoryDrawer` (version list → timestamp, author, config view), and a "History" trigger in [CheckDrawer.tsx](frontend/src/components/checks/CheckDrawer.tsx). Frontend tests.

def _in_check(column: str, values: tuple[str, ...], name: str) -> CheckConstraint:

  "old_string": "def create_check(\n    session: Session,\n    *,\n    suite_id: uuid.UUID,\n    name: str,\n    kind: str,\n    expectation_type: str,\n    config: dict[str, Any],\n    warn_threshold: Decimal | None,\n    fail_threshold: Decimal | None,\n    critical_threshold: Decimal | None,\n) -> Check:\n    \"\"\"Create a check in a suite.\n\n    Raises `SuiteNotFoundError` (404) if the suite does not exist, or\n    `CheckConfigInvalidError` (422) for an unsupported kind.\n    \"\"\"\n    suite = get_suite(session, suite_id)  # 404 if the suite is missing\n    validate_kind(kind)\n    if is_custom_sql(expectation_type):\n        validate_custom_sql_check(\n            expectation_type=expectation_type,\n            config=config,\n            connection_type=_connection_type(session, suite),\n        )\n\n    check = Check(\n        suite_id=suite_id,\n        name=name,\n        kind=kind,\n        expectation_type=expectation_type,\n        config=config,\n        warn_threshold=warn_threshold,\n        fail_threshold=fail_threshold,\n        critical_threshold=critical_threshold,\n    )\n    session.add(check)\n    session.commit()\n    session.refresh(check)\n    log.info(\"check_created\", check_id=str(check.id), suite_id=str(suite_id))\n    return check",
  "new_string": "def record_check_version(\n    session: Session, check: Check, *, actor_id: uuid.UUID | None\n) -> CheckVersion:\n    \"\"\"Append an immutable snapshot of `check`'s current state as its next\n    version (a per-check sequence starting at 1). The caller commits — this only\n    adds the row, so the snapshot and the create/update it records commit\n    atomically. The `(check_id, version_no)` unique constraint is the backstop\n    against a concurrent double-write computing the same number (rare under v1's\n    single-tenant, low-concurrency editing).\n\n    `check.id` must be populated (flush or commit the check first).\n    \"\"\"\n    next_no = (\n        session.scalar(\n            select(func.coalesce(func.max(CheckVersion.version_no), 0)).where(\n                CheckVersion.check_id == check.id\n            )\n        )\n        or 0\n    ) + 1\n    version = CheckVersion(\n        check_id=check.id,\n        version_no=next_no,\n        name=check.name,\n        kind=check.kind,\n        expectation_type=check.expectation_type,\n        config=check.config,\n        warn_threshold=check.warn_threshold,\n        fail_threshold=check.fail_threshold,\n        critical_threshold=check.critical_threshold,\n        changed_by=actor_id,\n    )\n    session.add(version)\n    return version\n\n\ndef create_check(\n    session: Session,\n    *,\n    suite_id: uuid.UUID,\n    name: str,\n    kind: str,\n    expectation_type: str,\n    config: dict[str, Any],\n    warn_threshold: Decimal | None,\n    fail_threshold: Decimal | None,\n    critical_threshold: Decimal | None,\n    actor_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,\n) -> Check:\n    \"\"\"Create a check in a suite, recording its first version (#280).\n\n    Raises `SuiteNotFoundError` (404) if the suite does not exist, or\n    `CheckConfigInvalidError` (422) for an unsupported kind.\n    \"\"\"\n    suite = get_suite(session, suite_id)  # 404 if the suite is missing\n    validate_kind(kind)\n    if is_custom_sql(expectation_type):\n        validate_custom_sql_check(\n            expectation_type=expectation_type,\n            config=config,\n            connection_type=_connection_type(session, suite),\n        )\n\n    check = Check(\n        suite_id=suite_id,\n        name=name,\n        kind=kind,\n        expectation_type=expectation_type,\n        config=config,\n        warn_threshold=warn_threshold,\n        fail_threshold=fail_threshold,\n        critical_threshold=critical_threshold,\n    )\n    session.add(check)\n    session.flush()  # assign check.id so the v1 snapshot can reference it\n    record_check_version(session, check, actor_id=actor_id)\n    session.commit()\n    session.refresh(check)\n    log.info(\"check_created\", check_id=str(check.id), suite_id=str(suite_id))\n    return check"

{

  "new_string": "    require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum=\"edit\")\n    svc.delete_check(db, suite_id, check_id)\n\n\n# ───────────────────────── version history (#280) ──────────────────\n\n\nclass CheckVersionRead(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"One snapshot in a check's history. `changed_by_name` is the author's\n    display name (or email), resolved server-side so the drawer needn't join\n    users; NULL when the author is a system actor or has been removed.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    version_no: int\n    name: str\n    kind: str\n    expectation_type: str\n    config: dict[str, Any]\n    warn_threshold: float | None\n    fail_threshold: float | None\n    critical_threshold: float | None\n    changed_by: uuid.UUID | None\n    changed_by_name: str | None\n    created_at: datetime\n\n\n@router.get(\n    \"/suites/{suite_id}/checks/{check_id}/versions\",\n    response_model=list[CheckVersionRead],\n    summary=\"List a check's version history (newest first)\",\n)\ndef list_check_versions(\n    suite_id: uuid.UUID,\n    check_id: uuid.UUID,\n    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n) -> list[CheckVersionRead]:\n    require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum=\"view\")\n    return [\n        CheckVersionRead(\n            version_no=v.version_no,\n            name=v.name,\n            kind=v.kind,\n            expectation_type=v.expectation_type,\n            config=v.config,\n            warn_threshold=float(v.warn_threshold) if v.warn_threshold is not None else None,\n            fail_threshold=float(v.fail_threshold) if v.fail_threshold is not None else None,\n            critical_threshold=(\n                float(v.critical_threshold) if v.critical_threshold is not None else None\n            ),\n            changed_by=v.changed_by,\n            changed_by_name=(v.author.display_name or v.author.email) if v.author else None,\n            created_at=v.created_at,\n        )\n        for v in svc.list_check_versions(db, suite_id, check_id)\n    ]\n\n\n# ───────────────────────── dry-run (preview, no persistence) ────────"
}

270	    e = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email="e@ex")

272	    db_session.flush()
273	    conn = Connection(
274	        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
275	        type="snowflake",
276	        env="dev",
277	        config={"account": "x"},
278	        created_by=owner.id,
279	    )
280	    db_session.add(conn)

282	    suite = Suite(name="s", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id)

class SuiteImportRequest(BaseModel):
    connection_id: uuid.UUID
    document: SuiteDocument


@router.get(
    "/suites/{suite_id}/export",
    response_model=SuiteDocument,
    summary="Export a suite as a portable document",
)
def export_suite(
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> SuiteDocument:
    suite = require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="view")
    return SuiteDocument.model_validate(suite_io.export_suite(suite))


@router.post(
    "/suites/import",
    response_model=SuiteRead,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    summary="Import a suite document onto a connection",
)
def import_suite(
    payload: SuiteImportRequest,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> SuiteRead:
    # Like create_suite: any authenticated user may import; the new suite is
    # owned by them. Thresholds/config round-trip exactly (Decimal in/out).
    doc = payload.document
    suite = suite_io.import_suite(
        db,
        version=doc.version,
        name=doc.name,
        description=doc.description,
        checks=[c.model_dump() for c in doc.checks],
        connection_id=payload.connection_id,
        created_by=current_user.id,
    )
    return SuiteRead.model_validate(suite)

@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+"""add check_versions (per-check config history) (#280)
+
+Revision ID: c4d5e6f7a8b9
+Revises: b1f2c3d4e5a6
+Create Date: 2026-06-15 00:00:00.000000+00:00
+
+Checks carried no history — ``check_service.update_check`` overwrote the row in
+place, so a prior config was unrecoverable. This adds a ``check_versions`` table
+holding an immutable snapshot of a check's editable state, written on create and
+after every successful update; it backs the "version history" drawer ("see
+previous config before overwriting"). This is per-check config history, not the
+cross-entity audit log (deferred to v1.1).
+
+``version_no`` is a per-check sequence (unique with ``check_id``). A version is
+cascade-deleted with its check, but survives its author (``changed_by`` is
+``SET NULL`` so a removed user doesn't drop the snapshot).
+
+Backward-compatible: a brand-new table, no change to existing tables, no data
+rewrite, no two-step. Existing checks simply have no recorded history until
+their next create/update writes one.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+
+import sqlalchemy as sa
+from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB, UUID
+
+from alembic import op
+
+# revision identifiers, used by Alembic.
+revision: str = "c4d5e6f7a8b9"
+down_revision: str | None = "b1f2c3d4e5a6"
+branch_labels: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
+depends_on: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
+
+
+def upgrade() -> None:
+    op.create_table(
+        "check_versions",
+        sa.Column(
+            "id",
+            UUID(as_uuid=True),
+            server_default=sa.text("gen_random_uuid()"),
+            nullable=False,
+        ),
+        sa.Column("check_id", UUID(as_uuid=True), nullable=False),
+        sa.Column("version_no", sa.Integer(), nullable=False),
+        sa.Column("name", sa.String(length=256), nullable=False),
+        sa.Column("kind", sa.String(length=32), nullable=False),
+        sa.Column("expectation_type", sa.String(length=128), nullable=False),
+        sa.Column("config", JSONB(), nullable=False),
+        sa.Column("warn_threshold", sa.Numeric(), nullable=True),
+        sa.Column("fail_threshold", sa.Numeric(), nullable=True),
+        sa.Column("critical_threshold", sa.Numeric(), nullable=True),
+        sa.Column("changed_by", UUID(as_uuid=True), nullable=True),
+        sa.Column(
+            "created_at",
+            sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
+            server_default=sa.func.now(),
+            nullable=False,
+        ),
+        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(["check_id"], ["checks.id"], ondelete="CASCADE"),
+        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(["changed_by"], ["users.id"], ondelete="SET NULL"),
+        sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint("id"),
+        sa.UniqueConstraint("check_id", "version_no", name="uq_check_versions_check_version"),
+    )
+    op.create_index("ix_check_versions_check_id", "check_versions", ["check_id"])
+
+
+def downgrade() -> None:
+    op.drop_index("ix_check_versions_check_id", table_name="check_versions")
+    op.drop_table("check_versions")
diff --git a/backend/app/api/v1/checks.py b/backend/app/api/v1/checks.py

@@ -12,6 +12,7 @@ responses emit `float` for clean JSON numbers, coerced from the stored Decimal.
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import uuid

+def record_check_version(
+    session: Session, check: Check, *, actor_id: uuid.UUID | None
+) -> CheckVersion:
+    """Append an immutable snapshot of `check`'s current state as its next
+    version (a per-check sequence starting at 1). The caller commits — this only
+    adds the row, so the snapshot and the create/update it records commit
+    atomically. The `(check_id, version_no)` unique constraint is the backstop
+    against a concurrent double-write computing the same number (rare under v1's
+    single-tenant, low-concurrency editing).
+
+    `check.id` must be populated (flush or commit the check first).
+    """
+    next_no = (
+        session.scalar(
+            select(func.coalesce(func.max(CheckVersion.version_no), 0)).where(
+                CheckVersion.check_id == check.id
+            )
+        )
+        or 0
+    ) + 1
+    version = CheckVersion(
+        check_id=check.id,
+        version_no=next_no,
+        name=check.name,
+        kind=check.kind,
+        expectation_type=check.expectation_type,
+        config=check.config,
+        warn_threshold=check.warn_threshold,
+        fail_threshold=check.fail_threshold,
+        critical_threshold=check.critical_threshold,
+        changed_by=actor_id,
+    )
+    session.add(version)
+    return version
+

+) -> list[CheckVersion]:
+    """A check's version history, newest first (#280). 404 if the check is

**Summary of review** (changes in `backend/app/services/check_service.py`, `backend/app/api/v1/checks.py`, `backend/app/services/suite_io_service.py`, `backend/app/db/models.py`, migration `c4d5e6f7a8b9_add_check_versions.py`):

Two real findings, both in `check_service.py`:

1. **No-op PATCH pollutes history** (line 212) — `update_check` always calls `record_check_version`, even when the PATCH body changes nothing. Since `CheckUpdate` makes all fields optional, an empty/idempotent PATCH appends a duplicate snapshot and bumps `version_no`. Medium severity.

2. **Concurrent version write → unhandled 500** (line 70) — `max(version_no)+1` is computed then inserted under the `(check_id, version_no)` unique constraint with no retry/catch; a concurrent writer raises `IntegrityError` → generic 500. The docstring explicitly acknowledges this is an accepted tradeoff for v1's low-concurrency single-tenant model, so it's lower severity but real.

**Items I checked and cleared (not bugs):**
- Migration chain is clean: `c4d5e6f7a8b9` → `b1f2c3d4e5a6` (the prior head; nothing else references it). Up/down symmetric, constraint/index names match the ORM `__table_args__`. FK `ondelete` (CASCADE on check_id, SET NULL on changed_by) matches model and docstring intent.
- `session.flush()` before commit in `create_check`/`import_suite` doesn't change rollback semantics — it's all one transaction, so a later validation/commit failure still rolls back atomically.
- `config=check.config` snapshot aliasing is safe: `update_check` reassigns `check.config` to a new dict rather than mutating in place, so old snapshots aren't corrupted.
- `update_check` records the **post-update** state (confirmed by tests); validation runs *before* `record_check_version`, so a rejected custom-SQL update persists no version.
- `float(... if not None else None)` threshold coercion in the API and the author display_name/email fallback (`v.author.display_name or v.author.email`) are correct; `selectinload(author)` avoids N+1.
- Authz on the new endpoint uses `minimum="view"` consistent with other read endpoints; outsider gets 404 via `get_check`.

Immutable snapshot of a check'\\''s editable state (`name`/`kind`/`expectation_type`/`config`/thresholds) + `changed_by` (`SET NULL` so a snapshot outlives a removed author); `version_no` a per-check sequence, unique with `check_id`.\n- **`record_check_version()`** snapshots v1 on create, appends after each *real* update, and snapshots each imported check; `actor_id` threaded from `current_user`.\n- **`GET /suites/{suite_id}/checks/{check_id}/versions`** — suite-authz `view`-gated, newest-first, author name resolved server-side (model property + `from_attributes`).\n\n## Scope\nPer-check config history only — **not** the cross-entity audit log (v1.1). **View-only**; restore is a deferred follow-up (will file once the frontend lands).\n\n## Review (`/code-review` high — agents)\nApplied:\n- **No-op PATCH no longer mints a duplicate version** — `update_check` only snapshots when `session.is_modified(check)`, so an empty/identical-value save doesn'\\''t pollute history (test added).\n- **Removed duplicated Decimal→float coercion** in `CheckVersionRead` — now `from_attributes` + a `changed_by_name` model property, matching `CheckRead`.\n- Simplified the `version_no` query (single `or 0`, dropped redundant SQL `coalesce`).\n\nAccepted v1 tradeoffs (noted, not fixed):\n- **Concurrent version write → 500.** `max(version_no)+1` under the unique constraint can collide on simultaneous edits of one check; surfaces as a 500 rather than a clean retry. Acceptable for v1 single-tenant, low-concurrency editing (documented in the helper docstring).\n- **Import does one `max()` SELECT per check.** Negligible for typical handful-of-check suites; not special-cased.\n\n## Testing\n- 7 new tests: create records v1, update appends v2 (newest-first, v1 preserves old config), **no-op update appends nothing**, author recorded, import snapshots each check, viewer reads / outsider 404s, unknown check 404.\n- Migration up→down→up verified against Postgres 16; full backend suite **683 passed / 2 skipped, 96%**. black/ruff/mypy/bandit clean locally.\n\nFixes #280\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)' 2>&1 | tail -3",
  "description": "Open PR for version-history backend"
}
