=== useAsyncData signature ===
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react';

/** Three-state result of an async fetch. */
export type AsyncState<T> =
  | { status: 'loading' }
  | { status: 'ok'; data: T }
  | { status: 'error'; error: string };

/**
 * Fetch on mount (and on `reload()`), with a cancelled-guard so a late
 * resolution after unmount doesn't set state, and rejection normalised to a
 * string `error`. Shared by the data pages (Home, Connections, …) so the
 * cancelled-effect dance lives in one place rather than being re-derived per page.
 *
 * `reload` re-runs the fetcher (e.g. after a mutation) while keeping the current
 * data visible until the refetch resolves — no flash back to the loading state.
 */
export function useAsyncData<T>(fetcher: () => Promise<T>): {
  state: AsyncState<T>;
  reload: () => void;
} {
  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T>>({ status: 'loading' });
  const [nonce, setNonce] = useState(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
    fetcher()
      .then((data) => {
        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });
      })
      .catch((err: unknown) => {
        if (!cancelled) {
          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
        }
      });
    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
    };
    // Re-run on mount and whenever `reload` bumps the nonce; the fetcher identity
    // is intentionally not a dependency.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [nonce]);

  const reload = useCallback(() => setNonce((n) => n + 1), []);
  return { state, reload };
}

 */
export function formatScalar(value: unknown): string {
  if (value === null || value === undefined) return '—';
  return typeof value === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(value) : String(value);
}

/** Absolute timestamp as a locale string, or an em dash when absent. */
export function formatTimestamp(iso: string | null): string {
  if (!iso) return '—';
  const d = new Date(iso);
  return Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) ? '—' : d.toLocaleString();
}

/**
 * Run duration (finished − started) as a compact human string: `850ms`, `12s`,
 * `1m 3s`. Returns an em dash when either bound is missing (queued / never
 * finished) or the interval is negative (clock skew).
 */
export function formatDuration(startedAt: string | null, finishedAt: string | null): string {
  if (!startedAt || !finishedAt) return '—';
  const ms = new Date(finishedAt).getTime() - new Date(startedAt).getTime();
  if (Number.isNaN(ms) || ms < 0) return '—';
  if (ms < 1000) return `${ms}ms`;
  const totalSeconds = Math.round(ms / 1000);
  if (totalSeconds < 60) return `${totalSeconds}s`;
  const minutes = Math.floor(totalSeconds / 60);

  "content": "import { Alert, Descriptions, Drawer, Empty, Flex, List, Spin, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';\n\nimport { type CheckVersion, listCheckVersions } from '../../api/suites';\nimport { formatTimestamp } from '../results/resultsFormat';\nimport { useAsyncData } from '../../hooks/useAsyncData';\nimport { EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE } from './expectationCatalog';\n\n/**\n * Read-only history of a check's saved configurations (#280) — \"see previous\n * config before overwriting\". Each version is an immutable snapshot the backend\n * records on create and on every real edit; newest first. v1 is view-only (no\n * restore). Mounted only while open (`destroyOnHidden`) so it refetches each time.\n */\nexport function CheckHistoryDrawer({\n  open,\n  suiteId,\n  check,\n  onClose,\n}: {\n  open: boolean;\n  suiteId: string;\n  /** The check whose history to show; null while none is selected. */\n  check: { id: string; name: string } | null;\n  onClose: () => void;\n}) {\n  return (\n    <Drawer\n      title={check ? `History — “${check.name}”` : 'History'}\n      open={open}\n      onClose={onClose}\n      width={520}\n      destroyOnHidden\n    >\n      {check && <CheckHistoryBody suiteId={suiteId} checkId={check.id} />}\n    </Drawer>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction CheckHistoryBody({ suiteId, checkId }: { suiteId: string; checkId: string }) {\n  const { state } = useAsyncData(() => listCheckVersions(suiteId, checkId));\n\n  if (state.status === 'loading') {\n    return <Spin tip=\"Loading history…\" />;\n  }\n  if (state.status === 'error') {\n    return (\n      <Alert type=\"error\" showIcon message=\"Failed to load history\" description={state.error} />\n    );\n  }\n  if (state.data.length === 0) {\n    // Only checks created before the history feature shipped have no snapshots.\n    return <Empty image={Empty.PRESENTED_IMAGE_SIMPLE} description=\"No history recorded yet.\" />;\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <List\n      dataSource={state.data}\n      // The first row is the newest snapshot — i.e. the check's current saved state.\n      renderItem={(version, index) => <VersionItem version={version} current={index === 0} />}\n    />\n  );\n}\n\nfunction VersionItem({ version, current }: { version: CheckVersion; current: boolean }) {\n  const label = EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[version.expectation_type]?.label ?? version.expectation_type;\n  return (\n    <List.Item>\n      <Flex vertical gap={8} style={{ width: '100%' }}>\n        <Flex align=\"center\" gap={8} wrap>\n          <Tag color=\"blue\">v{version.version_no}</Tag>\n          {current && <Tag color=\"green\">Current</Tag>}\n          <Typography.Text strong>{version.name}</Typography.Text>\n          <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\" style={{ marginLeft: 'auto', fontSize: 12 }}>\n            {version.changed_by_name ?? 'Unknown'} · {formatTimestamp(version.created_at)}\n          </Typography.Text>\n        </Flex>\n        <Descriptions size=\"small\" column={1} bordered styles={{ label: { width: 120 } }}>\n          <Descriptions.Item label=\"Expectation\">{label}</Descriptions.Item>\n          <Descriptions.Item label=\"Config\">\n            <Typography.Text code style={{ whiteSpace: 'pre-wrap', wordBreak: 'break-word' }}>\n              {JSON.stringify(version.config)}\n            </Typography.Text>\n          </Descriptions.Item>\n          <Descriptions.Item label=\"Thresholds\">{formatThresholds(version)}</Descriptions.Item>\n        </Descriptions>\n      </Flex>\n    </List.Item>\n  );\n}\n\n/** Compact warn/fail/critical line, or an em dash when the check is plain pass/fail. */\nfunction formatThresholds(version: CheckVersion): string {\n  const parts: string[] = [];\n  if (version.warn_threshold !== null) parts.push(`warn ${version.warn_threshold}`);\n  if (version.fail_threshold !== null) parts.push(`fail ${version.fail_threshold}`);\n  if (version.critical_threshold !== null) parts.push(`critical ${version.critical_threshold}`);\n  return parts.length > 0 ? parts.join(' · ') : '—';\n}\n"
}

@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+import { Alert, Descriptions, Drawer, Empty, Flex, List, Spin, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';
+
+import { type CheckVersion, listCheckVersions } from '../../api/suites';
+import { formatTimestamp } from '../results/resultsFormat';
+import { useAsyncData } from '../../hooks/useAsyncData';
+import { EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE } from './expectationCatalog';
+
+/**
+ * Read-only history of a check's saved configurations (#280) — "see previous
+ * config before overwriting". Each version is an immutable snapshot the backend
+ * records on create and on every real edit; newest first. v1 is view-only (no
+ * restore). Mounted only while open (`destroyOnHidden`) so it refetches each time.
+ */
+export function CheckHistoryDrawer({
+  open,
+  suiteId,
+  check,
+  onClose,
+}: {
+  open: boolean;
+  suiteId: string;
+  /** The check whose history to show; null while none is selected. */
+  check: { id: string; name: string } | null;
+  onClose: () => void;
+}) {
+  return (
+    <Drawer
+      title={check ? `History — “${check.name}”` : 'History'}
+      open={open}
+      onClose={onClose}
+      width={520}
+      destroyOnHidden
+    >
+      {check && <CheckHistoryBody suiteId={suiteId} checkId={check.id} />}
+    </Drawer>
+  );
+}
+
+function CheckHistoryBody({ suiteId, checkId }: { suiteId: string; checkId: string }) {
+  const { state } = useAsyncData(() => listCheckVersions(suiteId, checkId));
+
+  if (state.status === 'loading') {
+    return <Spin tip="Loading history…" />;
+  }
+  if (state.status === 'error') {
+    return (
+      <Alert type="error" showIcon message="Failed to load history" description={state.error} />
+    );
+  }
+  if (state.data.length === 0) {
+    // Only checks created before the history feature shipped have no snapshots.
+    return <Empty image={Empty.PRESENTED_IMAGE_SIMPLE} description="No history recorded yet." />;
+  }
+
+  return (
+    <List
+      dataSource={state.data}
+      // The first row is the newest snapshot — i.e. the check's current saved state.
+      renderItem={(version, index) => <VersionItem version={version} current={index === 0} />}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+function VersionItem({ version, current }: { version: CheckVersion; current: boolean }) {
+  const label = EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[version.expectation_type]?.label ?? version.expectation_type;
+  return (
+    <List.Item>
+      <Flex vertical gap={8} style={{ width: '100%' }}>
+        <Flex align="center" gap={8} wrap>
+          <Tag color="blue">v{version.version_no}</Tag>
+          {current && <Tag color="green">Current</Tag>}
+          <Typography.Text strong>{version.name}</Typography.Text>
+          <Typography.Text type="secondary" style={{ marginLeft: 'auto', fontSize: 12 }}>
+            {version.changed_by_name ?? 'Unknown'} · {formatTimestamp(version.created_at)}
+          </Typography.Text>
+        </Flex>
+        <Descriptions size="small" column={1} bordered styles={{ label: { width: 120 } }}>
+          <Descriptions.Item label="Expectation">{label}</Descriptions.Item>
+          <Descriptions.Item label="Config">
+            <Typography.Text code style={{ whiteSpace: 'pre-wrap', wordBreak: 'break-word' }}>
+              {JSON.stringify(version.config)}
+            </Typography.Text>
+          </Descriptions.Item>
+          <Descriptions.Item label="Thresholds">{formatThresholds(version)}</Descriptions.Item>
+        </Descriptions>
+      </Flex>
+    </List.Item>
+  );
+}
+
+/** Compact warn/fail/critical line, or an em dash when the check is plain pass/fail. */
+function formatThresholds(version: CheckVersion): string {
+  const parts: string[] = [];
+  if (version.warn_threshold !== null) parts.push(`warn ${version.warn_threshold}`);
+  if (version.fail_threshold !== null) parts.push(`fail ${version.fail_threshold}`);
+  if (version.critical_threshold !== null) parts.push(`critical ${version.critical_threshold}`);
+  return parts.length > 0 ? parts.join(' · ') : '—';
+}

Confirmed. The findings are solid. Here is my review.

```json
[
  {
    "file": "frontend/src/components/checks/CheckDrawer.tsx",
    "line": 43,
    "summary": "historyOpen state is never reset when the parent CheckDrawer closes or switches to a different check, so it leaks across edit sessions.",
    "failure_scenario": "User opens Edit on check A, clicks History (historyOpen=true), then closes the parent drawer WITHOUT closing the history child first (e.g. presses the parent's Cancel/X, or onSaved fires after a Save). The parent's destroyOnHidden unmounts the child DOM but CheckDrawer itself stays mounted (Suites.tsx keeps it with open=false), so the historyOpen=true state survives. Next time the user opens Edit for a different check B, the History drawer auto-pops open immediately showing B's history, with no user action. Fix: reset historyOpen in the open/check effect (e.g. setHistoryOpen(false) when !open or when check.id changes)."
  },
  {
    "file": "frontend/src/components/checks/CheckHistoryDrawer.tsx",
    "line": 32,
    "summary": "Nested Drawer relies on parent's destroyOnHidden to unmount it; if the parent is closed while historyOpen is still true the child can briefly render over an empty backdrop during the parent's close transition.",
    "failure_scenario": "Because the child Drawer is rendered inside the parent Drawer's JSX and reads historyOpen independently, closing the parent while the history child is open leaves open={true} on the child for the duration of the parent's exit animation. antd portals each Drawer to document.body with its own z-index, so the orphaned history drawer (and its mask) can flash on screen with no parent behind it before destroyOnHidden tears it down. Coupled with the historyOpen-leak above, this also means the child re-portals on the next parent open. Resetting historyOpen on parent close (same fix as the first finding) removes the flash."
  }
]
```

## Summary

I reviewed the three changed files plus the helpers (`useAsyncData`, `formatTimestamp`, `EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE`). Two real findings, both rooted in the same defect: **`historyOpen` in `CheckDrawer` is never reset.**

**Things I checked and found correct (no bug):**
- **`useAsyncData` fire timing / stale checkId:** `CheckHistoryDrawer` uses `destroyOnHidden`, so `CheckHistoryBody` (which owns the `useAsyncData` call) unmounts on close and remounts on open. Each open does a fresh fetch with the current `checkId` — no double-fetch, no never-fetch, no stale-checkId within the history view itself.
- **"Current" tag at index 0:** Matches the backend contract (snapshot on create + every real edit, newest first). Sound.
- **Empty state:** Handled — checks predating the feature show the `Empty` placeholder.
- **`changed_by_name` null:** Handled via `?? 'Unknown'`.
- **Threshold `0` rendering:** `!== null` checks correctly pass a `0` threshold (`0 !== null`), rendering `warn 0` rather than dropping it. Type is `number | null`, so no `undefined`/`0` ambiguity.
- **`state.data` access:** After the `'loading'`/`'error'` guards, TypeScript narrows to `'ok'`, which carries `.data`. Compiles and runs.
- **`List` keys / `<Spin tip>` without children:** Both match existing accepted patterns elsewhere (Results, SharePanel, TriggersPanel); not introduced here.
- **History button in create mode:** Correctly gated behind `check &&`, so it never shows when `check` is undefined.

The fix for both findings is the same one-liner: reset `historyOpen` to false when the parent drawer closes or the edited check changes (e.g. in the existing `[open, check, form]` effect).

Both halves of the version-history drawer are now built, reviewed, and pushed. While CI runs on the frontend PR, here's the status:

## Frontend drawer — PR #282 (CI running)
The actual view-only drawer: a **History** button on the check editor opens a newest-first version list (latest tagged **Current**) showing expectation, config, thresholds, and author + timestamp.

`/code-review` (agents) caught a **real bug before merge**: `historyOpen` was never reset, so closing the editor or switching checks left it open and the drawer would auto-pop showing the *new* check. Fixed with the codebase's render-phase reset pattern (an effect tripped the `set-state-in-effect` lint rule), with a regression test. Also fixed three quality issues it surfaced — custom-SQL config was collapsing to one escaped line, threshold labels now match the editor's `≥` convention, and the empty-state copy no longer implies legacy checks are unconfigured. 192 frontend tests green, all gates clean.

## Where this leaves Week 4
- **#281 (backend)** — merged. History table + snapshotting + read API.
- **#282 (frontend)** — open, CI running. The drawer itself.

Once #282 merges, the **check version-history drawer is done** — leaving only the **admin page** on the Week-4 epic (#173), which is still genuinely backend-blocked on a list-all-suites/users endpoint.

```
1	"""Suite authorization — the single primitive every suite-scoped endpoint gates on.
2	
3	A user's effective permission on a suite is the highest of: **owner** (they are
4	`suite.created_by` — implicit, immutable, never a share row) or their `shares`
5	row (`view` < `edit` < `admin`). Capability ladder (decided for v1):
6	
7	    view   — read the suite, its checks, its results
8	    edit   — + create/update/delete checks, update the suite, trigger runs
9	    admin  — + manage shares (grant/revoke) AND delete the suite
10	    owner  — same capabilities as admin, but it is the creator: cannot be
11	             revoked or demoted, and granting a share to the owner is rejected.
12	
13	`require_permission` is the gate the API layer calls: it 404s a suite the user
14	can't see at all (existence is hidden), and 403s one they can see but lack the
15	level for. It returns the `Suite` so callers don't re-fetch.
16	
17	FastAPI-free (takes a `Session` + the user id); the API layer passes
18	`current_user.id`.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import uuid
24	from collections.abc import Sequence
25	
26	from sqlalchemy import select
27	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
28	
29	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
30	from backend.app.db.models import Share, Suite
31	from backend.app.services.suite_service import SuiteNotFoundError
32	
33	OWNER = "owner"
34	
35	# Ordered capability ranks. `owner` ranks above `admin` so it always clears an
36	# admin gate, even though their capabilities are identical — the distinction is
37	# that owner is the immutable creator, not a grantable/revocable share.
38	_RANK = {"view": 1, "edit": 2, "admin": 3, OWNER: 4}
39	
40	
41	class SuiteForbiddenError(DataQError):
42	    status_code = 403
43	    code = "suite_forbidden"
44	
45	
46	def effective_permission(session: Session, suite: Suite, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> str | None:
47	    """The user's level on `suite` (`owner`/`admin`/`edit`/`view`), or None."""
48	    if suite.created_by == user_id:
49	        return OWNER
50	    share = session.scalars(
51	        select(Share).where(Share.suite_id == suite.id, Share.user_id == user_id)
52	    ).first()
53	    return share.permission if share is not None else None
54	
55	
56	def effective_permissions(
57	    session: Session, suites: Sequence[Suite], user_id: uuid.UUID
58	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, str | None]:
59	    """Batch `effective_permission` for many suites in one shares query (no N+1).
60	
61	    Owned suites resolve to `owner` without touching `shares`; the rest are
62	    looked up in a single `IN` query. Used to stamp each suite in a list with the
63	    caller's level so the UI can gate per-suite actions (manage shares, delete).
64	    """
65	    owned = {s.id for s in suites if s.created_by == user_id}
66	    shared_ids = [s.id for s in suites if s.id not in owned]
67	    levels: dict[uuid.UUID, str] = {}
68	    if shared_ids:
69	        rows = session.scalars(
70	            select(Share).where(Share.user_id == user_id, Share.suite_id.in_(shared_ids))
71	        )
72	        levels = {row.suite_id: row.permission for row in rows}
73	    return {s.id: (OWNER if s.id in owned else levels.get(s.id)) for s in suites}
74	
75	
76	def require_permission(
77	    session: Session,
78	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
79	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
80	    *,
81	    minimum: str,
82	) -> Suite:
83	    """Return the suite iff the user has at least `minimum` permission on it.
84	
85	    Raises `SuiteNotFoundError` (404) if the suite doesn't exist **or** the user
86	    has no access at all (existence is hidden), and `SuiteForbiddenError` (403)
87	    if they have some access but below `minimum`.
88	    """
89	    suite = session.get(Suite, suite_id)
90	    if suite is None:
91	        raise SuiteNotFoundError("suite not found", detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id)})
92	    level = effective_permission(session, suite, user_id)
93	    if level is None:
94	        # No access → indistinguishable from "doesn't exist" (don't leak the id).
95	        raise SuiteNotFoundError("suite not found", detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id)})
96	    if _RANK[level] < _RANK[minimum]:
97	        raise SuiteForbiddenError(
98	            f"this action requires {minimum!r} permission on the suite",
99	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "have": level, "need": minimum},
100	        )
101	    return suite
102

I've now mapped the full picture. Here's what the admin page needs, end to end.

## The core gap: there is no workspace-admin concept yet

Today `admin` exists **only per-suite** ([suite_authz.py](backend/app/services/suite_authz.py) — `view < edit < admin < owner`). There is no notion of a person who can administer the *whole workspace*. The [User model](backend/app/db/models.py#L71) has no role/`is_admin` field, auth resolves users straight from Azure AD with no allowlist, and [list_suites](backend/app/api/v1/suites.py#L124) deliberately scopes to owned-or-shared. So "list **all** suites/users/access" needs a new authz primitive — that's the real backend block, exactly as progress.md line 315 flags it.

**This is the one decision I need from you** (below). Everything else follows from it.

---

## Backend changes

1. **Workspace-admin authz primitive** — a `require_workspace_admin` dependency + an `is_workspace_admin(user)` predicate. Mechanism depends on your answer below.
2. **`admin_service.py`** (FastAPI-free, like the other services) — three queries that bypass the per-suite scoping:
   - all suites + owner display name, check count, share count, target/env
   - all users + created/last-seen + how many suites they own/are shared on
   - access overview — every share row across all suites (who has what, where)
3. **`api/v1/admin.py` router** — `GET /admin/suites`, `/admin/users`, `/admin/access`, all behind `require_workspace_admin` (→ real 403 for non-admins). Additive, backward-compatible, **no migration** if we go config-allowlist.
4. **Extend `/me`** ([me.py](backend/app/api/v1/me.py)) with `is_workspace_admin: bool` so the frontend can gate the nav item + route without a second call.
5. **Tests** — admin→200, non-admin→403, and that the list-all genuinely bypasses owned-or-shared scoping (seed a suite the admin doesn't own and assert it appears).

## Frontend changes

1. **`api/admin.ts`** — typed client for the three endpoints.
2. **`pages/Admin.tsx`** — three sections/tabs (Suites · Users · Access) on antd `Table`s, matching the `AdminScreen.jsx` design ref.
3. **`api/me.ts` + nav gating** — add `is_workspace_admin` to `MeResponse`; show the **Admin** nav item (footer group per the design) and register the `/admin` route **only** when true.
4. **A real 403 page** — none exists today. Server-driven (the route renders it when `/admin/*` returns 403), not a client toggle — per CLAUDE.md §11 and the design note ("adopt the 403 page, drop the demo 'View as' switch").
5. **Tests** — admin sees tables, non-admin sees 403 / no nav item.

---

> AGENT

Good question — and it cuts two ways. Let me clarify both, because neither is a lock-in problem:

**1. Azure/IdP lock-in? No.** The allowlist matches on **`user.email`** — a generic identity attribute that [`get_current_user`](backend/app/core/auth.py#L172) already populates from *whatever* auth provider (Azure today, anything tomorrow). It does **not** read MSAL/Entra claims, AAD object ids, or tenant ids in service code — so it stays clean against CLAUDE.md §11 and the anti-lock-in seams (ADR 0010/0013). If you swap IdPs post-v1, the allowlist keeps working as long as the new provider yields an email. Azure stays "one impl behind the seam."

**2. Tenant-scoped? Yes — and that's correct by design.** DataQ is **single-tenant** (CLAUDE.md §1). There's one workspace, so a workspace-wide admin allowlist is exactly the right grain — there's no second tenant for it to leak across. If the BYOL/marketplace path ever makes this multi-tenant (ADR 0013, post-v1), admin identity would move into per-tenant data (the `is_admin` column route) at that point — but pulling that in now would be speculative scope for a tenant count of one.

So: **email allowlist, env-driven, no migration** — generic on the auth axis, appropriately tenant-wide on the scope axis. It's the recommended option and it doesn't paint us into an Azure or a single-tenant corner.

One small robustness note I'll bake in: compare emails **case-insensitively** (and trimmed), since IdP-supplied email casing isn't guaranteed stable.

Want me to go ahead and build it on this basis — backend first (authz primitive + `admin_service` + `/admin` router + `/me` flag + tests), then the frontend page + 403 + nav gating, as two reviewed PRs?

1	"""Azure AD bearer-token auth + user upsert.
2	
3	Two operating modes — picked once at import time from settings:
4	
5	- **Real mode** — `AZURE_TENANT_ID` + `AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID` are set.
6	  Tokens are validated by `fastapi-azure-auth`: issuer, audience, signature,
7	  expiry, and the configured scope. The OpenID config is loaded at app
8	  startup via `init_auth()` and refreshed automatically.
9	
10	- **Dev bypass** — all three of:
11	  `ENVIRONMENT=dev`, `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`, Azure vars empty.
12	  No token required. Resolves every request to a fixed dev user upserted
13	  into the `users` table. Intended for local development against a
14	  Postgres in `docker-compose` without a real Azure tenant.
15	
16	If neither mode is configured, `init_auth` raises at startup — fail-closed.

1	"""User directory lookup — search the single-tenant user table.
2	
3	The sharing UI grants access by `user_id`, but a human only knows an email or
4	name; this is the search that turns one into the other. Single tenant, so any
5	authenticated user may search the whole directory — there is no per-tenant
6	scoping to apply. FastAPI-free: takes a `Session` + query string.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from sqlalchemy import func, or_, select
12	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
13	
14	from backend.app.db.models import User
15	
16	# A short query would match most of the directory; require enough to be a real
17	# prefix/substring before we run the scan.
18	MIN_QUERY_LEN = 2
19	# Cap the result set so a broad term can't return the whole directory in one go.
20	MAX_LIMIT = 50
21	DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
22	
23	
24	def _escape_like(term: str) -> str:
25	    r"""Escape LIKE wildcards so a user's literal `%` / `_` / `\` stays literal."""
26	    return term.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_")
27	
28	
29	def search_users(session: Session, query: str, *, limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT) -> list[User]:
30	    """Find users whose email or display name contains `query` (case-insensitive).
31	
32	    Returns `[]` for a query shorter than `MIN_QUERY_LEN` (the caller's
33	    type-ahead simply shows nothing until enough is typed). `limit` is clamped
34	    to `[1, MAX_LIMIT]`. Results are ordered by email for a stable list.
35	    """
36	    term = query.strip()
37	    if len(term) < MIN_QUERY_LEN:
38	        return []
39	    capped = max(1, min(limit, MAX_LIMIT))
40	    pattern = f"%{_escape_like(term)}%"
41	    stmt = (
42	        select(User)
43	        .where(
44	            or_(
45	                User.email.ilike(pattern, escape="\\"),
46	                func.coalesce(User.display_name, "").ilike(pattern, escape="\\"),
47	            )
48	        )
49	        .order_by(User.email)
50	        .limit(capped)
51	    )
52	    return list(session.scalars(stmt))
53

70	    db: Session,
71	    *,
72	    aad_object_id: str,
73	    email: str,
74	    display_name: str | None,
75	) -> User:
76	    now = datetime.now(UTC)
77	    stmt = (
78	        insert(User)
79	        .values(
80	            aad_object_id=aad_object_id,
81	            email=email,
82	            display_name=display_name,
83	            last_seen_at=now,

85	        .on_conflict_do_update(
86	            index_elements=["aad_object_id"],

88	                "email": email,
89	                "display_name": display_name,
90	                "last_seen_at": now,
91	                "updated_at": now,
92	            },
93	        )
94	        .returning(User)
95	    )
96	    user = db.execute(stmt).scalar_one()
97	    db.commit()
98	    return user

101	def _extract_claims(azure_user: AzureUser) -> tuple[str, str, str | None]:
102	    claims: dict[str, Any] = azure_user.claims
103	    aad_oid = str(claims["oid"])
104	    email = str(claims.get("preferred_username") or claims.get("email") or claims.get("upn") or "")
105	    display_name_raw = claims.get("name")
106	    display_name = str(display_name_raw) if display_name_raw is not None else None
107	    return aad_oid, email, display_name
108

117	        log.info(

"""Shared pytest fixtures."""

import os
from collections.abc import Iterator

# Set test-mode env vars BEFORE any backend.app.* import resolves. The auth
# module computes its mode at import time from settings; without these the
# TestClient lifespan would raise 'Auth not configured'.
os.environ.setdefault("ENVIRONMENT", "dev")
os.environ.setdefault("AUTH_DEV_BYPASS", "true")

import pytest

from backend.app.core import secrets
from backend.app.core.config import get_settings


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _reset_caches() -> Iterator[None]:
    """Clear cached singletons between tests so settings + secret store rebuild."""
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    secrets.reset_secret_store_cache()
    yield
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    secrets.reset_secret_store_cache()


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def stub_run_dispatch(request: pytest.FixtureRequest, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> list[str]:
    """Stub `run_dispatch.dispatch_run` so any code path that triggers a suite run
    (the pipeline-success ungate #215, the probe, manual runs) never publishes to
    a real broker.

    Returns the list of dispatched run-ids (as strings), so a test can assert
    dispatch happened. Tests that need bespoke dispatch behaviour (e.g. the
    broker-failure path) re-patch `run_dispatch.dispatch_run` themselves — their
    function-scoped patch is applied after this autouse fixture and so wins. The
    probe e2e test uses `apply_async` (a real publish), which this does not touch.

    `@pytest.mark.real_dispatch` opts out entirely — for tests of `dispatch_run`
    itself, which spy `celery_app.send_task` instead.
    """
    calls: list[str] = []
    if request.node.get_closest_marker("real_dispatch") is None:
        from backend.app.services import run_dispatch

        monkeypatch.setattr(run_dispatch, "dispatch_run", lambda run_id: calls.append(str(run_id)))
    return calls


@pytest.fixture
def clean_kv_env(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """Strip every KV_SECRET_* env var so tests start from a clean slate."""
    import os

    for key in list(os.environ):
        if key.startswith("KV_SECRET_"):
            monkeypatch.delenv(key, raising=False)

# other environment regardless of this flag's value.
AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true

# ── Secret store ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 'redis' = shared plaintext store in the dev Redis (default). Lets the API and
#           Celery worker share a credential the API writes at runtime — needed
#           by connection-driven worker runs (#86). api + worker both load this
#           file, so they agree on the mode.
# 'env'   = read connection secrets from KV_SECRET_<NAME> env vars (per-process).
# 'azure_key_vault' = read from Azure Key Vault (staging / prod); requires
#                     AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL. Auth via DefaultAzureCredential.
SECRET_STORE=redis
AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL=

# NOTE on 'env' mode: KV_SECRET_<UPPER_SNAKE_NAME> values are read by the secret
# store straight from the process environment — do NOT add them to this file.
# Settings runs extra="forbid" and would reject them as unknown keys. Supply them
# as real env vars instead: `export KV_SECRET_SNOWFLAKE_UAT_FINANCE=...` for host
# dev, or a compose `environment:` entry for the api + worker services. The name
# matches Connection.secret_ref (e.g. 'snowflake-uat-finance').

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/services/admin_service.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Workspace-admin read queries — the all-suites / all-users / access overview\nbehind the Admin page.\n\nDeliberately *unscoped*: unlike `suite_service.list_suites` (owned-or-shared),\nthese return the whole workspace, so the API layer must gate them on\n`require_workspace_admin`. Read-only, FastAPI-free (takes a `Session`).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom uuid import UUID\n\nfrom sqlalchemy import func, select\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Share, Suite, User\nfrom backend.app.services.suite_authz import OWNER\n\n# Strongest-first permission rank for ordering the access overview.\n_PERMISSION_RANK = {OWNER: 0, \"admin\": 1, \"edit\": 2, \"view\": 3}\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass AdminSuiteRow:\n    \"\"\"One suite in the admin overview, with its owner, datasource, and counts.\"\"\"\n\n    id: UUID\n    name: str\n    connection_name: str\n    connection_type: str\n    env: str\n    owner_id: UUID\n    owner_email: str\n    owner_name: str | None\n    check_count: int\n    share_count: int\n    created_at: datetime\n    updated_at: datetime\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass AdminUserRow:\n    \"\"\"One user in the admin overview, with how many suites they own / share in.\"\"\"\n\n    id: UUID\n    email: str\n    display_name: str | None\n    last_seen_at: datetime | None\n    created_at: datetime\n    owned_suite_count: int\n    shared_suite_count: int\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass AdminAccessRow:\n    \"\"\"One (user → suite) access grant: an implicit owner or an explicit share.\"\"\"\n\n    suite_id: UUID\n    suite_name: str\n    user_id: UUID\n    user_email: str\n    user_name: str | None\n    permission: str  # 'owner' | 'admin' | 'edit' | 'view'\n\n\ndef list_all_suites(session: Session) -> list[AdminSuiteRow]:\n    \"\"\"Every suite with owner + datasource + check/share counts, newest first.\n\n    Counts use `distinct` because the check and share outer-joins multiply rows.\n    \"\"\"\n    stmt = (\n        select(\n            Suite.id,\n            Suite.name,\n            Connection.name,\n            Connection.type,\n            Connection.env,\n            User.id,\n            User.email,\n            User.display_name,\n            func.count(func.distinct(Check.id)),\n            func.count(func.distinct(Share.id)),\n            Suite.created_at,\n            Suite.updated_at,\n        )\n        .join(User, Suite.created_by == User.id)\n        .join(Connection, Suite.connection_id == Connection.id)\n        .outerjoin(Check, Check.suite_id == Suite.id)\n        .outerjoin(Share, Share.suite_id == Suite.id)\n        # Group by each table's PK (Postgres lets us select its other columns).\n        .group_by(Suite.id, Connection.id, User.id)\n        .order_by(Suite.created_at.desc())\n    )\n    return [AdminSuiteRow(*row) for row in session.execute(stmt)]\n\n\ndef list_all_users(session: Session) -> list[AdminUserRow]:\n    \"\"\"Every user with their owned-suite and shared-suite counts, by email.\"\"\"\n    stmt = (\n        select(\n            User.id,\n            User.email,\n            User.display_name,\n            User.last_seen_at,\n            User.created_at,\n            func.count(func.distinct(Suite.id)),\n            func.count(func.distinct(Share.id)),\n        )\n        .outerjoin(Suite, Suite.created_by == User.id)\n        .outerjoin(Share, Share.user_id == User.id)\n        .group_by(User.id)\n        .order_by(User.email)\n    )\n    return [AdminUserRow(*row) for row in session.execute(stmt)]\n\n\ndef list_all_access(session: Session) -> list[AdminAccessRow]:\n    \"\"\"Full access matrix: every implicit owner + every explicit share row.\n\n    Ordered by suite name, then strongest permission first, then user email.\n    \"\"\"\n    owner_stmt = select(\n        Suite.id, Suite.name, User.id, User.email, User.display_name\n    ).join(User, Suite.created_by == User.id)\n    share_stmt = (\n        select(Suite.id, Suite.name, User.id, User.email, User.display_name, Share.permission)\n        .join(Suite, Share.suite_id == Suite.id)\n        .join(User, Share.user_id == User.id)\n    )\n\n    rows = [\n        AdminAccessRow(sid, sname, uid, email, name, OWNER)\n        for sid, sname, uid, email, name in session.execute(owner_stmt)\n    ]\n    rows += [\n        AdminAccessRow(sid, sname, uid, email, name, perm)\n        for sid, sname, uid, email, name, perm in session.execute(share_stmt)\n    ]\n    rows.sort(\n        key=lambda r: (r.suite_name.lower(), _PERMISSION_RANK.get(r.permission, 9), r.user_email)\n    )\n    return rows\n"
}

"""Suite endpoint tests against a real Postgres (db_session) via TestClient.

get_db is overridden to the shared test session; auth runs in dev-bypass mode
(conftest), which upserts the dev user for the suite's created_by. A connection
(with its own owner) is inserted directly for the FK. Skips without
TEST_DATABASE_URL.
"""

import uuid
from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

import pandas as pd
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import func, select

from backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user
from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Suite, User
from backend.app.db.session import get_db
from backend.app.main import app
from backend.app.services import profile_service


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    try:
        yield TestClient(app)
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()


def _connection(db_session: Any) -> Connection:
    """Insert a connection (with its own owner) for suites to bind to."""
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email="owner@example.com")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="snowflake",
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "ab12345.eu-west-1"},
        secret_ref="kv-sf",
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.commit()
    return conn


def _orchestration_connection(db_session: Any, provider: str = "adf") -> Connection:
    """Insert an ADF/Airflow connection — an orchestration provider, never a
    suite datasource (CLAUDE.md §4)."""
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email="orch@example.com")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"{provider}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type=provider,
        env="prod",
        config={},
        secret_ref=f"kv-{provider}",
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.commit()
    return conn
```

@@ -0,0 +1,83 @@
+"""Workspace-admin read endpoints — the all-suites / all-users / access overview
+the Admin page consumes.
+
+Every route is gated by `require_workspace_admin` (config allowlist), declared
+once at the router so a non-admin gets a real 403. These bypass the
+owned-or-shared scoping `list_suites` applies — that's the point of the page.
+Read-only and additive; no new authz on the per-suite ladder.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from datetime import datetime
+from typing import Annotated
+from uuid import UUID
+
+from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
+from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+
+from backend.app.core.auth import require_workspace_admin
+from backend.app.db.session import get_db
+from backend.app.services import admin_service as svc
+
+router = APIRouter(
+    prefix="/admin",
+    tags=["admin"],
+    dependencies=[Depends(require_workspace_admin)],
+)
+
+
+class AdminSuiteRead(BaseModel):
+    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
+
+    id: UUID
+    name: str
+    connection_name: str
+    connection_type: str
+    env: str
+    owner_id: UUID
+    owner_email: str
+    owner_name: str | None
+    check_count: int
+    share_count: int
+    created_at: datetime
+    updated_at: datetime
+
+
+class AdminUserRead(BaseModel):

+
+    id: UUID
+    email: str

+

+
+

+
+@router.get("/access", response_model=list[AdminAccessRead], summary="Access overview (admin)")

diff --git a/backend/app/core/auth.py b/backend/app/core/auth.py
index 26ef5c9..eda5144 100644
--- a/backend/app/core/auth.py
+++ b/backend/app/core/auth.py
@@ -176,3 +176,34 @@ elif _dev_bypass_allowed(_settings):
     get_current_user = _get_current_user_dev_bypass
 else:
     get_current_user = _get_current_user_unconfigured
+
+
+def is_workspace_admin(user: User) -> bool:
+    """True iff the user is in the workspace-admin allowlist (WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS).
+
+    Workspace admin is a single config-driven set — the whole-workspace
+    administrator, distinct from the per-suite view/edit/admin/owner ladder in
+    `suite_authz`. Matched case-insensitively on the IdP-supplied email, a
+    generic identity attribute, so no Azure/Entra claim is read here
+    (ADR 0010/0013, CLAUDE.md §11). Reads settings live (not the import-time
+    singleton) so config changes and tests take effect.
+    """
+    email = (user.email or "").strip().lower()
+    return bool(email) and email in get_settings().workspace_admin_email_set
+
+
+def require_workspace_admin(
+    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
+) -> User:
+    """FastAPI dependency gating the /admin endpoints — 403 for a non-admin.
+
+    Server-side authz (never a client toggle): a non-admin gets a real 403, which
+    the frontend renders as the forbidden page.
+    """
+    if not is_workspace_admin(current_user):
+        raise DataQError(
+            code="workspace_admin_required",
+            message="This action requires workspace-admin access.",
+            status_code=403,
+        )
+    return current_user

diff --git a/backend/app/services/admin_service.py b/backend/app/services/admin_service.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8f9a9c1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/backend/app/services/admin_service.py
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+"""Workspace-admin read queries — the all-suites / all-users / access overview
+behind the Admin page.
+
+Deliberately *unscoped*: unlike `suite_service.list_suites` (owned-or-shared),
+these return the whole workspace, so the API layer must gate them on
+`require_workspace_admin`. Read-only, FastAPI-free (takes a `Session`).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import datetime
+from uuid import UUID
+
+from sqlalchemy import func, select
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+
+from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Share, Suite, User
+from backend.app.services.suite_authz import OWNER
+
+# Strongest-first permission rank for ordering the access overview.
+_PERMISSION_RANK = {OWNER: 0, "admin": 1, "edit": 2, "view": 3}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class AdminSuiteRow:
+    """One suite in the admin overview, with its owner, datasource, and counts."""
+
+    id: UUID
+    name: str
+    connection_name: str
+    connection_type: str
+    env: str
+    owner_id: UUID
+    owner_email: str
+    owner_name: str | None
+    check_count: int
+    share_count: int
+    created_at: datetime
+    updated_at: datetime
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class AdminUserRow:
+    """One user in the admin overview, with how many suites they own / share in."""
+
+    id: UUID
+    email: str
+    display_name: str | None
+    last_seen_at: datetime | None
+    created_at: datetime
+    owned_suite_count: int
+    shared_suite_count: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class AdminAccessRow:
+    """One (user → suite) access grant: an implicit owner or an explicit share."""
+
+    suite_id: UUID
+    suite_name: str
+    user_id: UUID
+    user_email: str
+    user_name: str | None
+    permission: str  # 'owner' | 'admin' | 'edit' | 'view'
+
+
+def list_all_suites(session: Session) -> list[AdminSuiteRow]:
+    """Every suite with owner + datasource + check/share counts, newest first.
+
+    Counts use `distinct` because the check and share outer-joins multiply rows.
+    """
+    stmt = (
+        select(
+            Suite.id,
+            Suite.name,
+            Connection.name,
+            Connection.type,
+            Connection.env,
+            User.id,
+            User.email,
+            User.display_name,
+            func.count(func.distinct(Check.id)),
+            func.count(func.distinct(Share.id)),
+            Suite.created_at,
+            Suite.updated_at,
+        )
+        .join(User, Suite.created_by == User.id)
+        .join(Connection, Suite.connection_id == Connection.id)
+        .outerjoin(Check, Check.suite_id == Suite.id)
+        .outerjoin(Share, Share.suite_id == Suite.id)
+        # Group by each table's PK (Postgres lets us select its other columns).
+        .group_by(Suite.id, Connection.id, User.id)
+        .order_by(Suite.created_at.desc())
+    )
+    return [AdminSuiteRow(*row) for row in session.execute(stmt)]
+
+
+def list_all_users(session: Session) -> list[AdminUserRow]:
+    """Every user with their owned-suite and shared-suite counts, by email."""
+    stmt = (
+        select(
+            User.id,
+            User.email,
+            User.display_name,
+            User.last_seen_at,
+            User.created_at,
+            func.count(func.distinct(Suite.id)),
+            func.count(func.distinct(Share.id)),
+        )
+        .outerjoin(Suite, Suite.created_by == User.id)
+        .outerjoin(Share, Share.user_id == User.id)
+        .group_by(User.id)
+        .order_by(User.email)
+    )
+    return [AdminUserRow(*row) for row in session.execute(stmt)]
+
+
+def list_all_access(session: Session) -> list[AdminAccessRow]:
+    """Full access matrix: every implicit owner + every explicit share row.
+
+    Ordered by suite name, then strongest permission first, then user email.
+    """
+    owner_stmt = select(Suite.id, Suite.name, User.id, User.email, User.display_name).join(
+        User, Suite.created_by == User.id
+    )
+    share_stmt = (
+        select(Suite.id, Suite.name, User.id, User.email, User.display_name, Share.permission)
+        .join(Suite, Share.suite_id == Suite.id)
+        .join(User, Share.user_id == User.id)
+    )
+
+    rows = [
+        AdminAccessRow(sid, sname, uid, email, name, OWNER)
+        for sid, sname, uid, email, name in session.execute(owner_stmt)
+    ]
+    rows += [
+        AdminAccessRow(sid, sname, uid, email, name, perm)
+        for sid, sname, uid, email, name, perm in session.execute(share_stmt)
+    ]
+    rows.sort(
+        key=lambda r: (r.suite_name.lower(), _PERMISSION_RANK.get(r.permission, 9), r.user_email)
+    )
+    return rows
diff --git a/backend/tests/api/test_admin.py b/backend/tests/api/test_admin.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..c8d6498
--- /dev/null
+++ b/backend/tests/api/test_admin.py
@@ -0,0 +1,169 @@
+"""Workspace-admin endpoint tests against a real Postgres via TestClient.
+
+Auth runs in dev-bypass mode (conftest), so the caller is the fixed dev user.
+`WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` is toggled per test to flip that user between admin and
+non-admin. The key property under test: an admin sees suites/users they neither
+own nor are shared on — the /admin endpoints bypass the owned-or-shared scoping
+`list_suites` applies. Skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL.
+"""
+
+import uuid
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
+
+from backend.app.core.auth import DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL
+from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
+from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Share, Suite, User
+from backend.app.db.session import get_db
+from backend.app.main import app
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
+    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
+    try:
+        yield TestClient(app)
+    finally:
+        app.dependency_overrides.clear()
+
+
+def _grant_admin(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, *emails: str) -> None:
+    """Make the given emails (default: the dev-bypass caller) workspace admins."""
+    monkeypatch.setenv("WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS", ",".join(emails or (DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,)))
+    get_settings.cache_clear()
+
+
+def _user(db_session: Any, email: str, display_name: str | None = None) -> User:
+    u = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=email, display_name=display_name)
+    db_session.add(u)
+    db_session.flush()
+    return u
+
+
+def _connection(db_session: Any, owner: User) -> Connection:
+    conn = Connection(
+        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
+        type="snowflake",
+        env="dev",
+        config={"account": "ab12345.eu-west-1"},
+        secret_ref="kv-sf",
+        created_by=owner.id,
+    )
+    db_session.add(conn)
+    db_session.flush()
+    return conn
+
+
+def _suite(db_session: Any, owner: User, conn: Connection, name: str) -> Suite:
+    suite = Suite(name=name, connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id)
+    db_session.add(suite)
+    db_session.flush()
+    return suite
+
+
+# ── authz gate ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+def test_non_admin_gets_403(client: TestClient) -> None:
+    # No WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS configured → the caller is not an admin.
+    get_settings.cache_clear()
+    for path in ("/api/v1/admin/suites", "/api/v1/admin/users", "/api/v1/admin/access"):
+        resp = client.get(path)
+        assert resp.status_code == 403, path
+
+
+def test_admin_email_match_is_case_insensitive(
+    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    _grant_admin(monkeypatch, DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL.upper())
+    assert client.get("/api/v1/admin/suites").status_code == 200
+
+
+# ── all suites ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+def test_admin_lists_suites_it_does_not_own(
+    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    # A suite owned by someone else, with two checks and one share — the admin
+    # neither owns nor is shared on it, yet must see it (scoping is bypassed).
+    other = _user(db_session, "owner@x.io", "Olive Owner")
+    conn = _connection(db_session, other)
+    suite = _suite(db_session, other, conn, "Finance DQ")
+    db_session.add_all(
+        [
+            Check(
+                suite_id=suite.id,
+                name="c1",
+                expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
+                config={"column": "id"},
+            ),
+            Check(
+                suite_id=suite.id,
+                name="c2",
+                expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
+                config={"column": "amt"},
+            ),
+        ]
+    )
+    viewer = _user(db_session, "viewer@x.io")
+    db_session.add(Share(suite_id=suite.id, user_id=viewer.id, permission="view"))
+    db_session.commit()
+
+    _grant_admin(monkeypatch)
+    resp = client.get("/api/v1/admin/suites")
+    assert resp.status_code == 200
+    [row] = [r for r in resp.json() if r["id"] == str(suite.id)]
+    assert row["name"] == "Finance DQ"
+    assert row["owner_email"] == "owner@x.io"
+    assert row["owner_name"] == "Olive Owner"
+    assert row["connection_type"] == "snowflake"
+    assert row["env"] == "dev"
+    assert row["check_count"] == 2
+    assert row["share_count"] == 1
+
+
+# ── all users ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+def test_admin_lists_users_with_counts(
+    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    owner = _user(db_session, "alice@x.io", "Alice")
+    conn = _connection(db_session, owner)
+    _suite(db_session, owner, conn, "S1")
+    _suite(db_session, owner, conn, "S2")
+    bob = _user(db_session, "bob@x.io")
+    s3 = _suite(db_session, owner, conn, "S3")
+    db_session.add(Share(suite_id=s3.id, user_id=bob.id, permission="edit"))
+    db_session.commit()
+
+    _grant_admin(monkeypatch)
+    rows = {r["email"]: r for r in client.get("/api/v1/admin/users").json()}
+    assert rows["alice@x.io"]["owned_suite_count"] == 3
+    assert rows["alice@x.io"]["shared_suite_count"] == 0
+    assert rows["bob@x.io"]["owned_suite_count"] == 0
+    assert rows["bob@x.io"]["shared_suite_count"] == 1
+
+
+# ── access overview ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+def test_admin_access_overview_lists_owner_and_shares(
+    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    owner = _user(db_session, "owner@x.io")
+    conn = _connection(db_session, owner)
+    suite = _suite(db_session, owner, conn, "Shared Suite")
+    editor = _user(db_session, "editor@x.io")
+    db_session.add(Share(suite_id=suite.id, user_id=editor.id, permission="edit"))
+    db_session.commit()
+
+    _grant_admin(monkeypatch)
+    rows = [r for r in client.get("/api/v1/admin/access").json() if r["suite_id"] == str(suite.id)]
+    grants = {(r["user_email"], r["permission"]) for r in rows}
+    assert ("owner@x.io", "owner") in grants
+    assert ("editor@x.io", "edit") in grants

+"""/me endpoint tests — focus on the `is_workspace_admin` flag the Admin nav
+gates on. Auth is dev-bypass (conftest); WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS toggles whether
+the caller is an admin. Skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
+
+from backend.app.core.auth import DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL
+from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
+from backend.app.db.session import get_db
+from backend.app.main import app
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
+    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
+    try:
+        yield TestClient(app)
+    finally:
+        app.dependency_overrides.clear()
+
+
+def test_me_flags_non_admin_by_default(client: TestClient) -> None:
+    get_settings.cache_clear()
+    body = client.get("/api/v1/me").json()
+    assert body["email"] == DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL
+    assert body["is_workspace_admin"] is False
+
+
+def test_me_flags_admin_when_allowlisted(
+    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setenv("WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS", f"someone@else.io,{DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL}")
+    get_settings.cache_clear()
+    body = client.get("/api/v1/me").json()
+    assert body["is_workspace_admin"] is True

6	  | { status: 'ok'; data: T }
7	  | { status: 'error'; error: string };
8	
9	/**
10	 * Fetch on mount (and on `reload()`), with a cancelled-guard so a late
11	 * resolution after unmount doesn't set state, and rejection normalised to a
12	 * string `error`. Shared by the data pages (Home, Connections, …) so the
13	 * cancelled-effect dance lives in one place rather than being re-derived per page.
14	 *
15	 * `reload` re-runs the fetcher (e.g. after a mutation) while keeping the current
16	 * data visible until the refetch resolves — no flash back to the loading state.
17	 */
18	export function useAsyncData<T>(fetcher: () => Promise<T>): {
19	  state: AsyncState<T>;
20	  reload: () => void;
21	} {
22	  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T>>({ status: 'loading' });
23	  const [nonce, setNonce] = useState(0);
24	
25	  useEffect(() => {
26	    let cancelled = false;
27	    fetcher()
28	      .then((data) => {
29	        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });
30	      })
31	      .catch((err: unknown) => {
32	        if (!cancelled) {
33	          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
34	        }
35	      });
36	    return () => {
37	      cancelled = true;
38	    };
39	    // Re-run on mount and whenever `reload` bumps the nonce; the fetcher identity
40	    // is intentionally not a dependency.
41	    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
42	  }, [nonce]);
43	
44	  const reload = useCallback(() => setNonce((n) => n + 1), []);
45	  return { state, reload };
46	}
47

1	import axios, { type AxiosError, type InternalAxiosRequestConfig } from 'axios';
2	
3	import { authConfig, authMode } from '../auth/config';
4	import { getMsalInstance } from '../auth/msalInstance';
5	
6	/**
7	 * Shared axios instance for DataQ API calls.
8	 *
9	 * baseURL is relative (/api/v1); vite dev proxy forwards to the FastAPI
10	 * backend on :8000, and production same-origin deploy needs no CORS.
11	 *
12	 * Request interceptor attaches an Azure AD bearer token in real auth mode.
13	 * In dev_bypass / unconfigured modes the interceptor is a no-op (backend
14	 * dev-bypass resolves the user without a token).
15	 *
16	 * Response interceptor surfaces the DataQ error envelope's human message
17	 * (`{ error: { code, message, detail } }`) as `error.message`, so callers'
18	 * `err.message` shows the actionable backend reason instead of axios's generic
19	 * "Request failed with status code 4xx".
20	 */
21	export const api = axios.create({
22	  baseURL: '/api/v1',
23	});
24	
25	api.interceptors.request.use(attachBearerToken);
26	
27	api.interceptors.response.use(
28	  (response) => response,
29	  (error: AxiosError<{ error?: { message?: string } }>) => {
30	    const apiMessage = error.response?.data?.error?.message;
31	    if (apiMessage) error.message = apiMessage;
32	    return Promise.reject(error);
33	  },
34	);
35	
36	async function attachBearerToken(
37	  config: InternalAxiosRequestConfig,
38	): Promise<InternalAxiosRequestConfig> {
39	  if (authMode !== 'real') return config;
40	  const instance = getMsalInstance();
41	  if (!instance) return config;
42	  const account = instance.getAllAccounts()[0];
43	  if (!account || !authConfig.apiScopeUri) return config;
44	
45	  const result = await instance.acquireTokenSilent({
46	    account,
47	    scopes: [authConfig.apiScopeUri],
48	  });
49	  config.headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${result.accessToken}`);
50	  return config;
51	}
52

1	import { useMsal } from '@azure/msal-react';
2	import { useMemo, type ReactNode } from 'react';
3	
4	import { authMode, DEV_USER } from './config';
5	import { CurrentUserContext, type CurrentUser } from './currentUserContext';
6	
7	/**
8	 * Provides the current user to the tree.
9	 *
10	 * - dev_bypass: static dev user.
11	 * - unconfigured: null (AuthGate shows the banner).
12	 * - real: subscribes to MSAL accounts via useMsal().
13	 */
14	export function CurrentUserProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
15	  if (authMode === 'dev_bypass') {
16	    return <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={DEV_USER}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>;
17	  }
18	  if (authMode === 'real') {
19	    return <RealCurrentUserProvider>{children}</RealCurrentUserProvider>;
20	  }
21	  return <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={null}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>;
22	}
23	
24	function RealCurrentUserProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
25	  const { accounts } = useMsal();
26	  const value = useMemo<CurrentUser | null>(() => {
27	    const account = accounts[0];
28	    if (!account) return null;
29	    return {
30	      name: account.name ?? '(unknown)',
31	      username: account.username,
32	      homeAccountId: account.homeAccountId,
33	      isDev: false,
34	    };
35	  }, [accounts]);
36	  return <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>;
37	}

20	// MSAL lifecycle (issue #62):

22	//   2. .handleRedirectPromise() must resolve before React renders so the
23	//      first paint reflects post-login state.
24	//   3. Errors surface to the console + a static page — fail loud during dev.
25	async function bootstrap() {
26	  const instance = getMsalInstance();
27	  if (instance) {
28	    await instance.initialize();
29	    await instance.handleRedirectPromise();
30	  }
31	  createRoot(rootEl).render(
32	    <StrictMode>
33	      <ConfigProvider theme={appTheme}>
34	        <AntApp>
35	          <ErrorBoundary>
36	            <MsalProvider>
37	              <CurrentUserProvider>
38	                <BrowserRouter>
39	                  <App />
40	                </BrowserRouter>
41	              </CurrentUserProvider>
42	            </MsalProvider>
43	          </ErrorBoundary>
44	        </AntApp>
45	      </ConfigProvider>
46	    </StrictMode>,
47	  );
48	}
49	
50	bootstrap().catch((err) => {

 * Connections API — the six configurable connection types (CLAUDE.md §4).

 * still `connections` rows and managed through the same CRUD surface.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/auth/MeProvider.tsx",
  "content": "import { useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';\n\nimport { fetchMe, type MeResponse } from '../api/me';\nimport type { AsyncState } from '../hooks/useAsyncData';\nimport { MeContext } from './meContext';\nimport { useCurrentUser } from './useCurrentUser';\n\n/**\n * Fetches `/me` once the user is authenticated and shares it via `MeContext`.\n *\n * The fetch is gated on `useCurrentUser()` (not done on bare mount) so that in\n * real-auth mode we wait until MSAL has an account — otherwise the request would\n * race ahead of the bearer token and 401. In dev-bypass the user is present\n * immediately. Re-runs if the signed-in identity changes.\n */\nexport function MeProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  const user = useCurrentUser();\n  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<MeResponse>>({ status: 'loading' });\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!user) return;\n    let cancelled = false;\n    setState({ status: 'loading' });\n    fetchMe()\n      .then((data) => {\n        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });\n      })\n      .catch((err: unknown) => {\n        if (!cancelled) {\n          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });\n        }\n      });\n    return () => {\n      cancelled = true;\n    };\n    // Keyed on the stable account id so a token refresh (new `user` object, same\n    // identity) doesn't refetch; a real identity change does.\n  }, [user?.homeAccountId, user]);\n\n  return <MeContext.Provider value={state}>{children}</MeContext.Provider>;\n}\n"
}

}

A non-admin who deep-links here sees the Forbidden page.\n */\nexport function Admin() {\n  const me = useMe();\n\n  if (me.status === 'loading') {\n    return <Spin size=\"large\" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;\n  }\n  if (me.status === 'error') {\n    return (\n      <Alert type=\"error\" showIcon message=\"Couldn't verify your access\" description={me.error} />\n    );\n  }\n  if (!me.data.is_workspace_admin) {\n    return <Forbidden message=\"The admin overview is restricted to workspace admins.\" />;\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical gap={24}>\n      <Typography.Title level={3} style={{ margin: 0 }}>\n        Admin\n      </Typography.Title>\n      <Tabs\n        defaultActiveKey=\"suites\"\n        items={[\n          { key: 'suites', label: 'Suites', children: <SuitesTab /> },\n          { key: 'users', label: 'Users', children: <UsersTab /> },\n          { key: 'access', label: 'Access', children: <AccessTab /> },\n        ]}\n      />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\n/** Shared load/error/table boilerplate for the three admin overviews. */\nfunction AdminTable<T extends object>({\n  fetcher,\n  columns,\n  rowKey,\n  loadingTip,\n  errorMessage,\n}: {\n  fetcher: () => Promise<T[]>;\n  columns: ColumnsType<T>;\n  rowKey: (row: T) => string;\n  loadingTip: string;\n  errorMessage: string;\n}) {\n  const { state } = useAsyncData(fetcher);\n  if (state.status === 'loading') return <Spin tip={loadingTip} size=\"large\" />;\n  if (state.status === 'error') {\n    return <Alert type=\"error\" showIcon message={errorMessage} description={state.error} />;\n  }\n  return (\n    <Table\n      dataSource={state.data}\n      columns={columns}\n      rowKey={rowKey}\n      size=\"small\"\n      pagination={{ pageSize: 20, hideOnSinglePage: true }}\n    />\n  );\n}\n\n/** Name over email, falling back to the email alone when no display name. */\nfunction Identity({ name, email }: { name: string | null; email: string }) {\n  if (!name) return <Typography.Text>{email}</Typography.Text>;\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical>\n      <Typography.Text>{name}</Typography.Text>\n      <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\" style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>\n        {email}\n      </Typography.Text>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\nconst PERMISSION_COLORS: Record<string, string> = {\n  owner: 'gold',\n  admin: 'volcano',\n  edit: 'blue',\n  view: 'default',\n};\n\nfunction SuitesTab() {\n  const columns: ColumnsType<AdminSuite> = [\n    { title: 'Suite', dataIndex: 'name' },\n    {\n      title: 'Owner',\n      key: 'owner',\n      render: (_, s) => <Identity name={s.owner_name} email={s.owner_email} />,\n    },\n    {\n      title: 'Datasource',\n      key: 'datasource',\n      render: (_, s) => (\n        <Flex align=\"center\" gap={6}>\n          <Typography.Text>{s.connection_name}</Typography.Text>\n          <Tag>{s.connection_type}</Tag>\n        </Flex>\n      ),\n    },\n    { title: 'Env', dataIndex: 'env', render: (env: string) => <Tag>{env}</Tag> },\n    { title: 'Checks', dataIndex: 'check_count', align: 'right' },\n    { title: 'Shared with', dataIndex: 'share_count', align: 'right' },\n    { title: 'Created', dataIndex: 'created_at', render: (v: string) => formatTimestamp(v) },\n  ];\n  return (\n    <AdminTable\n      fetcher={listAdminSuites}\n      columns={columns}\n      rowKey={(s) => s.id}\n      loadingTip=\"Loading suites…\"\n      errorMessage=\"Failed to load suites\"\n    />\n  );\n}\n\nfunction UsersTab() {\n  const columns: ColumnsType<AdminUser> = [\n    {\n      title: 'User',\n      key: 'user',\n      render: (_, u) => <Identity name={u.display_name} email={u.email} />,\n    },\n    { title: 'Suites owned', dataIndex: 'owned_suite_count', align: 'right' },\n    { title: 'Shared with them', dataIndex: 'shared_suite_count', align: 'right' },\n    { title: 'Last seen', dataIndex: 'last_seen_at', render: (v: string | null) => formatTimestamp(v) },\n  ];\n  return (\n    <AdminTable\n      fetcher={listAdminUsers}\n      columns={columns}\n      rowKey={(u) => u.id}\n      loadingTip=\"Loading users…\"\n      errorMessage=\"Failed to load users\"\n    />\n  );\n}\n\nfunction AccessTab() {\n  const columns: ColumnsType<AdminAccess> = [\n    { title: 'Suite', dataIndex: 'suite_name' },\n    {\n      title: 'User',\n      key: 'user',\n      render: (_, a) => <Identity name={a.user_name} email={a.user_email} />,\n    },\n    {\n      title: 'Permission',\n      dataIndex: 'permission',\n      render: (p: string) => <Tag color={PERMISSION_COLORS[p] ?? > AGENT

ESLint caught the synchronous `setState` in the effect body (same `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` rule as before). The `loading` reset is unnecessary — the initial context value is already `loading`, and keeping stale data visible during an identity-change refetch matches `useAsyncData`'s own "no flash to loading" philosophy. Removing it:

**Summary for the caller:** The frontend Admin/Me changes are clean and convention-compliant — no real cleanup is required. Key conclusions across the four angles:

- **Reuse:** `MeProvider/useMe` is *justified* — it de-duplicates the `/me` fetch that `Home.tsx` (Profile) already made, now serving both the nav gate and Profile from one fetch. `Forbidden.tsx` and `PERMISSION_COLORS` are genuinely new (no existing 403 component / permission-color map to reuse). The only soft point: `AdminTable` is a nicely-extracted load/error/Table generic, but `Results.tsx` still hand-rolls the same boilerplate inline 3+ times and wasn't migrated — leaving the pattern in two shapes (an opportunity, not a defect in the new code).
- **Simplification:** `AdminTable` is appropriately generic (3 in-file uses), not over-engineered. `Identity` is local and correctly scoped (not duplicated as a function).
- **Efficiency:** The `/me`-on-load concern does **not** hold — it's net neutral-to-positive (replaces a per-page fetch). No re-render storm (`user` is memoized; context value changes only on identity change / resolve).
- **Conventions (§11):** **No violation.** The admin gate reads the server-provided `is_workspace_admin` flag, never MSAL/Entra claims client-side (grep-confirmed). Route is always registered with a `Forbidden` fallback; nav gate is convenience only.

Net: zero blocking findings. The only actionable nit is the missed migration of `Results.tsx` onto `AdminTable` (consistency, not correctness), plus a slightly over-promising docstring in `Forbidden.tsx` (says it renders on endpoint 403s, but it's only wired to the client-side gate).

Combined review done. The frontend is clean except **one genuine latent bug** worth fixing:

**Will fix (1 real + 1 doc):**
- **MeProvider stale-state on sign-out** ([MeProvider.tsx](frontend/src/auth/MeProvider.tsx)) — when `user → null` (logout / in-app token expiry), the effect early-returns and never clears the last `/me`, so a stale `is_workspace_admin: true` (and the Admin nav) could linger. Masked today only because logout does a full-page `logoutRedirect`, but it's latent. Fix with a render-phase reset on identity change (the lint-safe idiom) — which also makes an identity *switch* correctly drop the previous user's data instead of flashing it.
- **Forbidden docstring** over-promises ("when an endpoint returns 403") vs the actual client-gate wiring — reword to match.

**Won't fix (confirmed non-issues):** `AdminTable`-vs-`Results.tsx` is a migrate-existing-code opportunity (out of scope, regression risk); `PERMISSION_COLORS`/`Identity`/`MeProvider` efficiency all confirmed appropriate; §11 conventions compliant (gate reads the server flag, never MSAL claims). 1	import { useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
2	
3	import { fetchMe, type MeResponse } from '../api/me';
4	import type { AsyncState } from '../hooks/useAsyncData';
5	import { MeContext } from './meContext';
6	import { useCurrentUser } from './useCurrentUser';
7	
8	/**
9	 * Fetches `/me` once the user is authenticated and shares it via `MeContext`.
10	 *
11	 * The fetch is gated on `useCurrentUser()` (not done on bare mount) so that in
12	 * real-auth mode we wait until MSAL has an account — otherwise the request would
13	 * race ahead of the bearer token and 401. In dev-bypass the user is present
14	 * immediately. Re-runs if the signed-in identity changes.
15	 */
16	export function MeProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
17	  const user = useCurrentUser();
18	  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<MeResponse>>({ status: 'loading' });
19	
20	  useEffect(() => {
21	    if (!user) return;
22	    let cancelled = false;
23	    // No synchronous setState('loading') here — the initial value is already
24	    // loading, and on an identity change we keep the prior data visible until the
25	    // refetch resolves (same "no flash to loading" behaviour as useAsyncData).
26	    fetchMe()
27	      .then((data) => {
28	        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });
29	      })
30	      .catch((err: unknown) => {
31	        if (!cancelled) {
32	          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
33	        }
34	      });
35	    return () => {
36	      cancelled = true;
37	    };
38	    // `user` is memoized by CurrentUserProvider (stable unless the signed-in
39	    // identity actually changes), so this refetches on real identity change only.
40	  }, [user]);
41	
42	  return <MeContext.Provider value={state}>{children}</MeContext.Provider>;
43	}
44

> AGENT

Here's the answer on the env file, with the exact hook that blocked it.

## Why `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` isn't in `.env.app.example`

A **PreToolUse hook** in [.claude/settings.json:43](.claude/settings.json#L43) blocked the edit. Its logic:

- **Block** any path matching `(^|/)\.env($|\.)` — i.e. `.env` at the start or after a `/`, followed by end-of-string **or a dot**.
- **Except** paths matching `\.env\.example$` — ending in *exactly* `.env.example`.

For `.env.app.example`:
- It **matches the block** (`.env.` → `.env` followed by `.`).
- It **misses the exception** — it ends in `.env.app.example`, not `.env.example`.

So the hook treats it like a real secret-bearing `.env` and refuses the write — even though `.env.app.example` is a **git-tracked, secret-free example template** (confirmed: it's tracked, and it's where every *other* app var like `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS` is documented). It's a **false positive**: the allow-pattern only whitelists the literal `*.env.example` suffix and never anticipated this repo's `.env.<role>.example` split (introduced in #209).

The variable is fully documented in [config.py](backend/app/core/config.py) instead, so nothing is lost functionally — but the example file is now inconsistent (it omits one real var).

**The fix** is a one-character-class change to the hook's exception regex so it allows the `.example` suffix generally:

```
\.env\.example$   →   \.env(\.[^/]+)?\.example$
```

That keeps real `.env` / `.env.app` files blocked while allowing `.env.example` **and** `.env.app.example`. I'd do this via the `update-config` skill (it owns `settings.json`). Want me to apply it and then add the `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` line to the example file?

## Situation
- **The blocker:** required check `Frontend — pnpm audit` is red on a **newly-published** high-severity `undici` advisory in a transitive **dev-only** dep (`vitest`→`jsdom`→`undici@7.25.0`). - **The fix is routine and has precedent:** [frontend/package.json:63](frontend/package.json#L63) already carries exactly this kind of transitive-CVE override (`dompurify`, `js-yaml`). Adding `"undici": ">=7.28.0"` + `pnpm install` clears it. (CI runs pnpm 9.15.4, which *does* read `pnpm.overrides` from package.json — the "field ignored" warning is only from my newer local pnpm, not CI.)

## Why I stopped
Bundling a dependency-security fix into the admin feature PR violates the working agreement against batching unrelated changes — and "defects → GitHub issue, never silent fixes." So the clean path is a **separate small `fix(deps)` PR** (with its own issue), merged first, then #289 rebases green.

## Proposed plan
1. File an issue + open a tiny `fix(deps): bump undici ≥7.28.0 (GHSA-vmh5-mc38-953g)` PR (override + lockfile only).
2. Merge it once *its* CI is green.
3. Rebase #289 → its pnpm-audit goes green → **merge #289**.
